categories.name: Amazon's AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional

questions.content: A company has millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The objects are in the S3 Standard storage class. All the S3 objects are accessed frequently. The number of users and applications that access the objects is increasing rapidly. The objects are encrypted with server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). A solutions architect reviews the company's monthly AWS invoice and notices that AWS KMS costs are increasing because of the high number of requests from Amazon S3. The solutions architect needs to optimize costs with minimal changes to the application. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create a new S3 bucket that has server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C) as the encryption typCopy the existing objects to the new S3 bucket. Specify SSE-C.
answers.explanation: SSE-C requires the customer to manage keys and specify keys with each request, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create a new S3 bucket that has server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) as the encryption typUse S3 Batch Operations to copy the existing objects to the new S3 bucket. Specify SSE-S3.
answers.explanation: Using server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3) eliminates the use of AWS KMS, reducing KMS request costs. S3 Batch Operations allow copying existing objects to a new bucket with minimal operational overhead. SSE-S3 provides encryption that is managed by Amazon S3 without additional cost or operational complexity. Switching encryption type to SSE-S3 requires minimal changes to the application since S3 handles encryption transparently.

answers.content: Use AWS CloudHSM to store the encryption keys. Create a new S3 bucket. Use S3 Batch Operations to copy the existing objects to the new S3 bucket. Encrypt the objects by using the keys from CloudHSM.
answers.explanation: Using AWS CloudHSM increases complexity and operational overhead compared to managed services.

answers.content: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class for the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Intelligent-Tiering archive configuration to transition objects that are not accessed for 90 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: Changing storage classes to Intelligent-Tiering and Glacier Deep Archive addresses cost related to storage, not KMS requests and encryption cost.

questions.content: A company is creating a centralized logging service running on Amazon EC2 that will receive and analyze logs from hundreds of AWS accounts. AWS PrivateLink is being used to provide connectivity between the client services and the logging servicIn each AWS account with a client, an interface endpoint has been created for the logging service and is availablThe logging service running on EC2 instances with a Network Load Balancer (NLB) are deployed in different subnets. The clients are unable to submit logs using the VPC endpoint. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Check that the NACL is attached to the logging service subnet to allow communications to and from the NLB subnets. Check that the NACL is attached to the NLB subnet to allow communications to and from the logging service subnets running on EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: NLB subnet ↔ EC2 subnet are different → NACLs (stateless) must explicitly allow traffic in both directions between these subnets

answers.content: Check that the NACL is attached to the logging service subnets to allow communications to and from the interface endpoint subnets. Check that the NACL is attached to the interface endpoint subnet to allow communications to and from the logging service subnets running on EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Interface endpoints are in client accounts; they don't directly face EC2 subnets — PrivateLink abstracts this boundary

answers.content: Check the security group for the logging service running on the EC2 instances to ensure it allows ingress from the NLB subnets.
answers.explanation: EC2 Security Group must allow ingress from NLB subnet CIDR, since traffic arrives at EC2 sourced from NLB node IPs

answers.content: Check the security group for the logging service running on EC2 instances to ensure it allows ingress from the clients.
answers.explanation: EC2 never sees direct client IPs via NLB (unless Proxy Protocol is enabled), and clients are in different accounts anyway

answers.content: Check the security group for the NLB to ensure it allows ingress from the interface endpoint subnets.
answers.explanation: NLBs do NOT have Security Groups — this is a fundamental NLB characteristic

questions.content: A company is creating a REST API to share information with six of its partners based in the United States. The company has created an Amazon API Gateway Regional endpoint. Each of the six partners will access the API once per day to post daily sales figures. After initial deployment, the company observes 1,000 requests per second originating from 500 different IP addresses around the world. The company believes this traffic is originating from a botnet and wants to secure its API while minimizing cost. Which approach should the company take to secure its API?

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the API as the origin. Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to block clients that submit more than five requests per day. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Configure CloudFront with an origin access identity (OAI) and associate it with the distribution. Configure API Gateway to ensure only the OAI can run the POST method.
answers.explanation: Configuring CloudFront origin access identity (OAI) with API Gateway is not applicable; OAI is used with S3 origins, not API Gateway.

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the API as the origin. Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to block clients that submit more than five requests per day. Associate the web ACL with the CloudFront distribution. Add a custom header to the CloudFront distribution populated with an API key. Configure the API to require an API key on the POST method.
answers.explanation: Adding a custom header with an API key via CloudFront adds complexity and cost without better security compared to direct API Gateway protection.

answers.content: Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to allow access to the IP addresses used by the six partners. Associate the web ACL with the API. Create a resource policy with a request limit and associate it with the API. Configure the API to require an API key on the POST method.
answers.explanation: Resource policies do not support request limits; usage plans provide proper request throttling controls and are better integrated with API keys.

answers.content: Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rule to allow access to the IP addresses used by the six partners. Associate the web ACL with the API. Create a usage plan with a request limit and associate it with the API. Create an API key and add it to the usage plan.
answers.explanation: Using AWS WAF to allow access only from the six partners' IP addresses restricts traffic to known clients, effectively blocking botnet traffic from unknown IPs. Associating the WAF web ACL directly with the API Gateway regional endpoint is simpler and more cost-effective than introducing CloudFront. Creating a usage plan with a request limit enforces throttling at the API Gateway level to limit partner usage and prevent abusUsing API keys tied to the usage plan authenticates known partners without requiring distribution or complex configuration. This approach balances security best practices (IP whitelisting, throttling, key authentication) with minimizing cost by avoiding CloudFront overhead.

questions.content: A company has five development teams that have each created five AWS accounts to develop and host applications. To track spending, the development teams log in to each account every month, record the current cost from the AWS Billing and Cost Management console, and provide the information to the company's finance team. The company has strict compliance requirements and needs to ensure that resources are created only in AWS Regions in the United States. However, some resources have been created in other Regions. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that gives the finance team the ability to track and consolidate expenditures for all the accounts. The solution also must ensure that the company can create resources only in Regions in the United States. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a new account to serve as a management account. Create an Amazon S3 bucket for the finance team. Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create monthly reports and to store the data in the finance team's S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: CUR + S3 is overly complex for this use case; requires configuring reports, buckets, and querying — Cost Explorer (E) is simpler and already built-in

answers.content: Create a new account to serve as a management account. Deploy an organization in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Invite all the existing accounts to the organization. Ensure that each account accepts the invitation.
answers.explanation: rerequisite for everything else — enables both Consolidated Billing AND Service Control Policies (SCPs).All features mode (not just billing features) is required for SCPs to work. One-time setup all 25 accounts join once

answers.content: Create an OU that includes all the development teams. Create an SCP that allows the creation of resources only in Regions that are in the United States. Apply the SCP to the OU.
answers.explanation: Allow-based SCP (whitelist) is harder to craft correctly; could inadvertently block AWS global services (IAM, CloudFront, Route53) that are region-agnostic

answers.content: Create an OU that includes all the development teams. Create an SCP that denies the creation of resources in Regions that are outside the United States. Apply the SCP to the OU.
answers.explanation: AWS best practice = deny what you don't want (blacklist), not whitelist.Applied at the OU level → automatically enforces policy across all 25 accounts without touching each account individually.Deny-based SCPs are simpler, more targeted, and harder to accidentally misconfigure

answers.content: Create an IAM role in the management account. Attach a policy that includes permissions to view the Billing and Cost Management consolAllow the finance team users to assume the rolUse AWS Cost Explorer and the Billing and Cost Management console to analyze cost.
answers.explanation: With Organizations, the management account's Cost Explorer shows ALL member accounts in one view.Finance team assumes one role, one account instead of 25 separate logins.No manual monthly data collection needed

answers.content: Create an IAM role in each AWS account. Attach a policy that includes permissions to view the Billing and Cost Management console. Allow the finance team users to assume the role.
answers.explanation: Requires creating/managing 25 IAM roles across 25 accounts — not operationally efficient; this is essentially what they're already doing manually

questions.content: A company has a data lake in Amazon S3 that needs to be accessed by hundreds of applications across many AWS accounts. The company's information security policy states that the S3 bucket must not be accessed over the public internet and that each application should have the minimum permissions necessary to function. To meet these requirements, a solutions architect plans to use an S3 access point that is restricted to specific VPCs for each application. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to implement this solution? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an S3 access point for each application in the AWS account that owns the S3 bucket. Configure each access point to be accessible only from the application's VPC. Update the bucket policy to require access from an access point.
answers.explanation: Access points created in the BUCKET OWNER's account.S3 Access Points must be in the same account as the bucket — they cannot be created in other accounts.Each access point has its own policy → enforces least privilege per application.VPC restriction on access point ensures traffic only accepted from that VPC.aws:sourceVpce condition in bucket policy forces all access through an access point

answers.content: Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in each application's VPC. Configure the endpoint policy to allow access to an S3 access point. Create a VPC gateway attachment for the S3 endpoint.
answers.explanation: Interface endpoints for S3 exist but are PrivateLink-based (costly, unnecessary). Also, VPC gateway attachment is invalid terminology for interface endpoints attachments are for IGWs/VGWs, not interface endpoints

answers.content: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in each application's VPConfigure the endpoint policy to allow access to an S3 access point. Specify the route table that is used to access the access point.
answers.explanation: Gateway Endpoint in each APPLICATION's VPC.Gateway endpoints keep S3 traffic entirely within the AWS network (no internet).Works via route table entries — traffic to S3 is routed through the endpoint automatically.Free of charge — no hourly cost unlike interface endpoints.Endpoint policy further restricts which access points can be reached

answers.content: Create an S3 access point for each application in each AWS account and attach the access points to the S3 bucket. Configure each access point to be accessible only from the application's VPC. Update the bucket policy to require access from an access point.
answers.explanation: Access points cannot be created in a different account from the bucket — this is architecturally impossible

answers.content: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the data lake's VPC. Attach an endpoint policy to allow access to the S3 bucket. Specify the route table that is used to access the bucket.
answers.explanation: Gateway endpoint placed in the data lake's VPC instead of the application's VPC —  the applications need the endpoint in their VPC to route traffic privately

questions.content: A company's solutions architect is analyzing costs of a multi-application environment. The environment is deployed across multiple Availability Zones in a single AWS Region. After a recent acquisition, the company manages two organizations in AWS Organizations. The company has created multiple service provider applications as AWS PrivateLink-powered VPC endpoint services in one organization. The company has created multiple service consumer applications in the other organization. Data transfer charges are much higher than the company expected, and the solutions architect needs to reduce the costs. The solutions architect must recommend guidelines for developers to follow when they deploy services. These guidelines must minimize data transfer charges for the whole environment. Which guidelines meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use AWS Resource Access Manager to share the subnets that host the service provider applications with other accounts in the organization.
answers.explanation: RAM sharing of subnets does not inherently reduce data transfer costs and is not related directly to AWS PrivateLink data flow optimization.

answers.content: Place the service provider applications and the service consumer applications in AWS accounts in the same organization.
answers.explanation: RAM subnet sharing changes the architecture (shared VPC), doesn't directly address cross-AZ PrivateLink costs

answers.content: Turn off cross-zone load balancing for the Network Load Balancer in all service provider application deployments.
answers.explanation: Turn off cross-zone load balancing for the Network Load Balancer in all service provider application deployments.Inter-Availability Zone (AZ) data transfer is often a significant cost factor in AWS. When a Network Load Balancer (NLB) has cross-zone load balancing enabled, it routes traffic equally to targets across all enabled AZs. If a consumer connects to an NLB endpoint in one AZ, but the traffic is routed to a provider application in a different AZ, AWS charges for the cross-AZ data transfer. By turning off cross-zone load balancing, the NLB only sends traffic to targets within its own AZ. This allows the use of the zonal endpoint (Option D) to keep traffic within the same AZ, minimizing cross-AZ data transfer costs.

answers.content: Ensure that service consumer compute resources use the Availability Zone-specific endpoint service by using the endpoint's local DNS name.
answers.explanation: Interface endpoints expose two types of DNS names:Regional DNS:  vpce-xxx.s3.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com→ May resolve to endpoint ENI in a DIFFERENT AZ → cross-AZ charge.AZ-Specific:   vpce-xxx-us-east-1a.vpce.amazonaws.com→ Always resolves to endpoint ENI in YOUR AZ → no cross-AZ charge

answers.content: Create a Savings Plan that provides adequate coverage for the organization's planned inter-Availability Zone data transfer usage.
answers.explanation: Savings Plans cover compute costs (EC2, Lambda, Fargate) — they do not cover data transfer charges at all

questions.content: A company has an application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are part of an Auto Scaling group. The application has unpredictable workloads and frequently scales out and in. The company's development team wants to analyze application logs to find ways to improve the application's performancHowever, the logs are no longer available after instances scale in. Which solution will give the development team the ability to view the application logs after a scale-in event?

answers.content: Enable access logs for the ALB. Store the logs in an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: ALB access logs capture load balancer traffic but do not capture application logs from EC2 instances.

answers.content: Configure the EC2 instances to publish logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by using the unified CloudWatch agent.
answers.explanation: Publishing logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs ensures that logs are centralized and persist even after EC2 instances are terminated due to scale-in. CloudWatch Logs provides a managed, durable logging solution that is independent of the lifecycle of individual instances. This approach aligns with AWS best practices for log management and supports analyzing logs after instances no longer exist.

answers.content: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use a step scaling policy.
answers.explanation: Step scaling policies control instance scaling but do not address log persistence after scale-in.

answers.content: Instrument the application with AWS X-Ray tracing.
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray provides tracing for performance analysis but does not store full application logs for post-termination access.

questions.content: A company runs an application in an on-premises data center. The application gives users the ability to upload media files. The files persist in a file server. The web application has many users. The application server is overutilized, which causes data uploads to fail occasionally. The company frequently adds new storage to the file server. The company wants to resolve these challenges by migrating the application to AWS. Users from across the United States and Canada access the application. Only authenticated users should have the ability to access the application to upload files. The company will consider a solution that refactors the application, and the company needs to accelerate application development. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the application server to Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the requests. Modify the application to use Amazon S3 to persist the files. Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users.
answers.explanation: Requires managing and scaling EC2 instances, which increases operational overhead

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the application server to Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the requests. Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to give users the ability to sign in to the application. Modify the application to use Amazon S3 to persist the files.
answers.explanation: IAM Identity Center is not designed for application user authentication and would add complexity

answers.content: Create a static website for uploads of media files. Store the static assets in Amazon S3. Use AWS AppSync to create an API. Use AWS Lambda resolvers to upload the media files to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users.
answers.explanation: Using AppSync with Lambda adds complexity; not as streamlined as Amplify for accelerating development

answers.content: Use AWS Amplify to create a static website for uploads of media files. Use Amplify Hosting to serve the website through Amazon CloudFront. Use Amazon S3 to store the uploaded media files. Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users.
answers.explanation: AWS Amplify is a managed service that accelerates application development with low operational overhead Amplify Hosting uses Amazon CloudFront for content distribution, improving performance for users across the US and Canada Amazon Cognito provides secure user authentication, ensuring only authenticated users can upload files Using Amazon S3 for storage leverages managed, scalable object storage for media files This solution refactors the application to a modern, serverless architecture, minimizing operational management compared to managing EC2 instances

questions.content: A media storage application uploads user photos to Amazon S3 for processing by AWS Lambda functions. Application state is stored in Amazon DynamoDB tables. Users are reporting that some uploaded photos are not being processed properly. The application developers trace the logs and find that Lambda is experiencing photo processing issues when thousands of users upload photos simultaneously. The issues are the result of Lambda concurrency limits and the performance of DynamoDB when data is saved. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to increase the performance and reliability of the application? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Evaluate and adjust the RCUs for the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: RCUs = Read Capacity Units; the issue is with writes (saving data), not reads

answers.content: Evaluate and adjust the WCUs for the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: This solves Problem 2 (DynamoDB write performance):The issue is explicitly when data is saved = write operations.WCUs control write throughput capacity.Insufficient WCUs → DynamoDB throttles writes → ProvisionedThroughputExceededException.Increasing WCUs (or switching to on-demand mode) handles write bursts

answers.content: Add an Amazon ElastiCache layer to increase the performance of Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: ElastiCache is a read cache — helps with repeated reads; does nothing for write performance or Lambda concurrency

answers.content: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and reprocessing logic between Amazon S3 and the Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: Benefits:SQS absorbs the burst — messages queue up instead of all hitting Lambda simultaneously.Lambda processes at a sustainable concurrency rate.Reprocessing logic = failed messages go back to queue (or DLQ) for retry.Decouples ingestion from processing = improved reliability

answers.content: Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to provide lower latency to users.
answers.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration reduces upload latency for end users; doesn't affect Lambda concurrency or DynamoDB write performance

questions.content: A company manufactures smart vehicles. The company uses a custom application to collect vehicle data. The vehicles use the MQTT protocol to connect to the application. The company processes the data in 5-minute intervals. The company then copies vehicle telematics data to on-premises storagCustom applications analyze this data to detect anomalies. The number of vehicles that send data grows constantly. Newer vehicles generate high volumes of data. The on-premises storage solution is not able to scale for peak traffic, which results in data loss. The company must modernize the solution and migrate the solution to AWS to resolve the scaling challenges. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Use AWS IoT Greengrass to send the vehicle data to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Create an Apache Kafka application to store the data in Amazon S3. Use a pretrained model in Amazon SageMaker to detect anomalies.
answers.explanation: Using AWS IoT Greengrass and Amazon MSK introduces more operational overhead compared to fully managed services like AWS IoT Core and Kinesis Firehose; managing Kafka clusters adds complexity.

answers.content: Use AWS IoT Core to receive the vehicle data. Configure rules to route data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that stores the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application that reads from the delivery stream to detect anomalies.
answers.explanation: AWS IoT Core is a managed service designed to natively support the MQTT protocol, which is used by the vehicles to send data. Rules in AWS IoT Core can be configured to route data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, a fully managed service that reliably delivers streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3, addressing scaling challenges and ensuring reliable storagAmazon Kinesis Data Analytics can process the streaming data in real time to detect anomalies. This solution has the least operational overhead because it leverages fully managed, integrated AWS services purpose-built for IoT and streaming data processing, avoiding custom management of Kafka or self-managed message brokers.

answers.content: Use AWS IoT FleetWise to collect the vehicle data. Send the data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Use an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Use the built-in machine learning transforms in AWS Glue to detect anomalies.
answers.explanation: AWS IoT FleetWise is not mentioned as a service compatible with this architecture, and using AWS Glue for anomaly detection adds operational complexity and is less real-time than Kinesis Data Analytics.

answers.content: Use Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ to collect the vehicle data. Send the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Lookout for Metrics to detect anomalies.
answers.explanation: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ is a managed message broker but does not natively support MQTT, making it less suitable for the MQTT protocol used by vehicles; also, it introduces more operational overhead than AWS IoT Core.

questions.content: A company operates an on-premises software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution that ingests several files daily. The company provides multiple public SFTP endpoints to its customers to facilitate the file transfers. The customers add the SFTP endpoint IP addresses to their firewall allow list for outbound traffic. Changes to the SFTP endpoint IP addresses are not permitted. The company wants to migrate the SaaS solution to AWS and decrease the operational overhead of the file transfer servicWhich solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Register the customer-owned block of IP addresses in the company's AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address pool and assign them to an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint. Use AWS Transfer to store the files in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: AWS Transfer for SFTP is a managed AWS service designed specifically to provide SFTP endpoints integrated with Amazon S3 for file storage, minimizing operational overhead. Registering the customer-owned block of IP addresses in the AWS account and assigning Elastic IPs from that block to the AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint satisfies the requirement that SFTP endpoint IP addresses cannot change, maintaining the firewall allow list integrity for customers. Storing files in Amazon S3 aligns with AWS best practices for durable, scalable, and managed storagOptions B and C require managing EC2 instances and application load balancers or network load balancers, increasing operational complexity, and they do not guarantee use of the customer-owned IP address block for SFTP endpoints. Option D incorrectly suggests assigning Elastic IP addresses to an S3 VPC endpoint, which does not support SFTP or IP assignment, and enabling SFTP support directly on an S3 bucket is not possible.

answers.content: Add a subnet containing the customer-owned block of IP addresses to a VPC. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address pool and assign them to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Launch EC2 instances hosting FTP services in an Auto Scaling group behind the ALStore the files in attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.
answers.explanation: Managing FTP services on EC2 behind an ALB increases operational overhead and does not guarantee static customer-owned IP addresses as required.

answers.content: Register the customer-owned block of IP addresses with Amazon Route 53. Create alias records in Route 53 that point to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Launch EC2 instances hosting FTP services in an Auto Scaling group behind the NLB. Store the files in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Using an NLB with EC2 instances for FTP is more complex to manage and does not ensure SFTP support or static customer IP addresses for endpoints.

answers.content: Register the customer-owned block of IP addresses in the company's AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address pool and assign them to an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint. Enable SFTP support on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 VPC endpoints do not support Elastic IP assignment or native SFTP access, making this option invalid.

questions.content: A financial services company loaded millions of historical stock trades into an Amazon DynamoDB tablThe table uses on-demand capacity modOnce each day at midnight, a few million new records are loaded into the tablApplication read activity against the table happens in bursts throughout the day. and a limited set of keys are repeatedly looked up. The company needs to reduce costs associated with DynamoDB. Which strategy should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the DynamoDB table
answers.explanation: incorrect because although ElastiCache can reduce read load, it does not change the DynamoDB on-demand pricing model and requires custom cache management logic, so it does not directly optimize DynamoDB costs

answers.content: Deploy DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX). Configure DynamoDB auto scaling. Purchase Savings Plans in Cost Explorer.
answers.explanation: incorrect because DynamoDB is not covered by Savings Plans, making that cost recommendation invalid

answers.content: Use provisioned capacity modPurchase Savings Plans in Cost Explorer.
answers.explanation: incorrect because switching to provisioned capacity alone does not reduce repeated read consumption from hot keys, so without DAX the RCU cost remains unnecessarily high.

answers.content: Deploy DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX). Use provisioned capacity modConfigure DynamoDB auto scaling.
answers.explanation: correct because switching from on-demand to provisioned capacity with auto scaling reduces predictable steady-state costs, DAX significantly lowers read capacity consumption by caching frequently accessed hot keys, and Savings Plans do not apply to DynamoDB, making D the only option that effectively reduces overall DynamoDB costs.

questions.content: An entertainment company recently launched a new game. To ensure a good experience for players during the launch period, the company deployed a static quantity of 12 r6g.16xlarge (memory optimized) Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer. The company's operations team used the Amazon CloudWatch agent and a custom metric to include memory utilization in its monitoring strategy. Analysis of the CloudWatch metrics from the launch period showed consumption at about one quarter of the CPU and memory that the company expected. Initial demand for the game has subsided and has become more variablThe company decides to use an Auto Scaling group that monitors the CPU and memory consumption to dynamically scale the instance fleet. A solutions architect needs to configure the Auto Scaling group to meet demand in the most cost-effective way. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy c6g.4xlarge (compute optimized) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 3, a desired capacity of 3, and a maximum capacity of 12.
answers.explanation: Switching to compute optimized instances ignores the memory optimization indicated as necessary by prior usage patterns.

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy m6g.4xlarge (general purpose) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 3, a desired capacity of 3, and a maximum capacity of 12.
answers.explanation: Using general purpose instances may not provide the required memory capacity as efficiently as memory optimized instances.

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy r6g.4xlarge (memory optimized) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 3, a desired capacity of 3, and a maximum capacity of 12.
answers.explanation: The initial deployment used r6g.16xlarge (memory optimized) instances, and monitoring indicates underutilization of CPU and memory. To be cost-effective while matching resource needs, downsizing the instance size but keeping the same instance family (memory optimized r6g) is preferred. Configuring the Auto Scaling group with r6g.4xlarge instances allows scaling between 3 and 12 instances, providing flexibility to match variable demand with appropriate memory capacity per instancAWS best practices recommend target tracking scaling policies with monitoring on CPU and memory metrics to ensure dynamic scaling according to demand. Options that switch instance family to compute optimized (c6g) or general purpose (m6g) instances risk mismatching the memory requirements observed in monitoring.

answers.content: Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy r6g.8xlarge (memory optimized) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 2, a desired capacity of 2, and a maximum capacity of 6.
answers.explanation: Using larger r6g.8xlarge instances with a small maximum count reduces scaling granularity and flexibility, potentially leading to higher costs or capacity issues.

questions.content: A company uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster for applications in a single AWS Region. The company's database team must monitor all data activity on all the databases. Which solution will achieve this goal?

answers.content: Set up an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) task. Specify the Aurora DB cluster as the sourcSpecify Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose as the target. Use Kinesis Data Firehose to upload the data into an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for further analysis.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS CDC targets migration, not full activity monitoring; Kinesis Data Firehose to OpenSearch is not the recommended managed stream for Aurora database activity streams.

answers.content: Start a database activity stream on the Aurora DB cluster to capture the activity stream in Amazon EventBridgDefine an AWS Lambda function as a target for EventBridgProgram the Lambda function to decrypt the messages from EventBridge and to publish all database activity to Amazon S3 for further analysis.
answers.explanation: EventBridge is not a supported target for Aurora database activity streams currently, and the solution requires custom Lambda decryption, adding unnecessary complexity and security risk.

answers.content: Start a database activity stream on the Aurora DB cluster to push the activity stream to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to consume the Kinesis data stream and to deliver the data to Amazon S3 for further analysis.
answers.explanation: Starting a database activity stream on the Aurora DB cluster is the intended AWS managed method to capture database activities. Pushing the activity stream data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream and then using Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver the data securely to Amazon S3 aligns with managed services and best practices for scalable, secure data ingestion and storagThis approach avoids custom decryption coding or indirect event handling, providing a direct and managed solution for monitoring database activity. AWS DMS CDC tasks are designed primarily for data replication and migration, not comprehensive activity monitoring.

answers.content: Set up an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) task. Specify the Aurora DB cluster as the sourcSpecify Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose as the target. Use Kinesis Data Firehose to upload the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster. Run queries on the Amazon Redshift data to determine database activities on the Aurora database.
answers.explanation: Using AWS DMS CDC with Kinesis Data Firehose to Redshift is more complex and designed for migration/analytics rather than direct activity monitoring; adds unnecessary operational overhead.

questions.content: A company has a new application that needs to run on five Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The application requires high-throughput, low-latency network connections between all of the EC2 instances where the application will run. There is no requirement for the application to be fault tolerant. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Launch five new EC2 instances into a cluster placement group. Ensure that the EC2 instance type supports enhanced networking.
answers.explanation: Cluster placement groups provide high-throughput, low-latency network connections between tightly coupled EC2 instances in a single Availability ZonEnsuring the EC2 instance type supports enhanced networking improves network performance and reduces latency. The question states there is no requirement for fault tolerance, so cluster placement group is preferred over partition or spread for networking performancThe key facts do not mention Auto Scaling group benefits for this use case, and additional network interfaces do not guarantee high-throughput, low-latency connections.

answers.content: Launch five new EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group in the same Availability ZonAttach an extra elastic network interface to each EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling groups focus on fault tolerance and scaling, which is not required; an extra network interface does not inherently provide high-throughput, low-latency connections.

answers.content: Launch five new EC2 instances into a partition placement group. Ensure that the EC2 instance type supports enhanced networking.
answers.explanation: Partition placement groups are designed for fault tolerance and spreading instances across partitions, not for low-latency high throughput networking.

answers.content: Launch five new EC2 instances into a spread placement group. Attach an extra elastic network interface to each EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Spread placement groups are intended to reduce correlated failures by spreading instances, which does not optimize for low-latency network performance.

questions.content: An education company is running a web application used by college students around the world. The application runs in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A system administrator detects a weekly spike in the number of failed login attempts, which overwhelm the application's authentication servicAll the failed login attempts originate from about 500 different IP addresses that change each week. A solutions architect must prevent the failed login attempts from overwhelming the authentication servicWhich solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

answers.content: Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a security group and security group policy to deny access from the IP addresses.
answers.explanation: Security groups cannot easily block dynamic and frequently changing IP addresses; manual updates would be needed.

answers.content: Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule, and set the rule action to Block. Connect the web ACL to the ALB.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF supports rate-based rules that can automatically block IP addresses that exceed a defined request threshold, which is suitable for mitigating large numbers of failed login attempts from many different IPs. Using a rate-based rule is operationally efficient since it automatically adapts to changing IP addresses each week without manual updates. Attaching the web ACL to the ALB ensures filtering happens at the edge of the application traffic. AWS Firewall Manager is a management tool but does not eliminate the need for manual updates when IPs change weekly, and security groups do not support easily blocking dynamic IP sets or rate limiting.

answers.content: Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a security group and security group policy to allow access only to specific CIDR ranges.
answers.explanation: Allowing only specific CIDR ranges is too restrictive and not practical given users worldwide; also does not address dynamic IP blocking or rate limiting.

answers.content: Create an AWS WAF web ACL with an IP set match rule, and set the rule action to Block. Connect the web ACL to the ALB.
answers.explanation: Using an IP set match rule requires manual updates for changing IP addresses weekly, which is not operationally efficient compared to rate-based rules.

questions.content: A company needs to create and manage multiple AWS accounts for a number of departments from a central location. The security team requires read-only access to all accounts from its own AWS account. The company is using AWS Organizations and created an account for the security team. How should a solutions architect meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role to create a new IAM policy with read-only access in each member account. Establish a trust relationship between the IAM policy in each member account and the security account. Ask the security team to use the IAM policy to gain access.
answers.explanation: IAM policies cannot be assumed; assuming roles (not policies) enables cross-account access.

answers.content: Use the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role to create a new IAM role with read-only access in each member account. Establish a trust relationship between the IAM role in each member account and the security account. Ask the security team to use the IAM role to gain access.
answers.explanation: Creating new IAM roles in each member account is unnecessary; OrganizationAccountAccessRole already exists and is managed by AWS Organizations.

answers.content: Ask the security team to use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to call the AssumeRole API for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the management account from the security account. Use the generated temporary credentials to gain access.
answers.explanation: OrganizationAccountAccessRole exists in member accounts, not the management account; assuming it in the management account is invalid.

answers.content: Ask the security team to use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to call the AssumeRole API for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the member account from the security account. Use the generated temporary credentials to gain access.
answers.explanation: AWS Organizations automatically creates an IAM role named OrganizationAccountAccessRole in each member account for cross-account access. The security team needs read-only access to all member accounts, so they should AssumeRole into the OrganizationAccountAccessRole role in each member account to gain temporary credentials. Using AWS STS AssumeRole with OrganizationAccountAccessRole in member accounts aligns with security best practices, avoids managing custom policies or roles, and uses managed AWS features. This method respects isolation between accounts and grants the security team the required access from their own security account securely.

questions.content: A large company runs workloads in VPCs that are deployed across hundreds of AWS accounts. Each VPC consists of public subnets and private subnets that span across multiple Availability Zones. NAT gateways are deployed in the public subnets and allow outbound connectivity to the internet from the private subnets. A solutions architect is working on a hub-and-spoke design. All private subnets in the spoke VPCs must route traffic to the internet through an egress VPC. The solutions architect already has deployed a NAT gateway in an egress VPC in a central AWS account. Which set of additional steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create peering connections between the egress VPC and the spoke VPCs. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
answers.explanation: VPC peering does not scale well for hundreds of accounts and does not support transitive routing required in hub-and-spoke architectures.

answers.content: Create a transit gateway, and share it with the existing AWS accounts. Attach existing VPCs to the transit gateway. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
answers.explanation: Transit Gateway allows centralized connectivity and routing among multiple VPCs across multiple accounts, aligning with a hub-and-spoke design. Attaching existing VPCs to a shared Transit Gateway enables private subnets in spoke VPCs to route traffic through the egress VPC's NAT gateway. Configuring required routing through the Transit Gateway supports secure and managed internet access, leveraging managed AWS services as preferred. Though there is an extra Transit Gateway data processing charge, centralizing NAT gateway access with Transit Gateway is a recommended AWS architecture.

answers.content: Create a transit gateway in every account. Attach the NAT gateway to the transit gateways. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
answers.explanation: Creating a Transit Gateway in every account complicates management and bypasses the hub-and-spoke centralization requirement.

answers.content: Create an AWS PrivateLink connection between the egress VPC and the spoke VPCs. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
answers.explanation: AWS PrivateLink is designed for private connectivity to services, not for centralizing internet egress routing through a NAT gateway.

questions.content: A company has developed a hybrid solution between its data center and AWS. The company uses Amazon VPC and Amazon EC2 instances that send application logs to Amazon CloudWatch. The EC2 instances read data from multiple relational databases that are hosted on premises. The company wants to monitor which EC2 instances are connected to the databases in near-real timThe company already has a monitoring solution that uses Splunk on premises. A solutions architect needs to determine how to send networking traffic to Splunk. How should the solutions architect meet these requirements?

answers.content: Enable VPC flows logs, and send them to CloudWatch. Create an AWS Lambda function to periodically export the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon S3 bucket by using the pre-defined export function. Generate ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY AWS credentials. Configure Splunk to pull the logs from the S3 bucket by using those credentials.
answers.explanation: Involves generating AWS credentials and custom polling from S3, which is less secure and less real-time compared to managed streaming approaches.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination. Configure a pre-processing AWS Lambda function with a Kinesis Data Firehose stream processor that extracts individual log events from records sent by CloudWatch Logs subscription filters. Enable VPC flows logs, and send them to CloudWatch. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription that sends log events to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.
answers.explanation: Using a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination enables near-real-time, managed delivery of log data to Splunk, which aligns with AWS best practices. Creating a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to send VPC flow logs to Kinesis Data Firehose directly integrates managed AWS services without requiring manual or custom credential management. A pre-processing Lambda function ensures efficient extraction and transformation of log events before delivery to Splunk, meeting the requirement for near-real-time monitoring. This approach avoids insecure practices like generating and distributing AWS credentials for pulling logs from S3, or complex manual ETL and polling mechanisms.

answers.content: Ask the company to log every request that is made to the databases along with the EC2 instance IP address. Export the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs grouped by database namExport Athena results to another S3 bucket. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to automatically send any new file that is put in the S3 bucket to Splunk.
answers.explanation: Relies heavily on manual log exporting, Athena querying, and Lambda polling, introducing latency and operational complexity not suitable for near-real-time monitoring.

answers.content: Send the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL Applications. Configure a 1-minute sliding window to collect the events. Create a SQL query that uses the anomaly detection template to monitor any networking traffic anomalies in near-real timSend the result to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination.
answers.explanation: Focuses on anomaly detection via Kinesis Data Analytics rather than direct ingestion of all traffic logs into Splunk, which does not satisfy the requirement to monitor connections in near-real time.

questions.content: A solutions architect is planning to migrate critical Microsoft SQL Server databases to AWS. Because the databases are legacy systems, the solutions architect will move the databases to a modern data architecturThe solutions architect must migrate the databases with near-zero downtimWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration Service and the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Perform an in-place upgrade before the migration. Export the migrated data to Amazon Aurora Serverless after cutover. Repoint the applications to Amazon Aurora.
answers.explanation: Application Migration Service is for rehosting entire servers, and AWS SCT is for schema conversion, not designed for near-zero downtime migrations to Aurora Serverless in this legacy SQL Server case.

answers.content: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to rehost the databasSet Amazon S3 as a target. Set up change data capture (CDC) replication. When the source and destination are fully synchronized, load the data from Amazon S3 into an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance.
answers.explanation: Using AWS DMS to replicate to S3 and then loading into RDS requires an additional loading step, which does not support near-zero downtime effectively.

answers.content: Use native database high availability tools. Connect the source system to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instancConfigure replication accordingly. When data replication is finished, transition the workload to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance.
answers.explanation: AWS best practices recommend using native database high availability tools for near-zero downtime migrations of Microsoft SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for SQL Server. The provided facts recommend migration from on-premises SQL Server to Amazon RDS for SQL Server using native SQL Server tools or AWS DMS, but near-zero downtime is best achieved with native high availability tools. Connecting the source to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance with replication configured allows for synchronized data transfer with minimal downtimThis approach aligns with the recommended use of managed AWS services for hosting SQL Server databases while leveraging native capabilities for replication and failover.

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration ServicRehost the database server on Amazon EC2. When data replication is finished, detach the database and move the database to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instancReattach the database and then cut over all networking.
answers.explanation: Application Migration Service rehosts servers on EC2, which adds operational overhead, and detaching/attaching databases before cutover is not aligned with near-zero downtime best practices.

questions.content: A company has an IoT platform that runs in an on-premises environment. The platform consists of a server that connects to IoT devices by using the MQTT protocol. The platform collects telemetry data from the devices at least once every 5 minutes. The platform also stores device metadata in a MongoDB cluster. An application that is installed on an on-premises machine runs periodic jobs to aggregate and transform the telemetry and device metadata. The application creates reports that users view by using another web application that runs on the same on-premises machinThe periodic jobs take 120-600 seconds to run. However, the web application is always running. The company is moving the platform to AWS and must reduce the operational overhead of the stack. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Use AWS Lambda functions to connect to the IoT devices
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Lambda cannot maintain long-lived persistent MQTT connections to thousands of IoT devices, and managing device connectivity is operationally complex compared to using AWS IoT Core.

answers.content: Configure the IoT devices to publish to AWS IoT Core
answers.explanation: correct because AWS IoT Core is a fully managed service that natively supports MQTT, removes the need to manage brokers or servers, and significantly reduces operational overhead.

answers.content: Write the metadata to a self-managed MongoDB database on an Amazon EC2 instance
answers.explanation: incorrect because running a self-managed MongoDB database on EC2 requires patching, backups, scaling, monitoring, and high availability management, which increases operational overhead.

answers.content: Write the metadata to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
answers.explanation: correct because Amazon DocumentDB is a managed service compatible with MongoDB that offloads maintenance tasks such as backups, patching, and scaling, thereby reducing operational burden.

answers.content: Use AWS Step Functions state machines with AWS Lambda tasks to prepare the reports and to write the reports to Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront with an S3 origin to serve the reports
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Step Functions with Lambda provides fully managed orchestration for periodic batch jobs without managing servers, and storing reports in S3 with CloudFront eliminates the need to run a continuously operating web server.

answers.content: Use an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with Amazon EC2 instances to prepare the reports. Use an ingress controller in the EKS cluster to serve the reports
answers.explanation: incorrect because running EKS with EC2 introduces cluster management, node scaling, patching, and networking overhead, which contradicts the requirement to minimize operational effort.

questions.content: A company's public API runs as tasks on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The tasks run on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and are configured with Service Auto Scaling for the tasks based on CPU utilization. This service has been running well for several months. Recently, API performance slowed down and made the application unusablThe company discovered that a significant number of SQL injection attacks had occurred against the API and that the API service had scaled to its maximum amount. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that prevents SQL injection attacks from reaching the ECS API servicThe solution must allow legitimate traffic through and must maximize operational efficiency. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL to monitor the HTTP requests and HTTPS requests that are forwarded to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
answers.explanation: Monitoring requests only does not prevent SQL injection attacks; it lacks blocking capability.

answers.content: Create a new AWS WAF Bot Control implementation. Add a rule in the AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group to monitor traffic and allow only legitimate traffic to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF Bot Control targets bots, not specific SQL injection attack patterns, thus less effective for this scenario.

answers.content: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Add a new rule that blocks requests that match the SQL database rule group. Set the web ACL to allow all other traffic that does not match those rules. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF web ACLs with managed rule groups for SQL injection provide a direct and operationally efficient way to block SQL injection attempts. Attaching a WAF web ACL to the ALB in front of ECS tasks protects the service without requiring changes to the application code or infrastructurBlocking SQL injection attacks at the WAF layer aligns with AWS best practices for security and operational efficiency. AWS WAF managed rule groups specifically include protections against SQL injection, making this approach highly targeted and effective.

answers.content: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Create a new empty IP set in AWS WAF. Add a new rule to the web ACL to block requests that originate from IP addresses in the new IP set. Create an AWS Lambda function that scrapes the API logs for IP addresses that send SQL injection attacks, and add those IP addresses to the IP set. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function to parse logs and update IP blocklists is reactive, complex, and less operationally efficient compared to managed WAF rules.

questions.content: A company is building a hybrid environment that includes servers in an on-premises data center and in the AWS Cloud. The company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances in three VPCs. Each VPC is in a different AWS Region. The company has established an AWS Direct. Connect connection to the data center from the Region that is closest to the data center. The company needs the servers in the on-premises data center to have access to the EC2 instances in all three VPCs. The servers in the on-premises data center also must have access to AWS public services. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST cost? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a Direct Connect gateway in the Region that is closest to the data center. Attach the Direct Connect connection to the Direct Connect gateway. Use the Direct Connect gateway to connect the VPCs in the other two Regions.
answers.explanation: correct because a Direct Connect gateway allows a single Direct Connect connection to access multiple VPCs across different Regions, eliminating the need for additional Direct Connect circuits and minimizing cost.

answers.content: Set up additional Direct Connect connections from the on-premises data center to the other two Regions.
answers.explanation: incorrect because provisioning separate Direct Connect connections to each additional Region significantly increases cost and is unnecessary when a Direct Connect gateway can provide cross-Region connectivity.

answers.content: Create a private VIF. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the private VIF to the VPCs in the other two Regions.
answers.explanation: incorrect because a private VIF is used to access VPC resources over Direct Connect and cannot be used to establish Site-to-Site VPN connections over it.

answers.content: Create a public VIF. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the public VIF to the VPCs in the other two Regions.
answers.explanation: correct because a public VIF enables access to AWS public services over Direct Connect and supports establishing VPN connections to VPCs in other Regions without requiring additional Direct Connect circuits.

answers.content: Use VPC peering to establish a connection between the VPCs across the Regions Create a private VIF with the existing Direct Connect connection to connect to the peered VPCs.
answers.explanation: incorrect because VPC peering across Regions would incur inter-Region data transfer charges and still would not provide access to AWS public services without a public VIF, making it less cost-effective.

questions.content: A company is using an organization in AWS Organizations to manage hundreds of AWS accounts. A solutions architect is working on a solution to provide baseline protection for the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) top 10 web application vulnerabilities. The solutions architect is using AWS WAF for all existing and new Amazon CloudFront distributions that are deployed within the organization. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to provide the baseline protection? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Enable AWS Config in all accounts
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Config is required for AWS Firewall Manager to evaluate resource compliance and automatically apply WAF policies across accounts.

answers.content: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in all accounts
answers.explanation: incorrect because Amazon GuardDuty detects threats and malicious activity but does not deploy or enforce AWS WAF rules for OWASP protection.

answers.content: Enable all features for the organization
answers.explanation: correct because enabling all features in AWS Organizations is required to use AWS Firewall Manager centrally across multiple accounts in the organization.

answers.content: Use AWS Firewall Manager to deploy AWS WAF rules in all accounts for all CloudFront distributions
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Firewall Manager allows centralized deployment and enforcement of AWS WAF rules (including OWASP protections) across all CloudFront distributions in existing and new accounts.

answers.content: Use AWS Shield Advanced to deploy AWS WAF rules in all accounts for all CloudFront distributions
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Shield Advanced provides DDoS protection and integrates with WAF, but it does not centrally deploy baseline OWASP WAF rules across accounts.

answers.content: Use AWS Security Hub to deploy AWS WAF rules in all accounts for all CloudFront distributions
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Security Hub aggregates and reports security findings but does not deploy or manage AWS WAF rules.

questions.content: A company is storing sensitive data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must log all activities for objects in the S3 bucket and must keep the logs for 5 years. The company's security team also must receive an email notification every time there is an attempt to delete data in the S3 bucket. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log S3 data events.
answers.explanation: correct because CloudTrail data events provide detailed logging of object-level API activity such as GetObject and DeleteObject, which is required to track all object activities.

answers.content: Configure S3 server access logging for the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: incorrect because S3 server access logging does not capture all object-level API events as comprehensively as CloudTrail data events and is less suitable for auditing sensitive data access.

answers.content: Configure Amazon S3 to send object deletion events to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
answers.explanation: incorrect because S3 cannot directly send deletion notifications to Amazon SES, and SES is not designed for event-driven storage notifications.

answers.content: Configure Amazon S3 to send object deletion events to an Amazon EventBridge event bus that publishes to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
answers.explanation: correct because configuring S3 object deletion events to EventBridge and then to SNS enables automated email notifications in a simple and cost-effective serverless manner.

answers.content: Configure Amazon S3 to send the logs to Amazon Timestream with data storage tiering.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Amazon Timestream is a time-series database and is not a cost-effective or appropriate solution for long-term log retention.

answers.content: Configure a new S3 bucket to store the logs with an S3 Lifecycle policy.
answers.explanation: correct because storing logs in a separate S3 bucket with a lifecycle policy (for example transitioning to Glacier storage classes) ensures durable and cost-effective retention for 5 years.

questions.content: A solutions architect is designing an application to accept timesheet entries from employees on their mobile devices. Timesheets will be submitted weekly, with most of the submissions occurring on Friday. The data must be stored in a format that allows payroll administrators to run monthly reports. The infrastructure must be highly available and scale to match the rate of incoming data and reporting requests. Which combination of steps meets these requirements while minimizing operational overhead? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Deploy the application to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances with load balancing across multiple Availability Zones. Use scheduled Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to add capacity before the high volume of submissions on Fridays.
answers.explanation: incorrect because running the application on EC2 instances requires managing servers, scaling policies, patching, and capacity planning, which increases operational overhead compared to serverless alternatives.

answers.content: Deploy the application in a container using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with load balancing across multiple Availability Zones. Use scheduled Service Auto Scaling to add capacity before the high volume of submissions on Fridays.
answers.explanation: incorrect because although ECS reduces some management compared to EC2, it still requires cluster and service management, scaling configuration, and operational maintenance, which is more overhead than a fully serverless architecture.

answers.content: Deploy the application front end to an Amazon S3 bucket served by Amazon CloudFront. Deploy the application backend using Amazon API Gateway with an AWS Lambda proxy integration.
answers.explanation: correct because hosting the frontend on S3 with CloudFront and using API Gateway with Lambda provides a highly available, automatically scaling, fully managed serverless architecture with minimal operational effort.

answers.content: Store the timesheet submission data in Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon QuickSight to generate the reports using Amazon Redshift as the data source.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Amazon Redshift requires cluster management and is optimized for large-scale data warehousing, which introduces unnecessary operational overhead for this workload.

answers.content: Store the timesheet submission data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena and Amazon QuickSight to generate the reports using Amazon S3 as the data source.
answers.explanation: correct because storing submissions in S3 and querying with Athena enables serverless, scalable reporting, and QuickSight can generate reports without managing database infrastructure, minimizing operational overhead.

questions.content: A global manufacturing company plans to migrate the majority of its applications to AWS. However, the company is concerned about applications that need to remain within a specific country or in the company's central on-premises data center because of data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. The company also is concerned about the applications that it hosts in some of its factory sites, where limited network infrastructure exists. The company wants a consistent developer experience so that its developers can build applications once and deploy on premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid architecturThe developers must be able to use the same tools, APIs, and services that are familiar to them. Which solution will provide a consistent hybrid experience to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate all applications to the closest AWS Region that is compliant. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the central on-premises data center and AWS. Deploy a Direct Connect gateway.
answers.explanation: Migrating all applications to the closest AWS Region does not address the need to keep some applications on premises for latency or regulatory reasons.

answers.content: Use AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices for the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. Retain the devices on premises. Deploy AWS Wavelength to host the workloads in the factory sites.
answers.explanation: Using Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices and AWS Wavelength does not provide the consistent AWS APIs and developer experience for hybrid deployments as Outposts does.

answers.content: Install AWS Outposts for the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. Use AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devices to host the workloads in the factory sites.
answers.explanation: AWS Outposts provides fully managed infrastructure and services on premises, enabling a consistent developer experience with the same AWS APIs, tools, and services. AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devices offer on-premises edge computing capabilities where network infrastructure is limited, fitting the factory sites' scenario. This solution addresses regulatory requirements, latency needs, and limited network infrastructure while maintaining a unified developer experiencThe key facts emphasize hybrid cloud architectures integrating on-premises and cloud resources, which AWS Outposts and Snowball Edge fulfill.

answers.content: Migrate the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds to an AWS Local ZonDeploy AWS Wavelength to host the workloads in the factory sites.
answers.explanation: AWS Local Zones and AWS Wavelength do not provide the full hybrid architecture with on-premises hardware and the consistent developer experience required.

questions.content: A large education company recently introduced Amazon Workspaces to provide access to internal applications across multiple universities. The company is storing user profiles on an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. The file system is configured with a DNS alias and is connected to a self-managed Active Directory. As more users begin to use the Workspaces, login time increases to unacceptable levels. An investigation reveals a degradation in performance of the file system. The company created the file system on HDD storage with a throughput of 16 MBps. A solutions architect must improve the performance of the file system during a defined maintenance window. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort?

answers.content: Use AWS Backup to create a point-in-time backup of the file system. Restore the backup to a new FSx for Windows File Server file system. Select SSD as the storage typSelect 32 MBps as the throughput capacity. When the backup and restore process is completed, adjust the DNS alias accordingly. Delete the original file system.
answers.explanation: correct because restoring from an AWS Backup to a new FSx for Windows File Server allows changing the storage type from HDD to SSD and increasing throughput to 32 MBps in a controlled maintenance window with minimal operational complexity, then simply updating the DNS alias.

answers.content: Disconnect users from the file system. In the Amazon FSx console, update the throughput capacity to 32 MBps. Update the storage type to SSD. Reconnect users to the file system.
answers.explanation: incorrect because FSx for Windows File Server does not allow changing the storage type from HDD to SSD after creation, so this option is not technically feasible.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent onto a new Amazon EC2 instancCreate a task. Configure the existing file system as the source location. Configure a new FSx for Windows File Server file system with SSD storage and 32 MBps of throughput as the target location. Schedule the task. When the task is completed, adjust the DNS alias accordingly. Delete the original file system.
answers.explanation: incorrect because using AWS DataSync introduces additional setup, agent deployment, task configuration, and operational steps, which increases administrative effort compared to a native backup and restore process.

answers.content: Enable shadow copies on the existing file system by using a Windows PowerShell command. Schedule the shadow copy job to create a point-in-time backup of the file system. Choose to restore previous versions. Create a new FSx for Windows File Server file system with SSD storage and 32 MBps of throughput. When the copy job is completed, adjust the DNS alias. Delete the original file system.
answers.explanation: incorrect because shadow copies are intended for file recovery within the same file system and cannot be used to migrate data to a new file system with different storage characteristics, making this approach unsuitable.

questions.content: An online gaming company needs to rehost its gaming platform on AWS. The company's gaming application requires high performance computing (HPC) processing and has a leaderboard that changes frequently. An Ubuntu instance that is optimized for compute generation hosts a Node.js application for game display. Game state is tracked in an on-premises Redis instancThe company needs a migration strategy that optimizes application performancWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group of m5.large Amazon EC2 Spot Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon ElastlCache for Redis cluster to maintain the leaderboard.
answers.explanation: m5.large instances are general purpose, not compute-optimized, which is suboptimal for HPC workloads; Spot Instances can be interrupted, risking instability.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group of c5.large Amazon EC2 Spot Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster to maintain the leaderboard.
answers.explanation: OpenSearch Service is not designed for a leaderboard use case; it is for search and analytics, not a key-value store with low latency like Redis.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group of c5.large Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to maintain the leaderboard.
answers.explanation: Compute-optimized EC2 instances (c5.large) are recommended for high-performance computing workloads, aligning with the gaming platform's HPC requirements. Using Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is the preferred managed service for a frequent-changing leaderboard, optimizing performance and simplifying migration from the on-premises Redis instancOn-Demand instances ensure availability and stability, which is critical for a gaming platform compared to Spot Instances that may be interrupted. The use of an Application Load Balancer with an Auto Scaling group aligns with best practices for availability and scalability.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group of m5.large Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to maintain the leaderboard.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is a managed key-value store but is not the best fit for a frequently changing leaderboard requiring fast in-memory access; also, m5.large is not compute-optimized.

questions.content: A company hosts an application on AWS. The application reads and writes objects that are stored in a single Amazon S3 bucket. The company must modify the application to deploy the application in two AWS Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as an origin. Deploy the application to a second Region Modify the application to use the CloudFront distribution. Use AWS Global Accelerator to access the data in the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: CloudFront is primarily a content delivery network and does not synchronize S3 bucket data across Regions; AWS Global Accelerator does not provide S3 data replication, so this lacks data consistency.

answers.content: Create a new S3 bucket in a second Region. Set up bidirectional S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) between the original S3 bucket and the new S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Multi-Region Access Point that uses both S3 buckets. Deploy a modified application to both Regions.
answers.explanation: S3 Multi-Region Access Points provide a managed, low operational overhead solution for accessing S3 buckets across multiple Regions, improving availability and performancBidirectional S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) ensures data consistency between buckets across Regions, which is essential for the application to read and write in both Regions. Deploying the application to both Regions and using the Multi-Region Access Point allows the application to seamlessly access data without custom routing logic or additional services. This solution leverages managed AWS services designed for multi-Region data access with minimal operational overhead, adhering to AWS best practices.
