answers.content: Create a new S3 bucket in a second Region Deploy the application in the second Region. Configure the application to use the new S3 bucket. Set up S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the original S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Setup is unidirectional replication only, which may lead to data inconsistency as writes to the second bucket are not replicated back, increasing operational complexity and risk.

answers.content: Set up an S3 gateway endpoint with the S3 bucket as an origin. Deploy the application to a second Region. Modify the application to use the new S3 gateway endpoint. Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 gateway endpoints are for VPC access optimization and do not facilitate cross-Region data access or replication; Intelligent-Tiering is unrelated to multi-Region deployments.

questions.content: A solutions architect has implemented a SAML 2.0 federated identity solution with their company's on-premises identity provider (IdP) to authenticate users' access to the AWS environment. When the solutions architect tests authentication through the federated identity web portal, access to the AWS environment is granted. However, when test users attempt to authenticate through the federated identity web portal, they are not able to access the AWS environment. Which items should the solutions architect check to ensure identity federation is properly configured? (Choose three.)

answers.content: The IAM user's permissions policy has allowed the use of SAML federation for that user.
answers.explanation: incorrect because SAML federation grants access by allowing users to assume IAM roles, not by attaching permissions to IAM users, so IAM user policies are not relevant.

answers.content: The IAM roles created for the federated users' or federated groups' trust policy have set the SAML provider as the principal. B. Test users are not in the AWSFederatedUsers group in the company's IdP.
answers.explanation: correct because the IAM role trust policy must specify the SAML provider as the principal; otherwise federated users cannot assume the role.

answers.content: Test users are not in the AWSFederatedUsers group in the company's IdP.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS does not require a specific group name such as AWSFederatedUsers; access depends on proper SAML assertion mapping, not group naming.

answers.content: The web portal calls the AWS STS AssumeRoleWithSAML API with the ARN of the SAML provider, the ARN of the IAM role, and the SAML assertion from IdP.
answers.explanation: correct because the federation process requires the web portal to call the STS AssumeRoleWithSAML API with the correct SAML provider ARN, role ARN, and valid SAML assertion.

answers.content: The on-premises IdP's DNS hostname is reachable from the AWS environment VPCs.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS does not need network connectivity to the on-premises IdP; authentication occurs between the user and the IdP before AWS receives the SAML assertion.

answers.content: The company's IdP defines SAML assertions that properly map users or groups. In the company to IAM roles with appropriate permissions.
answers.explanation: correct because the IdP must generate SAML assertions that correctly map users or groups to the appropriate IAM roles for authorization to succeed.

questions.content: A solutions architect needs to improve an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The application uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance that is experiencing overloaded connections. Most of the application's operations insert records into the databasThe application currently stores credentials in a text-based configuration filThe solutions architect needs to implement a solution so that the application can handle the current connection load. The solution must keep the credentials secure and must provide the ability to rotate the credentials automatically on a regular basis. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon RDS Proxy layer. In front of the DB instancStore the connection credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
answers.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy helps manage and pool database connections, reducing overload on Aurora MySQL instances. Storing credentials in AWS Secrets Manager ensures secure storage and supports automatic credential rotation. Using RDS Proxy with Secrets Manager aligns with AWS best practices for security and handling connection loads. Parameter Store does not inherently provide automatic secret rotation, making Secrets Manager the preferred choice for credential management.

answers.content: Deploy an Amazon RDS Proxy layer in front of the DB instancStore the connection credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
answers.explanation: Parameter Store does not support automatic credential rotation as effectively as Secrets Manager.

answers.content: Create an Aurora Replica. Store the connection credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager
answers.explanation: Creating an Aurora Replica does not address connection overload or secure credential rotation.

answers.content: Create an Aurora Replica. Store the connection credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
answers.explanation: Both creating a replica and storing credentials in Parameter Store do not solve connection overload or provide automatic credential rotation.

questions.content: A company needs to build a disaster recovery (DR) solution for its ecommerce websitThe web application is hosted on a fleet of t3.large Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instancThe EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that extends across multiple Availability Zones. In the event of a disaster, the web application must fail over to the secondary environment with an RPO of 30 seconds and an RTO of 10 minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision the new infrastructure in the DR Region. Create a cross-Region read replica for the DB instancSet up a backup plan in AWS Backup to create cross-Region backups for the EC2 instances and the DB instancCreate a cron expression to back up the EC2 instances and the DB instance every 30 seconds to the DR Region. Recover the EC2 instances from the latest EC2 backup. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to automatically fail over to the DR Region in the event of a disaster.
answers.explanation: Backing up EC2 instances every 30 seconds via cron is not feasible and backups are slower to restore, making it unlikely to meet the 10-minute RTO.

answers.content: Use infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision the new infrastructure in the DR Region. Create a cross-Region read replica for the DB instancSet up AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to continuously replicate the EC2 instances to the DR Region. Run the EC2 instances at the minimum capacity in the DR Region. Use an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy to automatically fail over to the DR Region in the event of a disaster. Increase the desired capacity of the Auto Scaling group.
answers.explanation: Option B uses AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, which provides continuous replication for EC2 instances, supporting a low RPO of 30 seconds. Creating a cross-Region read replica for the RDS instance aligns with best practices for disaster recovery by allowing efficient failover and meeting RTO of 10 minutes. Running EC2 instances at minimum capacity in the DR Region supports cost-effectiveness while enabling quick scaling on failover. Using Route 53 failover routing policy ensures automatic failover which is recommended for disaster recovery scenarios. Option B leverages managed AWS services designed for disaster recovery and meets both RPO and RTO requirements cost-effectively.

answers.content: Set up a backup plan in AWS Backup to create cross-Region backups for the EC2 instances and the DB instancCreate a cron expression to back up the EC2 instances and the DB instance every 30 seconds to the DR Region. Use infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision the new infrastructure in the DR Region. Manually restore the backed-up data on new instances. Use an Amazon Route 53 simple routing policy to automatically fail over to the DR Region in the event of a disaster.
answers.explanation: Manual restoration of backups and using a simple routing policy do not support automatic failover or the tight RTO and RPO requirements.

answers.content: Use infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision the new infrastructure in the DR Region. Create an Amazon Aurora global databasSet up AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to continuously replicate the EC2 instances to the DR Region. Run the Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances at full capacity in the DR Region. Use an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy to automatically fail over to the DR Region in the event of a disaster.
answers.explanation: Aurora global database is irrelevant for RDS MySQL and running EC2 instances at full capacity in DR Region is not cost-effective.

questions.content: A company is planning a one-time migration of an on-premises MySQL database to Amazon Aurora MySQL in the us-east-1 Region. The company's current internet connection has limited bandwidth. The on-premises MySQL database is 60 TB in sizThe company estimates that it will take a month to transfer the data to AWS over the current internet connection. The company needs a migration solution that will migrate the database more quickly. Which solution will migrate the database in the LEAST amount of time?

answers.content: Request a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and AWS. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the on-premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect can reduce transfer time but ordering and provisioning 1 Gbps connection can be slow; still relies on network, which is limited.

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync with the current internet connection to accelerate the data transfer between the on-premises data center and AWS. Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the on-premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync improves transfer but still constrained by limited bandwidth, and Application Migration Service is not intended for database migration.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowball Edge devicLoad the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using the S3 interfacUse AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data from Amazon S3 to Aurora MySQL.
answers.explanation: AWS Snowball devices enable offline data transfer of large datasets faster than limited internet bandwidth. Using Snowball Edge to load data into Amazon S3 and then using AWS DMS to migrate to Aurora MySQL utilizes managed AWS services. AWS DMS is appropriate for database migration, ensuring consistency and minimal data loss for MySQL to Aurora MySQL migration. This approach avoids slow internet transfer and leverages physical data transfer and managed migration services.

answers.content: Order an AWS Snowball devicLoad the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using the S3 Adapter for Snowball. Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the data from Amazon S3 to Aurora MySQL.
answers.explanation: AWS Snowball without Edge offers lower compute capabilities and Application Migration Service is not suitable for database migration from S3 to Aurora MySQL.

questions.content: A company has an application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on a fleet of 20 Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are persistent and store data on multiple attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company must maintain backups in a separate AWS Region. The company must be able to recover the EC2 instances and their configuration within 1 business day, with loss of no more than 1 day's worth of data. The company has limited staff and needs a backup solution that optimizes operational efficiency and cost. The company already has created an AWS CloudFormation template that can deploy the required network configuration in a secondary Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a second CloudFormation template that can recreate the EC2 instances in the secondary Region. Run daily multivolume snapshots by using AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks. Copy the snapshots to the secondary Region. In the event of a failure launch the CloudFormation templates, restore the EBS volumes from snapshots, and transfer usage to the secondary Region.
answers.explanation: Manual snapshot management using Systems Manager Automation is more operationally complex and less preferred than AWS Backup.

answers.content: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to create daily multivolume snapshots of the EBS volumes. In the event of a failure, launch the CloudFormation template and use Amazon DLM to restore the EBS volumes and transfer usage to the secondary Region.
answers.explanation: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager does not support restoring EBS volumes across Regions or managing instance configurations, limiting disaster recovery capability.

answers.content: Use AWS Backup to create a scheduled daily backup plan for the EC2 instances. Configure the backup task to copy the backups to a vault in the secondary Region. In the event of a failure, launch the CloudFormation template, restore the instance volumes and configurations from the backup vault, and transfer usage to the secondary Region.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup provides a managed service to create scheduled daily backups, including multi-volume EC2 instances, optimizing operational efficiency. AWS Backup supports cross-Region backup vault replication, ensuring backups are stored in a secondary Region for disaster recovery. Using AWS Backup leverages a fully managed service, enhancing security and cost-effectiveness compared to manual snapshot management. The solution aligns with recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) targets by enabling recovery within a business day with no more than 1 day's data loss. Launching the CloudFormation template to restore network and instance configuration aligns with the existing infrastructure automation.

answers.content: Deploy EC2 instances of the same size and configuration to the secondary Region. Configure AWS DataSync daily to copy data from the primary Region to the secondary Region. In the event of a failure, launch the CloudFormation template and transfer usage to the secondary Region.
answers.explanation: DataSync focuses on data transfer but does not handle instance backups or configurations, and deploying instances without volume backups risks data loss beyond 1 day.

questions.content: A company is implementing a serverless architecture by using AWS Lambda functions that need to access a Microsoft SQL Server DB instance on Amazon RDS. The company has separate environments for development and production, including a clone of the database system. The company's developers are allowed to access the credentials for the development databasHowever, the credentials for the production database must be encrypted with a key that only members of the IT security team's IAM user group can access. This key must be rotated on a regular basis. What should a solutions architect do in the production environment to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Store the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store by using a SecureString parameter that is encrypted by an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Attach a role to each Lambda function to provide access to the SecureString parameter. Restrict access to the SecureString parameter and the customer managed key so that only the IT security team can access the parameter and the key.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store is less ideal than Secrets Manager for managing database credentials with rotation requirements.

answers.content: Encrypt the database credentials by using the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) default Lambda key. Store the credentials in the environment variables of each Lambda function. Load the credentials from the environment variables in the Lambda codRestrict access to the KMS key so that only the IT security team can access the key.
answers.explanation: Storing credentials in Lambda environment variables is discouraged and the default Lambda KMS key cannot be rotated by the customer.

answers.content: Store the database credentials in the environment variables of each Lambda function. Encrypt the environment variables by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Restrict access to the customer managed key so that only the IT security team can access the key.
answers.explanation: Environment variables are not encrypted by KMS keys directly and storing credentials there is less secure and not best practice.

answers.content: Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager as a secret that is associated with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Attach a role to each Lambda function to provide access to the secret. Restrict access to the secret and the customer managed key so that only the IT security team can access the secret and the key.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the preferred managed service for storing and managing database credentials securely. Using a customer managed AWS KMS key allows encryption keys to be controlled and rotated regularly as required. Attaching roles to Lambda functions provides secure access without embedding credentials in code or environment variables. Restricting access to the secret and KMS key to only the IT security team aligns with the requirement to limit production credential access. Secrets Manager natively supports secret rotation which meets the requirement for regular key rotation.

questions.content: An online retail company is migrating its legacy on-premises .NET application to AWS. The application runs on load-balanced frontend web servers, load-balanced application servers, and a Microsoft SQL Server databasThe company wants to use AWS managed services where possible and does not want to rewrite the application. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to resolve scaling issues and minimize licensing costs as the application scales. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer for the web tier and for the application tier. Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish turned on to replatform the SQL Server database.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish allows running SQL Server applications with minimal changes and significantly reduces licensing costs compared to running SQL Server natively. Deploying EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer supports scaling for web and application tiers without rewriting the application. AWS managed services like Aurora provide cost-effective scalability and reduce operational overhead compared to managing SQL Server on EC2 or container platforms. This approach meets the requirements of using managed services where possible, resolving scaling issues, and reducing licensing costs.

answers.content: Create images of all the servers by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Deploy Amazon EC2 instances that are based on the on-premises imports. Deploy the instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer for the web tier and for the application tier. Use Amazon DynamoDB as the database tier.
answers.explanation: Using AWS DMS incorrectly described and DynamoDB is not a suitable replacement for SQL Server for the application’s data model without rewriting.

answers.content: Containerize the web frontend tier and the application tier. Provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Create an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer for the web tier and for the application tier. Use Amazon RDS for SQL Server to host the database.
answers.explanation: Running SQL Server on RDS does not reduce licensing costs as effectively as Aurora with Babelfish and containerizing may require application changes.

answers.content: Separate the application functions into AWS Lambda functions. Use Amazon API Gateway for the web frontend tier and the application tier. Migrate the data to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
answers.explanation: Migrating to Lambda, API Gateway, S3, and Athena requires rewriting the application, which the company specifically wants to avoid.

questions.content: A software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider exposes APIs through an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB connects to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that is deployed in the us-east-1 Region. The exposed APIs contain usage of a few non-standard REST methods: LINK, UNLINK, LOCK, and UNLOCK. Users outside the United States are reporting long and inconsistent response times for these APIs. A solutions architect needs to resolve this problem with a solution that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the ALB as the origin.
answers.explanation: CloudFront may not support non-standard REST methods and primarily optimizes caching rather than consistent routing for dynamic APIs.

answers.content: Add an Amazon API Gateway edge-optimized API endpoint to expose the APIs. Configure the ALB as the target.
answers.explanation: API Gateway adds more operational overhead and possibly does not support the custom HTTP methods required, conflicting with the need to minimize overhead.

answers.content: Add an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure the ALB as the origin.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes users to optimal AWS endpoints, improving consistent performance for users globally with low operational overhead. CloudFront is primarily used for content delivery and caching standard HTTP methods but may not support non-standard REST methods such as LINK, UNLINK, LOCK, and UNLOCK effectively. API Gateway can add significant operational overhead as it requires rebuilding API endpoints and may not natively support all non-standard REST methods. Deploying APIs to multiple regions with Route 53 latency-based routing increases operational complexity and overhead due to managing multiple EKS clusters, conflicting with the requirement to minimize operational overhead.

answers.content: Deploy the APIs to two additional AWS Regions: eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2. Add latency-based routing records in Amazon Route 53.
answers.explanation: Deploying to multiple regions and managing latency-based DNS routing increases complexity and operational overhead, contrary to requirements.

questions.content: A company runs an unauthenticated static website (www.example.com) that includes a registration form for users. The website uses Amazon S3 for hosting and uses Amazon CloudFront as the content delivery network with AWS WAF configured. When the registration form is submitted, the website calls an Amazon API Gateway API endpoint that invokes an AWS Lambda function to process the payload and forward the payload to an external API call. During testing, a solutions architect encounters a cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) error. The solutions architect confirms that the CloudFront distribution origin has the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to www.example.com. What should the solutions architect do to resolve the error?

answers.content: Change the CORS configuration on the S3 bucket. Add rules for CORS to the AllowedOrigin element for www.example.com.
answers.explanation: The CORS configuration on the S3 bucket does not affect API Gateway endpoints and is unrelated to the CORS error seen on the API Gateway call.

answers.content: Enable the CORS setting in AWS WAF. Create a web ACL rule in which the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is set to www.example.com.
answers.explanation: AWS WAF does not have a CORS setting or the ability to set Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers; WAF is for filtering and blocking requests.

answers.content: Enable the CORS setting on the API Gateway API endpoint. Ensure that the API endpoint is configured to return all responses that have the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to www.example.com.
answers.explanation: CORS errors for API Gateway endpoints are resolved by enabling CORS on the API Gateway API endpoint and ensuring it returns the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to the correct origin. The CloudFront origin already includes the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, but the error persists because the API Gateway endpoint itself must be configured to allow CORS. AWS WAF does not provide a CORS setting as part of its web ACL configurations, so enabling CORS in WAF is not applicablThe Lambda function itself does not inherently set CORS headers; the integration response or API Gateway response must correctly return them. The S3 bucket CORS configuration affects only requests made directly to S3, not API Gateway endpoints.

answers.content: Enable the CORS setting on the Lambda function. Ensure that the return code of the function has the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to www.example.com.
answers.explanation: Adding CORS headers in the Lambda function response is not sufficient unless API Gateway is configured to pass these headers in its response to the client.

questions.content: A company is running an application on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The load on the application varies throughout the day, and EC2 instances are scaled in and out on a regular basis. Log files from the EC2 instances are copied to a central Amazon S3 bucket every 15 minutes. The security team discovers that log files are missing from some of the terminated EC2 instances. Which set of actions will ensure that log files are copied to the central S3 bucket from the terminated EC2 instances?

answers.content: Create a script to copy log files to Amazon S3, and store the script in a file on the EC2 instancCreate an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook and an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect lifecycle events from the Auto Scaling group. Invoke an AWS Lambda function on the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING transition to send ABANDON to the Auto Scaling group to prevent termination, run the script to copy the log files, and terminate the instance using the AWS SDK.
answers.explanation: Sending ABANDON to prevent termination disrupts auto scaling and is not a scalable or secure approach.

answers.content: Create an AWS Systems Manager document with a script to copy log files to Amazon S3. Create an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook and an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect lifecycle events from the Auto Scaling group. Invoke an AWS Lambda function on the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING transition to call the AWS Systems Manager API SendCommand operation to run the document to copy the log files and send CONTINUE to the Auto Scaling group to terminate the instance.
answers.explanation: Using Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks allows for intercepting instance termination events to perform custom actions. AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Documents enable running scripts remotely and securely on instances without storing scripts locally or relying on instance user data. Invoking SSM SendCommand through a Lambda function triggered by lifecycle hooks aligns with managed AWS services usage and best practices. Sending CONTINUE to the Auto Scaling group after logs are copied ensures the instance termination proceeds properly without manual intervention or prevention. This method avoids preventing termination indefinitely (which would disrupt auto scaling) and avoids custom event rules that rely on instance user data, improving security and manageability.

answers.content: Change the log delivery rate to every 5 minutes. Create a script to copy log files to Amazon S3, and add the script to EC2 instance user data. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect EC2 instance termination. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from the EventBridge rule that uses the AWS CLI to run the user-data script to copy the log files and terminate the instance.
answers.explanation: Running user data scripts on termination is not reliable; EventBridge rules do not have direct access to run scripts on instances, and frequent log delivery is unrelated to solving missing logs on termination.

answers.content: Create an AWS Systems Manager document with a script to copy log files to Amazon S3. Create an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook that publishes a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. From the SNS notification, call the AWS Systems Manager API SendCommand operation to run the document to copy the log files and send ABANDON to the Auto Scaling group to terminate the instance.
answers.explanation: Sending ABANDON after SNS notification may cause termination delays and disrupt auto scaling; manual intervention via SNS is less direct and less secure than SSM SendCommand.

questions.content: A company is in the process of implementing AWS Organizations to constrain its developers to use only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, and Amazon DynamoDB. The developers account resides in a dedicated organizational unit (OU). The solutions architect has implemented the following SCP on the developers account: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02/image5.png] When this policy is deployed, IAM users in the developers account are still able to use AWS services that are not listed in the policy. What should the solutions architect do to eliminate the developers' ability to use services outside the scope of this policy?

answers.content: Create an explicit deny statement for each AWS service that should be constrained.
answers.explanation: Explicitly denying each unwanted service is impractical and error-prone; more effective to remove permissive SCPs.

answers.content: Remove the FullAWSAccess SCP from the developers account's OU.
answers.explanation: The developers are still able to use services not listed because the FullAWSAccess SCP is attached to the developers account's OU, which allows all AWS services by default. SCPs only limit permissions but do not grant any; therefore, restrictive SCPs must not be overridden by a more permissive SCP like FullAWSAccess. Removing the FullAWSAccess SCP will allow the SCP that constrains usage to take effect and restrict developers to only EC2, S3, and DynamoDB, aligning with the intent to constrain service access.

answers.content: Modify the FullAWSAccess SCP to explicitly deny all services.
answers.explanation: Modifying FullAWSAccess to explicitly deny all services conflicts with its purpose and may cause management complications.

answers.content: Add an explicit deny statement using a wildcard to the end of the SCP.
answers.explanation: Adding an explicit deny wildcard at the end of the SCP may not be effective if FullAWSAccess SCP granting all permissions remains attached.

questions.content: A company's solutions architect is reviewing a web application that runs on AWS. The application references static assets in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company needs resiliency across multiple AWS Regions. The company already has created an S3 bucket in a second Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Configure the application to write each object to both S3 buckets. Set up an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone with a record set by using a weighted routing policy for each S3 bucket. Configure the application to reference the objects by using the Route 53 DNS name.
answers.explanation: Requires manual management by the application to write to both buckets and handle DNS routing, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function to copy objects from the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to the S3 bucket in the second Region. Invoke the Lambda function each time an object is written to the S3 bucket in us-east-1. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin group that contains the two S3 buckets as origins.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function to copy objects increases complexity and operational overhead compared to native S3 replication.

answers.content: Configure replication on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate objects to the S3 bucket in the second Region. Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin group that contains the two S3 buckets as origins.
answers.explanation: Configuring replication on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate objects to the bucket in the second Region uses live replication, which automatically replicates new and updated objects as they are written. Setting up an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin group containing both S3 buckets provides resiliency and automatic failover with minimal operational overhead. This solution leverages managed AWS services (S3 replication and CloudFront origin groups) and best practices for multi-Region resiliency.

answers.content: Configure replication on the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to replicate objects to the S3 bucket in the second Region. If failover is required, update the application code to load S3 objects from the S3 bucket in the second Region.
answers.explanation: Requires manual failover by updating application code, which increases operational overhead and reduces resilience.

questions.content: A company is hosting a three-tier web application in an on-premises environment. Due to a recent surge in traffic that resulted in downtime and a significant financial impact, company management has ordered that the application be moved to AWS. The application is written in .NET and has a dependency on a MySQL databasA solutions architect must design a scalable and highly available solution to meet the demand of 200,000 daily users. Which steps should the solutions architect take to design an appropriate solution?

answers.content: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to create a new application with a web server environment and an Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instancThe environment should launch a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon Route 53 alias record to route traffic from the company's domain to the NLB.
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk with Network Load Balancer is less optimal than ALB for HTTP/S traffic and does not mention multi-AZ deployment across multiple Availability Zones sufficiently, also NLB is more for TCP than HTTP-based web apps.

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation to launch a stack containing an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group spanning three Availability Zones. The stack should launch a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster with a Retain deletion policy. Use an Amazon Route 53 alias record to route traffic from the company's domain to the ALB.
answers.explanation: Option B uses CloudFormation which is a managed service to automate infrastructure deployment, aligning with best practices of managed AWS services over manual solutions. B includes an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an EC2 Auto Scaling group spanning three Availability Zones, providing scalability and high availability with no single point of failurB uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster, which is highly available and managed, preferred over single-instance RDS MySQL or snapshots for production workloads. The use of Route 53 alias records for DNS routing complements a reliable, scalable architecturMulti-AZ Aurora supports failover and automated backups, increasing the application's availability and resilience to failure.

answers.content: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to create an automatically scaling web server environment that spans two separate Regions with an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each Region. Create a Multi-AZ deployment of an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster with a cross-Region read replica. Use Amazon Route 53 with a geoproximity routing policy to route traffic between the two Regions.
answers.explanation: Two Regions deployment adds complexity and cost beyond the requirement; cross-Region read replicas have higher latency and added operational complexity which may not be necessary here.

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation to launch a stack containing an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of an Amazon ECS cluster of Spot instances spanning three Availability Zones. The stack should launch an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance with a Snapshot deletion policy. Use an Amazon Route 53 alias record to route traffic from the company's domain to the ALB.
answers.explanation: Using Spot instances introduces availability risk due to potential interruptions, and a single RDS MySQL DB instance with snapshot deletion policy lacks Multi-AZ high availability.

questions.content: A company needs to implement a patching process for its servers. The on-premises servers and Amazon EC2 instances use a variety of tools to perform patching. Management requires a single report showing the patch status of all the servers and instances. Which set of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager to manage patches on the on-premises servers and EC2 instances. Use Systems Manager to generate patch compliance reports.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager supports managing patches on both on-premises servers and EC2 instances, providing a unified patching solution. Systems Manager can generate patch compliance reports, enabling a consolidated view of patch status across the entire fleet. The key facts highlight that patching on on-premises instances can be integrated with Systems Manager using Patch Groups and Maintenance Windows. Security best practices and centralized management are facilitated by using Systems Manager, a managed AWS service designed specifically for this purpose.

answers.content: Use AWS OpsWorks to manage patches on the on-premises servers and EC2 instances. Use Amazon QuickSight integration with OpsWorks to generate patch compliance reports.
answers.explanation: AWS OpsWorks is not designed primarily for patch management or patch compliance reporting across hybrid environments.

answers.content: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to apply patches by scheduling an AWS Systems Manager patch remediation job. Use Amazon Inspector to generate patch compliance reports.
answers.explanation: Amazon Inspector focuses on vulnerability assessment, not patch compliance reporting; EventBridge is not used for patch status reporting.

answers.content: Use AWS OpsWorks to manage patches on the on-premises servers and EC2 instances. Use AWS X-Ray to post the patch status to AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter to generate patch compliance reports.
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray is a tracing service, not suited for patch compliance reporting; OpsWorks is also not appropriate for patch management in this context.

questions.content: A company is using multiple AWS accounts. The DNS records are stored in a private hosted zone for Amazon Route 53 in Account A. The company's applications and databases are running in Account B. A solutions architect will deploy a two-tier application in a new VPC. To simplify the configuration, the db.example.com CNAME record set for the Amazon RDS endpoint was created in a private hosted zone for Amazon Route 53. During deployment, the application failed to start. Troubleshooting revealed that db.example.com is not resolvable on the Amazon EC2 instancThe solutions architect confirmed that the record set was created correctly in Route 53. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Deploy the database on a separate EC2 instance in the new VPC. Create a record set for the instance's private IP in the private hosted zone.
answers.explanation: Deploying the database on EC2 and managing IP records manually ignores managed RDS benefits and complicates DNS management.

answers.content: Use SSH to connect to the application tier EC2 instancAdd an RDS endpoint IP address to the /etc/resolv.conf file.
answers.explanation: Manually editing /etc/resolv.conf is insecure, error-prone, and not a scalable or managed DNS solution.

answers.content: Create an authorization to associate the private hosted zone in Account A with the new VPC in Account B.
answers.explanation: correct because when a private hosted zone and VPC are in different accounts, an authorization must first be created in the hosted zone account (Account A) to allow association with the VPC in Account B.

answers.content: Create a private hosted zone for the example com domain in Account B. Configure Route 53 replication between AWS accounts.
answers.explanation: Creating a new private hosted zone and replicating records contradicts the best practice to avoid duplication and manual replication of hosted zones.

answers.content: Associate a new VPC in Account B with a hosted zone in Account A. Delete the association authorization in Account A.
answers.explanation: correct because after creating the authorization, the VPC in Account B must be associated with the private hosted zone in Account A to enable DNS resolution, and the authorization can then be removed.

questions.content: A company wants to use a third-party software-as-a-service (SaaS) application. The third-party SaaS application is consumed through several API calls. The third-party SaaS application also runs on AWS inside a VPC. The company will consume the third-party SaaS application from inside a VPC. The company has internal security policies that mandate the use of private connectivity that does not traverse the internet. No resources that run in the company VPC are allowed to be accessed from outside the company's VPC. All permissions must conform to the principles of least privilegWhich solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS PrivateLink interface VPC endpoint. Connect this endpoint to the endpoint service that the third-party SaaS application provides. Create a security group to limit the access to the endpoint. Associate the security group with the endpoint.
answers.explanation: AWS PrivateLink interface VPC endpoints enable private connectivity to third-party SaaS applications within AWS without traversing the internet, fulfilling the requirement for private connectivity. Creating a security group for the endpoint allows enforcement of least privilege by controlling access to the endpoint. This approach ensures no resources in the company VPC are exposed externally and matches best practices for secure, private access to third-party services hosted within AWS.

answers.content: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the third-party SaaS application and the company VPC. Configure network ACLs to limit access across the VPN tunnels.
answers.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN involves external network connectivity which may traverse the internet and is more complex than PrivateLink for this use case.

answers.content: Create a VPC peering connection between the third-party SaaS application and the company VPUpdate route tables by adding the needed routes for the peering connection.
answers.explanation: VPC peering exposes network access between VPCs but does not provide granular access control compared to PrivateLink and lacks the simplicity of retaining full network isolation.

answers.content: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint servicAsk the third-party SaaS provider to create an interface VPC endpoint for this endpoint servicGrant permissions for the endpoint service to the specific account of the third-party SaaS provider.
answers.explanation: Creating an endpoint service in the company VPC requires the third party to create an interface endpoint in their account, which reverses connectivity direction and does not satisfy the requirement to consume the third-party SaaS privately and securely.

questions.content: A company has many AWS accounts and uses AWS Organizations to manage all of them. A solutions architect must implement a solution that the company can use to share a common network across multiple accounts. The company's infrastructure team has a dedicated infrastructure account that has a VPC. The infrastructure team must use this account to manage the network. Individual accounts cannot have the ability to manage their own networks. However, individual accounts must be able to create AWS resources within subnets. Which combination of actions should the solutions architect perform to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create a transit gateway in the infrastructure account.
answers.explanation: incorrect because a transit gateway is used to connect multiple VPCs or networks, but the requirement is to centrally share subnets from a single VPC, which is better achieved with VPC sharing via AWS RAM.

answers.content: Enable resource sharing from the AWS Organizations management account.
answers.explanation: correct because resource sharing within AWS Organizations must be enabled to allow sharing of VPC subnets across accounts in the organization.

answers.content: Create VPCs in each AWS account within the organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the VPCs to share the same CIDR range and subnets as the VPC in the infrastructure account. Peer the VPCs in each individual account with the VPC in the infrastructure account.
answers.explanation: incorrect because creating separate VPCs in each account and peering them increases complexity and allows individual accounts to manage their own networks, which violates the requirement.

answers.content: Create a resource share in AWS Resource Access Manager in the infrastructure account. Select the specific AWS Organizations OU that will use the shared network. Select each subnet to associate with the resource share.
answers.explanation: correct because using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share specific subnets from the infrastructure account to selected OUs enables centralized network management while allowing other accounts to launch resources into those subnets.

answers.content: Create a resource share in AWS Resource Access Manager in the infrastructure account. Select the specific AWS Organizations OU that will use the shared network. Select each prefix list to associate with the resource share.
answers.explanation: incorrect because sharing prefix lists does not allow accounts to launch resources into shared subnets and does not satisfy the requirement for centralized VPC

questions.content: A company runs a processing engine in the AWS Cloud. The engine processes environmental data from logistics centers to calculate a sustainability index. The company has millions of devices in logistics centers that are spread across EuropThe devices send information to the processing engine through a RESTful API. The API experiences unpredictable bursts of traffic. The company must implement a solution to process all data that the devices send to the processing enginData loss is unacceptablWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the RESTful API. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuCreate a listener and a target group for the ALB Add the SQS queue as the target. Use a container that runs in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch type to process messages in the queue.
answers.explanation: ALB cannot have SQS as a target; it supports only IPs, instances, or Lambda, so this integration is invalid.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that implements the RESTful API. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuCreate an API Gateway service integration with the SQS queuCreate an AWS Lambda function to process messages in the SQS queue.
answers.explanation: Amazon API Gateway HTTP API is designed to handle APIs with unpredictable bursts of traffic, providing scalability and high availability. Amazon SQS ensures reliable message queueing with no data loss, meeting the requirement that data loss is unacceptablAPI Gateway integration with SQS is a managed service integration, simplifying architecture and improving reliability and maintainability. AWS Lambda can be used to process messages from SQS asynchronously at scale, without managing servers, fitting best practices for managed services and security.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API that implements the RESTful API. Create a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Create an API Gateway Auto Scaling group proxy integration. Use the EC2 instances to process incoming data.
answers.explanation: API Gateway does not support Auto Scaling group proxy integration; managing EC2 instances adds operational overhead and risk.

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the RESTful API. Create a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Set the data stream as the origin for the distribution. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume and process data in the data stream.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront cannot have a Kinesis Data Stream as an origin, so this architecture is invalid.

questions.content: A solutions architect is designing a solution to process events. The solution must have the ability to scale in and out based on the number of events that the solution receives. If a processing error occurs, the event must move into a separate queue for review. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Send event details to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure an AWS Lambda function as a subscriber to the SNS topic to process the events. Add an on-failure destination to the function. Set an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the target.
answers.explanation: SNS with Lambda on-failure destinations is less suited for scaling based on event volume compared to SQS-based polling and scaling; Lambda scaling might be constrained and SNS does not provide native queuing for failed events as smoothly as SQS dead-letter queues.

answers.content: Publish events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuCreate an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to scale in and out based on the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric of the queuConfigure the application to write failed messages to a dead-letter queue.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SQS with an Auto Scaling group for processing events supports dynamic scaling based on the number of events, as the Auto Scaling group can scale in and out based on the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric. SQS natively supports dead-letter queues for failed message handling, meeting the requirement to move events into a separate queue for review on processing errors. This approach aligns with AWS best practices by using managed services designed for message processing, scaling, and error handling. Option B explicitly mentions scaling and dead-letter queue features necessary to satisfy the problem statement.

answers.content: Write events to an Amazon DynamoDB tablConfigure a DynamoDB stream for the tablConfigure the stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the events.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB Streams with Lambda does not mention error handling with a dead-letter queue or scaling control based on event volume; it also may not provide the required separate queue for failed events.

answers.content: Publish events to an Amazon EventBndge event bus. Create and run an application on an Amazon EC2 instance with an Auto Scaling group that is behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Set the ALB as the event bus target. Configure the event bus to retry events. Write messages to a dead-letter queue if the application cannot process the messages.
answers.explanation: EventBridge with EC2 Auto Scaling and ALB is more complex, lacks a managed queue for failed events, and the event bus retry may not provide as straightforward a dead-letter queue mechanism, thus not best meeting the error handling and scaling requirements.

questions.content: A company runs an application on AWS. The company curates data from several different sources. The company uses proprietary algorithms to perform data transformations and aggregations. After the company performs ETL processes, the company stores the results in Amazon Redshift tables. The company sells this data to other companies. The company downloads the data as files from the Amazon Redshift tables and transmits the files to several data customers by using FTP. The number of data customers has grown significantly. Management of the data customers has become difficult. The company will use AWS Data Exchange to create a data product that the company can use to share data with customers. The company wants to confirm the identities of the customers before the company shares data. The customers also need access to the most recent data when the company publishes the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Use AWS Data Exchange for APIs to share data with customers. Configure subscription verification. In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, create an Amazon API Gateway Data API service integration with Amazon Redshift. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.
answers.explanation: Using API Gateway and creating a custom Data API introduces more operational overhead and complexity compared to managed datashares.

answers.content: In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, create an AWS Data Exchange datashare by connecting AWS Data Exchange to the Redshift cluster. Configure subscription verification. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.
answers.explanation: AWS Data Exchange datashares integrate directly with Amazon Redshift, enabling seamless, secure data sharing without moving data. Subscription verification in AWS Data Exchange confirms customer identities before access, aligning with the requirement to confirm identities. Datashares provide customers with access to the most recent data as data updates are shared automatically, meeting the requirement for up-to-date data access. This approach reduces operational overhead compared to manually downloading and uploading files or managing API Gateway and custom integrations.

answers.content: Download the data from the Amazon Redshift tables to an Amazon S3 bucket periodically. Use AWS Data Exchange for S3 to share data with customers. Configure subscription verification. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.
answers.explanation: Downloading data to S3 and sharing via Data Exchange S3 involves additional data movement and management, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Publish the Amazon Redshift data to an Open Data on AWS Data ExchangRequire the customers to subscribe to the data product in AWS Data ExchangIn the AWS account of the company that produces the data, attach IAM resource-based policies to the Amazon Redshift tables to allow access only to verified AWS accounts.
answers.explanation: Publishing as Open Data less securely handles subscription verification and attaching IAM policies to tables is complex and less operationally efficient.

questions.content: A company is designing its network configuration in the AWS Cloud. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage a multi-account setup. The company has three OUs. Each OU contains more than 100 AWS accounts. Each account has a single VPC, and all the VPCs in each OU are in the same AWS Region. The CIDR ranges for all the AWS accounts do not overlap. The company needs to implement a solution in which VPCs in the same OU can communicate with each other but cannot communicate with VPCs in other OUs. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that establishes VPC peering between accounts in each OU. Provision the stack set in each OU.
answers.explanation: VPC peering between 100+ accounts per OU creates a large number of peering connections and route updates, leading to high operational overhead.

answers.content: In each OU, create a dedicated networking account that has a single VPC. Share this VPC with all the other accounts in the OU by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create a VPC peering connection between the networking account and each account in the OU.
answers.explanation: Sharing VPCs and VPC peering still require multiple peering connections and route table management, increasing complexity with many accounts.

answers.content: Provision a transit gateway in an account in each OU. Share the transit gateway across the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create transit gateway VPC attachments for each VPC.
answers.explanation: Transit gateways enable scalable network connectivity across multiple VPCs without needing to create individual peering connections, reducing operational overhead. Transit gateways support centralized routing management and can be shared across accounts and OUs using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Using transit gateways aligns with operational best practices by minimizing manual route management compared to VPC peering, which requires route table updates for each connection. Dedicated networking accounts with transit gateways within each OU isolate communication between OUs as required.

answers.content: In each OU, create a dedicated networking account that has a single VPC. Establish a VPN connection between the networking account and the other accounts in the OU. Use third-party routing software to route transitive traffic between the VPCs.
answers.explanation: Using VPN connections and third-party routing software adds unnecessary complexity and operational overhead compared to managed transit gateway solutions.

questions.content: A company is migrating an application to AWS. It wants to use fully managed services as much as possible during the migration. The company needs to store large important documents within the application with the following requirements: 1. The data must be highly durable and available 2. The data must always be encrypted at rest and in transit 3. The encryption key must be managed by the company and rotated periodically Which of the following solutions should the solutions architect recommend?

answers.content: Deploy the storage gateway to AWS in file gateway modUse Amazon EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the storage gateway volumes.
answers.explanation: Storage Gateway with EBS encryption is less ideal than S3 for highly durable and available document storage and requires managing a gateway appliance.

answers.content: Use Amazon S3 with a bucket policy to enforce HTTPS for connections to the bucket and to enforce server-side encryption and AWS KMS for object encryption.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is a fully managed AWS service that provides high durability and availability for data storagS3 supports encryption at rest using AWS KMS keys, with the ability to use customer managed keys which the company can rotatBucket policies can enforce HTTPS, ensuring encryption in transit. Using a fully managed service like S3 aligns with the requirement to use fully managed services and avoid managing underlying infrastructure.

answers.content: Use Amazon DynamoDB with SSL to connect to DynamoDB. Use an AWS KMS key to encrypt DynamoDB objects at rest.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB is not optimized for storing large documents and may not meet durability and storage size requirements effectively.

answers.content: Deploy instances with Amazon EBS volumes attached to store this data. Use EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the data.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances with EBS volumes is not fully managed and requires manual management, which goes against the requirement to use fully managed services.

questions.content: An environmental company is deploying sensors in major cities throughout a country to measure air quality. The sensors connect to AWS IoT Core to ingest timeseries data readings. The company stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB. For business continuity, the company must have the ability to ingest and store data in two AWS Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Route 53 alias failover routing policy with values for AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions Migrate data to Amazon Aurora global tables.
answers.explanation: Migrating data to Amazon Aurora global tables is incorrect because the data is stored in DynamoDB, not Aurora.

answers.content: Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Migrate the data to Amazon MemoryDB for Redis and configure cross-Region replication.
answers.explanation: Migrating data to Amazon MemoryDB for Redis is not aligned with the current data store (DynamoDB) and MemoryDB is not suitable for timeseries storage at scale here.

answers.content: Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check that evaluates domain configuration health. Create a failover routing policy with values for the domain name from the AWS IoT Core domain configurations. Update the DynamoDB table to a global table.
answers.explanation: Creating a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region ensures multi-region data ingestion endpoints. Using an Amazon Route 53 health check and failover routing policy for AWS IoT Core domain configurations provides fault tolerance and business continuity. Updating the DynamoDB table to a global table enables multi-region replication and ensures the data is stored and synchronized across Regions. This approach uses managed AWS services designed for multi-region highly available architectures, aligning with best security and operational practices.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Configure DynamoDB streams and cross-Region data replication.
answers.explanation: Configuring only DynamoDB streams and cross-region data replication without using DynamoDB global tables is not sufficient for full multi-region write availability and business continuity.

questions.content: A company uses AWS Organizations for a multi-account setup in the AWS Cloud. The company's finance team has a data processing application that uses AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB. The company's marketing team wants to access the data that is stored in the DynamoDB tablThe DynamoDB table contains confidential data. The marketing team can have access to only specific attributes of data in the DynamoDB tablThe finance team and the marketing team have separate AWS accounts. What should a solutions architect do to provide the marketing team with the appropriate access to the DynamoDB table?

answers.content: Create an SCP to grant the marketing team's AWS account access to the specific attributes of the DynamoDB tablAttach the SCP to the OU of the finance team.
answers.explanation: SCPs only restrict permissions and are not used to grant specific attribute-level access.

answers.content: Create an IAM role in the finance team's account by using IAM policy conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes (fine-grained access control). Establish trust with the marketing team's account. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to assume the IAM role in the finance team's account.
answers.explanation: IAM policies with conditions can enforce fine-grained access control on DynamoDB attributes. Cross-account access is achieved by creating an IAM role in the resource-owning account (finance) with a trust relationship to the marketing team's account. IAM roles and trust relationships are standard AWS best practices for secure cross-account access. SCPs do not grant access but restrict permissions, so they cannot be used to grant attribute-level access. Resource-based policies for DynamoDB are limited and cannot specify fine-grained attribute-level conditions.

answers.content: Create a resource-based IAM policy that includes conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes (fine-grained access control). Attach the policy to the DynamoDB tablIn the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to access the DynamoDB table in the finance team's account.
answers.explanation: DynamoDB does not support resource-based policies with attribute-level fine-grained access conditions; access must be controlled via IAM roles.

answers.content: Create an IAM role in the finance team's account to access the DynamoDB tablUse an IAM permissions boundary to limit the access to the specific attributes. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to assume the IAM role in the finance team's account.
answers.explanation: IAM permissions boundaries do not provide fine-grained attribute-level access control for DynamoDB; policy conditions are required.

questions.content: A solutions architect is creating an application that stores objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect must deploy the application in two AWS Regions that will be used simultaneously. The objects in the two S3 buckets must remain synchronized with each other. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point Change the application to refer to the Multi-Region Access Point
answers.explanation: correct because an S3 Multi-Region Access Point provides a single global endpoint that routes requests to the closest bucket and simplifies multi-Region access with minimal application changes.

answers.content: Configure two-way S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) between the two S3 buckets
answers.explanation: correct because two-way S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) keeps objects synchronized automatically between both buckets without custom logic.

answers.content: Modify the application to store objects in each S3 bucket
answers.explanation: incorrect because modifying the application to write to both buckets increases operational complexity and risks inconsistency compared to managed replication.

answers.content: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule for each S3 bucket to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket
answers.explanation: incorrect because S3 Lifecycle rules cannot replicate objects between buckets; they are designed for storage class transitions and expiration.

answers.content: Enable S3 Versioning for each S3 bucket
answers.explanation: correct because S3 Versioning is required to enable Cross-Region Replication and ensures object changes are properly replicated.

answers.content: Configure an event notification for each S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket
answers.explanation: incorrect because using event notifications with Lambda to copy objects introduces unnecessary operational overhead compared to native S3 replication.

questions.content: A company is updating an application that customers use to make online orders. The number of attacks on the application by bad actors has increased recently. The company will host the updated application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The company will use Amazon DynamoDB to store application data. A public Application Load Balancer (ALB) will provide end users with access to the application. The company must prevent attacks and ensure business continuity with minimal service interruptions during an ongoing attack. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as the origin. Add a custom header and random value on the CloudFront domain. Configure the ALB to conditionally forward traffic if the header and value match.
answers.explanation: correct because placing CloudFront in front of the ALB hides the ALB from direct internet access and ensures traffic flows through CloudFront, and using a custom header that only CloudFront adds prevents attackers from bypassing CloudFront and directly targeting the ALB.

answers.content: Deploy the application in two AWS Regions. Configure Amazon Route 53 to route to both Regions with equal weight.
answers.explanation: incorrect because deploying in multiple Regions increases cost and complexity and is not required to mitigate application-layer attacks in the most cost-effective way.

answers.content: Configure auto scaling for Amazon ECS tasks Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster.
answers.explanation: incorrect because auto scaling and DAX improve performance but do not protect against malicious traffic or application-layer attacks.

answers.content: Configure Amazon ElastiCache to reduce overhead on DynamoDB.
answers.explanation: incorrect because ElastiCache may reduce database load but does not prevent or mitigate attacks against the application endpoint.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS WAF web ACL that includes an appropriate rule group. Associate the web ACL with the Amazon CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: correct because AWS WAF attached to CloudFront provides managed rule groups to block common web exploits (including OWASP threats) and helps maintain availability during attacks in a cost-effective manner.

questions.content: A company runs a web application on AWS. The web application delivers static content from an Amazon S3 bucket that is behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The application serves dynamic content by using an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that distributes requests to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups. The application uses a domain name setup in Amazon Route 53. Some users reported occasional issues when the users attempted to access the website during peak hours. An operations team found that the ALB sometimes returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable errors. The company wants to display a custom error message page when these errors occur. The page should be displayed immediately for this error codWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Set up a Route 53 failover routing policy. Configure a health check to determine the status of the ALB endpoint and to fail over to the failover S3 bucket endpoint.
answers.explanation: Route 53 failover introduces DNS propagation delays, so the error page is not displayed immediately.

answers.content: Create a second CloudFront distribution and an S3 static website to host the custom error pagSet up a Route 53 failover routing policy. Use an active-passive configuration between the two distributions.
answers.explanation: Creating a second CloudFront distribution and failover via Route 53 is more complex and increases management overhead.

answers.content: Create a CloudFront origin group that has two origins. Set the ALB endpoint as the primary origin. For the secondary origin, set an S3 bucket that is configured to host a static website Set up origin failover for the CloudFront distribution. Update the S3 static website to incorporate the custom error page.
answers.explanation: CloudFront origin failover with origin groups allows immediate failover to a custom error page hosted in S3 when the primary origin (ALB) returns HTTP 503 errors. This approach leverages managed AWS services with minimal operational overhead by using CloudFront's built-in origin failover featurUsing an S3 bucket configured as a static website for the error page aligns with best practices for serving static content. Other options involve more complex routing configurations or custom functions that increase operational overhead.

answers.content: Create a CloudFront function that validates each HTTP response code that the ALB returns. Create an S3 static website in an S3 bucket. Upload the custom error page to the S3 bucket as a failover. Update the function to read the S3 bucket and to serve the error page to the end users.
answers.explanation: Using a CloudFront function to validate HTTP response codes and serve S3 content requires custom code and complexity, increasing operational overhead.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate an application to AWS. The application runs as a Docker container and uses an NFS version 4 file sharA solutions architect must design a secure and scalable containerized solution that does not require provisioning or management of the underlying infrastructurWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Deploy the application containers by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch typUse Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for shared storagReference the EFS file system ID, container mount point, and EFS authorization IAM role in the ECS task definition.
answers.explanation: Amazon ECS with Fargate launch type provides a serverless container management solution, eliminating the need to manage underlying infrastructurAmazon EFS supports NFS version 4 and is a fully managed shared file system designed for scalability and secure multi-client access. ECS task definitions support referencing EFS file system IDs and IAM roles for secure authentication, adhering to security best practices. Using managed services like ECS Fargate and Amazon EFS aligns with AWS best practices to avoid custom infrastructure management.

answers.content: Deploy the application containers by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch typUse Amazon FSx for Lustre for shared storagReference the FSx for Lustre file system ID, container mount point, and FSx for Lustre authorization IAM role in the ECS task definition.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is not designed for NFS version 4 and is optimized for high-performance computing, not typical NFS workloads; thus it does not meet the NFS v4 requirement.

answers.content: Deploy the application containers by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch type and auto scaling turned on. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for shared storagMount the EFS file system on the ECS container instances. Add the EFS authorization IAM role to the EC2 instance profile.
answers.explanation: Using ECS with EC2 launch type requires managing and provisioning the underlying infrastructure, which the question explicitly aims to avoid.

answers.content: Deploy the application containers by using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch type and auto scaling turned on. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes with Multi-Attach enabled for shared storagAttach the EBS volumes to ECS container instances. Add the EBS authorization IAM role to an EC2 instance profile.
answers.explanation: Amazon EBS volumes are block storage and not designed as shared file systems across multiple instances or containers; also, managing EC2 instances contradicts the requirement to avoid provisioning infrastructure.

questions.content: A company is running an application in the AWS Cloud. The core business logic is running on a set of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the EC2 instances. Amazon Route 53 record api.example.com is pointing to the ALB. The company's development team makes major updates to the business logic. The company has a rule that when changes are deployed, only 10% of customers can receive the new logic during a testing window. A customer must use the same version of the business logic during the testing window. How should the company deploy the updates to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a second ALB, and deploy the new logic to a set of EC2 instances in a new Auto Scaling group. Configure the ALB to distribute traffic to the EC2 instances. Update the Route 53 record to use weighted routing, and point the record to both of the ALBs.
answers.explanation: Creating a second ALB and updating Route 53 with weighted routing adds unnecessary complexity and does not leverage ALB weighted routing and stickiness features.

answers.content: Create a second target group that is referenced by the ALDeploy the new logic to EC2 instances in this new target group. Update the ALB listener rule to use weighted target groups. Configure ALB target group stickiness.
answers.explanation: Creating a second target group within the existing ALB and deploying the new logic to EC2 instances in that target group allows traffic distribution via weighted target groups, meeting the requirement to send only 10% of customers to the new version. Configuring ALB target group stickiness ensures that a customer uses the same version of the business logic during the testing window, satisfying the session consistency requirement. This approach uses managed AWS services (ALB weighted target groups and stickiness) and avoids creating additional ALBs or complex routing outside of ALB's native capabilities.

answers.content: Create a new launch configuration for the Auto Scaling group. Specify the launch configuration to use the AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy, and set the MaxBatchSize option to 10. Replace the launch configuration on the Auto Scaling group. Deploy the changes.
answers.explanation: Using AutoScalingRollingUpdate with MaxBatchSize 10 is a rolling deployment strategy but does not guarantee only 10% of customers receive new logic nor session stickiness during testing.

answers.content: Create a second Auto Scaling group that is referenced by the ALB. Deploy the new logic on a set of EC2 instances in this new Auto Scaling group. Change the ALB routing algorithm to least outstanding requests (LOR). Configure ALB session stickiness.
answers.explanation: Changing ALB routing to least outstanding requests (LOR) does not control percentage-based traffic distribution, and session stickiness alone without weighted routing cannot limit to 10% customers.

questions.content: A company is using AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts. For security purposes, the company requires the creation of an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that enables integration with a third-party alerting system in all the Organizations member accounts. A solutions architect used an AWS CloudFormation template to create the SNS topic and stack sets to automate the deployment of CloudFormation stacks. Trusted access has been enabled in Organizations. What should the solutions architect do to deploy the CloudFormation StackSets in all AWS accounts?
