answers.content: Create a stack set in the Organizations member accounts. Use service-managed permissions. Set deployment options to deploy to an organization. Use CloudFormation StackSets drift detection.
answers.explanation: Duplicate key in the list, see explanation under the first A.

answers.content: Create stacks in the Organizations member accounts. Use self-service permissions. Set deployment options to deploy to an organization. Enable the CloudFormation StackSets automatic deployment.
answers.explanation: Self-service permissions require manual IAM role management in each account and don't leverage service-managed permissions with Organizations integration.

answers.content: Create a stack set in the Organizations management account. Use service-managed permissions. Set deployment options to deploy to the organization. Enable CloudFormation StackSets automatic deployment.
answers.explanation: Using service-managed permissions allows management of IAM roles automatically across all accounts, removing the need to create roles in each member account. Enabling deployment options to deploy to the organization ensures the CloudFormation stack set is deployed to all current member accounts. Enabling CloudFormation StackSets automatic deployment ensures that the stack sets will also be deployed automatically to any new accounts added to the organization in the futurService-managed permissions paired with AWS Organizations integration is the recommended and secure AWS best practice for managing StackSets at scale.

answers.content: Create stacks in the Organizations management account. Use service-managed permissions. Set deployment options to deploy to the organization. Enable CloudFormation StackSets drift detection.
answers.explanation: Creating stacks in the management account without using stack sets and choosing service-managed permissions contradicts the deployment scope and best practice.

questions.content: A company is storing data on premises on a Windows file server. The company produces 5 GB of new data daily. The company migrated part of its Windows-based workload to AWS and needs the data to be available on a file system in the cloud. The company already has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and AWS. Which data migration strategy should the company use?

answers.content: Use the file gateway option in AWS Storage Gateway to replace the existing Windows file server, and point the existing file share to the new file gateway.
answers.explanation: File Gateway does not natively support providing a fully managed cloud file system accessible concurrently with on-premises systems, it acts more as a cache and gateway rather than a full replacement file server in the cloud.

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync to schedule a daily task to replicate data between the on-premises Windows file server and Amazon FSx.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is designed to replicate data efficiently between on-premises storage and AWS managed file systems such as Amazon FSx. Amazon FSx supports Windows-based file workloads, making it suitable for migrating data from a Windows file server. Using AWS DataSync with Amazon FSx leverages managed services for efficient, secure, and scalable data transfer. This approach fits with the existing Direct Connect connection, which provides a dedicated network path with high bandwidth and low latency.

answers.content: Use AWS Data Pipeline to schedule a daily task to replicate data between the on-premises Windows file server and Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).
answers.explanation: AWS Data Pipeline is primarily an orchestration service for data workflows, not optimized for file-based data replication between on-premises and AWS file systems.

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync to schedule a daily task to replicate data between the on-premises Windows file server and Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is not optimized for Windows workloads; Amazon FSx is the preferred managed service for Windows file systems.

questions.content: A company has created an OU in AWS Organizations for each of its engineering teams. Each OU owns multiple AWS accounts. The organization has hundreds of AWS accounts. A solutions architect must design a solution so that each OU can view a breakdown of usage costs across its AWS accounts. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) for each OU by using AWS Resource Access Manager. Allow each team to visualize the CUR through an Amazon QuickSight dashboard.
answers.explanation: Creating separate CURs per OU with AWS Resource Access Manager adds unnecessary complexity, and AWS Resource Access Manager is not intended for CUR sharing.

answers.content: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) from the AWS Organizations management account. Allow each team to visualize the CUR through an Amazon QuickSight dashboard.
answers.explanation: Creating a single AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) from the AWS Organizations management account provides centralized cost data aggregation for all member accounts in the organization. Using the management account CUR allows teams to view their usage costs across multiple accounts within their OU without needing to create and manage multiple reports. Visualizing the CUR through Amazon QuickSight enables scalable, customizable dashboards for each team to analyze costs. This method aligns with best practices for centralized management and access control in a multi-account AWS Organization environment.

answers.content: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) in each AWS Organizations member account. Allow each team to visualize the CUR through an Amazon QuickSight dashboard.
answers.explanation: Creating a CUR in each member account is inefficient and difficult to manage for hundreds of accounts, violating best practices for centralization.

answers.content: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) by using AWS Systems Manager. Allow each team to visualize the CUR through Systems Manager OpsCenter dashboards.
answers.explanation: AWS Systems Manager is not designed for generating or visualizing Cost and Usage Reports, making this choice incorrect.

questions.content: A company is hosting a monolithic REST-based API for a mobile app on five Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets of a VPC. Mobile clients connect to the API by using a domain name that is hosted on Amazon Route 53. The company has created a Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy with the IP addresses of all the EC2 instances. Recently, the app has been overwhelmed by large and sudden increases to traffic. The app has not been able to keep up with the traffic. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution so that the app can handle the new and varying load. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Separate the API into individual AWS Lambda functions. Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API with Lambda integration for the backend. Update the Route 53 record to point to the API Gateway API.
answers.explanation: Re-architecting into Lambda and API Gateway involves significant operational overhead and changes, not minimal operational overhead.

answers.content: Containerize the API logic. Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Run the containers in the cluster by using Amazon EC2. Create a Kubernetes ingress. Update the Route 53 record to point to the Kubernetes ingress.
answers.explanation: Creating an EKS cluster adds operational complexity and overhead contrary to the requirement for least overhead.

answers.content: Create an Auto Scaling group. Place all the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to perform scaling actions that are based on CPU utilization. Create an AWS Lambda function that reacts to Auto Scaling group changes and updates the Route 53 record.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function to update Route 53 based on Auto Scaling events adds unnecessary custom automation complexity.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the API. Move the EC2 instances to private subnets in the VPC. Add the EC2 instances as targets for the ALB. Update the Route 53 record to point to the ALB.
answers.explanation: An Application Load Balancer (ALB) can efficiently distribute incoming traffic across multiple EC2 instances, handling varying load seamlessly. Moving EC2 instances to private subnets enhances security by not exposing them directly to the internet. Updating the Route 53 record to point to the ALB leverages a managed service for load balancing, reducing operational overhead. Using an ALB avoids the complexity of managing scaling logic via Lambda functions or Kubernetes, adhering to managed AWS service preference.

questions.content: An enterprise company wants to allow its developers to purchase third-party software through AWS MarketplacThe company uses an AWS Organizations account structure with full features enabled, and has a shared services account in each organizational unit (OU) that will be used by procurement managers. The procurement team's policy indicates that developers should be able to obtain third-party software from an approved list only and use Private Marketplace in AWS Marketplace to achieve this requirement. The procurement team wants administration of Private Marketplace to be restricted to a role named procurement-manager-role, which could be assumed by procurement managers. Other IAM users, groups, roles, and account administrators in the company should be denied Private Marketplace administrative access. What is the MOST efficient way to design an architecture to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an IAM role named procurement-manager-role in all AWS accounts in the organization. Add the PowerUserAccess managed policy to the rolApply an inline policy to all IAM users and roles in every AWS account to deny permissions on the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy.
answers.explanation: Using PowerUserAccess is overly broad and applying inline deny policies per user/account is complex and less secure than SCP-based controls.

answers.content: Create an IAM role named procurement-manager-role in all AWS accounts in the organization. Add the AdministratorAccess managed policy to the rolDefine a permissions boundary with the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy and attach it to all the developer roles.
answers.explanation: AdministratorAccess is excessive for marketplace administration and using permissions boundaries on developer roles is not aligned with restricting admin access centrally.

answers.content: Create an IAM role named procurement-manager-role in all the shared services accounts in the organization. Add the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy to the rolCreate an organization root-level SCP to deny permissions to administer Private Marketplace to everyone except the role named procurement-manager-rolCreate another organization root-level SCP to deny permissions to create an IAM role named procurement-manager-role to everyone in the organization.
answers.explanation: Creating the procurement-manager-role only in the shared services accounts aligns with the use of shared services accounts for procurement managers. Attaching the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy to this role delegates Private Marketplace administration efficiently to procurement managers. Using an organization root-level Service Control Policy (SCP) to deny Private Marketplace administrative permissions to all except this role ensures security and centralizes control, preventing unauthorized access in any account. An additional SCP denying creation of the procurement-manager-role prevents privilege escalation or role spoofing, maintaining strict security boundaries. This approach leverages AWS Organizations SCPs and managed policies for centralized and secure permission management, consistent with AWS best practices.

answers.content: Create an IAM role named procurement-manager-role in all AWS accounts that will be used by developers. Add the AWSPrivateMarketplaceAdminFullAccess managed policy to the rolCreate an SCP in Organizations to deny permissions to administer Private Marketplace to everyone except the role named procurement-manager-rolApply the SCP to all the shared services accounts in the organization.
answers.explanation: Creating procurement-manager-role in all developer accounts and applying SCP only to shared services accounts is inconsistent with centralizing procurement management and SCP scope.

questions.content: A company has 50 AWS accounts that are members of an organization in AWS Organizations. Each account contains multiple VPCs. The company wants to use AWS Transit Gateway to establish connectivity between the VPCs in each member account. Each time a new member account is created, the company wants to automate the process of creating a new VPC and a transit gateway attachment. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: From the management account, share the transit gateway with member accounts by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) is the supported method to share a transit gateway across accounts in AWS Organizations, enabling member accounts to create attachments to the shared transit gateway.

answers.content: From the management account, share the transit gateway with member accounts by using an AWS Organizations SCP.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Service Control Policies (SCPs) define permission guardrails and cannot be used to share resources such as a transit gateway.

answers.content: Launch an AWS CloudFormation stack set from the management account that automatically creates a new VPC and a VPC transit gateway attachment in a member account. Associate the attachment with the transit gateway in the management account by using the transit gateway ID.
answers.explanation: correct because using CloudFormation StackSets from the management account allows automatic creation of a VPC and transit gateway attachment in each new member account, enabling consistent and automated deployment.

answers.content: Launch an AWS CloudFormation stack set from the management account that automatically creates a new VPC and a peering transit gateway attachment in a member account. Share the attachment with the transit gateway in the management account by using a transit gateway service-linked role.
answers.explanation: incorrect because transit gateway peering attachments are used to connect separate transit gateways, not to attach VPCs to a shared transit gateway.

answers.content: From the management account, share the transit gateway with member accounts by using AWS Service Catalog.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Service Catalog is used to manage approved products and does not provide native functionality to share a transit gateway resource across accounts.

questions.content: A company that has multiple AWS accounts is using AWS Organizations. The company's AWS accounts host VPCs, Amazon EC2 instances, and containers. The company's compliance team has deployed a security tool in each VPC where the company has deployments. The security tools run on EC2 instances and send information to the AWS account that is dedicated for the compliance team. The company has tagged all the compliance-related resources with a key of "costCenter" and a value or "compliance". The company wants to identify the cost of the security tools that are running on the EC2 instances so that the company can charge the compliance team's AWS account. The cost calculation must be as accurate as possiblWhat should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: In the management account of the organization, activate the costCenter user-defined tag. Configure monthly AWS Cost and Usage Reports to save to an Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Use the tag breakdown in the report to obtain the total cost for the costCenter tagged resources.
answers.explanation: Activating user-defined tags in the management account ensures they appear in cost allocation reports and Cost Explorer. Configuring monthly AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) to save in an S3 bucket provides detailed and accurate cost data. Using the tag breakdown in the CUR allows precise cost allocation for resources tagged with costCenter=compliancThis approach uses managed AWS services and follows best practices for cost allocation and tagging.

answers.content: In the member accounts of the organization, activate the costCenter user-defined tag. Configure monthly AWS Cost and Usage Reports to save to an Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Schedule a monthly AWS Lambda function to retrieve the reports and calculate the total cost for the costCenter tagged resources.
answers.explanation: Activating tags in member accounts is insufficient because tags must be activated in the management account for Cost Explorer and CUR; also, using a Lambda to process CUR is unnecessary because CUR provides the needed breakdown.

answers.content: In the member accounts of the organization activate the costCenter user-defined tag. From the management account, schedule a monthly AWS Cost and Usage Report. Use the tag breakdown in the report to calculate the total cost for the costCenter tagged resources.
answers.explanation: Activating tags in member accounts is incorrect; tags must be activated in the management account to appear in reports.

answers.content: Create a custom report in the organization view in AWS Trusted Advisor. Configure the report to generate a monthly billing summary for the costCenter tagged resources in the compliance team's AWS account.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor does not support cost allocation reporting or tag-based billing summaries; it is not designed for such custom billing reports.

questions.content: A company has registered 10 new domain names. The company uses the domains for online marketing. The company needs a solution that will redirect online visitors to a specific URL for each domain. All domains and target URLs are defined in a JSON document. All DNS records are managed by Amazon Route 53. A solutions architect must implement a redirect service that accepts HTTP and HTTPS requests. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational effort? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a dynamic webpage that runs on an Amazon EC2 instancConfigure the webpage to use the JSON document in combination with the event message to look up and respond with a redirect URL.
answers.explanation: incorrect because running a dynamic webpage on EC2 introduces server management, scaling, patching, and maintenance overhead, which is unnecessary for a simple redirect service.

answers.content: Create an Application Load Balancer that includes HTTP and HTTPS listeners.
answers.explanation: incorrect because an Application Load Balancer requires backing compute resources and ongoing management, increasing operational effort compared to a fully serverless solution.

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the JSON document in combination with the event message to look up and respond with a redirect URL.
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Lambda can process the JSON document and dynamically return HTTP 301/302 redirect responses without managing servers.

answers.content: Use an Amazon API Gateway API with a custom domain to publish an AWS Lambda function.
answers.explanation: correct because Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain provides a fully managed HTTPS endpoint that integrates directly with Lambda and supports both HTTP and HTTPS requests.

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy a Lambda@Edge function.
answers.explanation: incorrect because CloudFront with Lambda@Edge adds additional configuration complexity and is not required for a simple redirect service.

answers.content: Create an SSL certificate by using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Include the domains as Subject Alternative Names.
answers.explanation: correct because an ACM certificate with the domains as Subject Alternative Names enables HTTPS support for all registered domains with minimal management overhead.

questions.content: A company is storing data in several Amazon DynamoDB tables. A solutions architect must use a serverless architecture to make the data accessible publicly through a simple API over HTTPS. The solution must scale automatically in response to demand. Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure this API with direct integrations to DynamoDB by using API Gateway's AWS integration type.
answers.explanation: correct because API Gateway REST API supports direct AWS service integration with DynamoDB, enabling a fully serverless HTTPS API without Lambda and with automatic scaling.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API. Configure this API with direct integrations to Dynamo DB by using API Gateway's AWS integration type.
answers.explanation: incorrect because API Gateway HTTP APIs do not support direct AWS service integrations with DynamoDB in the same way REST APIs do for this use case.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API. Configure this API with integrations to AWS Lambda functions that return data from the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: correct because API Gateway HTTP API integrated with Lambda provides a fully serverless, automatically scaling HTTPS endpoint that can retrieve data from DynamoDB.

answers.content: Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure this accelerator with AWS Lambda@Edge function integrations that return data from the DynamoDB tables.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Global Accelerator with Lambda@Edge is not designed to expose DynamoDB through a simple public API and introduces unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Create a Network Load Balancer. Configure listener rules to forward requests to the appropriate AWS Lambda functions.
answers.explanation: incorrect because a Network Load Balancer cannot directly invoke Lambda functions in this manner and would not provide a fully serverless API architecture.

questions.content: A company is developing a new service that will be accessed using TCP on a static port. A solutions architect must ensure that the service is highly available, has redundancy across Availability Zones, and is accessible using the DNS name my.service.com, which is publicly accessiblThe service must use fixed address assignments so other companies can add the addresses to their allow lists. Assuming that resources are deployed in multiple Availability Zones in a single Region, which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create Amazon EC2 instances with an Elastic IP address for each instancCreate a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the static TCP port. Register EC2 instances with the NLB. Create a new name server record set named my.service.com, and assign the Elastic IP addresses of the EC2 instances to the record set. Provide the Elastic IP addresses of the EC2 instances to the other companies to add to their allow lists.
answers.explanation: Assigning Elastic IPs directly to each EC2 instance does not provide load balancing or high availability and directly assigning EIPs to a DNS record set while also using an NLB is inconsistent.

answers.content: Create an Amazon ECS cluster and a service definition for the application. Create and assign public IP addresses for the ECS cluster. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the TCP port. Create a target group and assign the ECS cluster name to the NLCreate a new A record set named my.service.com, and assign the public IP addresses of the ECS cluster to the record set. Provide the public IP addresses of the ECS cluster to the other companies to add to their allow lists.
answers.explanation: Assigning public IP addresses to the ECS cluster and mapping them directly to DNS is not a best practice and does not provide fixed IPs or proper load balancing with target groups.

answers.content: Create Amazon EC2 instances for the servicCreate one Elastic IP address for each Availability ZonCreate a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the assigned TCP port. Assign the Elastic IP addresses to the NLB for each Availability ZonCreate a target group and register the EC2 instances with the NLB. Create a new A (alias) record set named my.service.com, and assign the NLB DNS name to the record set.
answers.explanation: Using Elastic IP addresses assigned to the Network Load Balancer preserves fixed IP addresses for external allow listing. Registering EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones with the NLB ensures high availability and redundancy. Creating an A (alias) record pointing to the NLB DNS name allows for default load balancing and accessibility via my.service.com. The Network Load Balancer supports static IP addresses and TCP protocol, which is required for the service.

answers.content: Create an Amazon ECS cluster and a service definition for the application. Create and assign public IP address for each host in the cluster. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and expose the static TCP port. Create a target group and assign the ECS service definition name to the ALB. Create a new CNAME record set and associate the public IP addresses to the record set. Provide the Elastic IP addresses of the Amazon EC2 instances to the other companies to add to their allow lists.
answers.explanation: Application Load Balancers do not support TCP protocol, and creating a CNAME record pointing to public IPs is invalid since CNAMEs should point to DNS names; also, exposing ECS hosts directly via public IPs is less secure and does not offer fixed IPs.

questions.content: A company is running a data-intensive application on AWS. The application runs on a cluster of hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances. A shared file system also runs on several EC2 instances that store 200 TB of data. The application reads and modifies the data on the shared file system and generates a report. The job runs once monthly, reads a subset of the files from the shared file system, and takes about 72 hours to completThe compute instances scale in an Auto Scaling group, but the instances that host the shared file system run continuously. The compute and storage instances are all in the same AWS Region. A solutions architect needs to reduce costs by replacing the shared file system instances. The file system must provide high performance access to the needed data for the duration of the 72-hour run. Which solution will provide the LARGEST overall cost reduction while meeting these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to an Amazon S3 bucket that uses the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Before the job runs each month, use Amazon FSx for Lustre to create a new file system with the data from Amazon S3 by using lazy loading. Use the new file system as the shared storage for the duration of the job. Delete the file system when the job is complete.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon S3 with S3 Intelligent-Tiering reduces costs for data storage by automatically optimizing storage costs based on access patterns. Amazon FSx for Lustre can be created on-demand using lazy loading from S3, providing high-performance shared file system access for the 72-hour job duration. Deleting the FSx Lustre file system after the job completes avoids the cost of continuously running shared file system instances. This approach aligns with the best practice of using managed AWS services for shared storage and avoiding persistent infrastructure costs.

answers.content: Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to a large Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with Multi-Attach enabled. Attach the EBS volume to each of the instances by using a user data script in the Auto Scaling group launch templatUse the EBS volume as the shared storage for the duration of the job. Detach the EBS volume when the job is complete
answers.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach is limited in scalability and requires manual attachment; it is not designed as a shared file system and can be costly for 200 TB storage.

answers.content: Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to an Amazon S3 bucket that uses the S3 Standard storage class. Before the job runs each month, use Amazon FSx for Lustre to create a new file system with the data from Amazon S3 by using batch loading. Use the new file system as the shared storage for the duration of the job. Delete the file system when the job is complete.
answers.explanation: Using S3 Standard with FSx Lustre batch loading can increase upfront cost and complexity compared to lazy loading; S3 Intelligent-Tiering offers better cost optimization.

answers.content: Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Before the job runs each month, use AWS Storage Gateway to create a file gateway with the data from Amazon S3. Use the file gateway as the shared storage for the job. Delete the file gateway when the job is complete.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway introduces operational overhead and is not optimized for large-scale, temporary high-performance shared access compared to FSx for Lustre.

questions.content: A software company has deployed an application that consumes a REST API by using Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon DynamoDB tablThe application is showing an increase in the number of errors during PUT requests. Most of the PUT calls come from a small number of clients that are authenticated with specific API keys. A solutions architect has identified that a large number of the PUT requests originate from one client. The API is noncritical, and clients can tolerate retries of unsuccessful calls. However, the errors are displayed to customers and are causing damage to the API's reputation. What should the solutions architect recommend to improve the customer experience?

answers.content: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and irregular variation in the client application. Ensure that the errors are caught and handled with descriptive error messages.
answers.explanation: Retry logic in the client does not prevent errors caused by requests overwhelming the API and does not address the source of errors effectively.

answers.content: Implement API throttling through a usage plan at the API Gateway level. Ensure that the client application handles code 429 replies without error.
answers.explanation: API Gateway throttling can protect the API from being overwhelmed by too many requests from one client. Throttle limits cause API Gateway to return 429 Too Many Requests errors, which clients can handle by retrying appropriately. This solution aligns with the fact that throttles are applied as targets to limit request rates and that clients can implement retry logic for 429 errors. Since the API is noncritical and clients can tolerate retries, throttling improves customer experience by preventing overload and giving clients clear guidance to retry.

answers.content: Turn on API caching to enhance responsiveness for the production stagRun 10-minute load tests. Verify that the cache capacity is appropriate for the workload.
answers.explanation: API caching is unlikely to reduce errors for PUT requests since these requests modify data and caching is primarily for GET requests.

answers.content: Implement reserved concurrency at the Lambda function level to provide the resources that are needed during sudden increases in traffic.
answers.explanation: Reserved concurrency in Lambda manages execution capacity but does not directly prevent API Gateway from being overwhelmed or reduce client-generated traffic spikes.

questions.content: A company is using an on-premises Active Directory service for user authentication. The company wants to use the same authentication service to sign in to the company's AWS accounts, which are using AWS Organizations. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connectivity already exists between the on-premises environment and all the company's AWS accounts. The company's security policy requires conditional access to the accounts based on user groups and roles. User identities must be managed in a single location. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to connect to Active Directory by using SAML 2.0. Enable automatic provisioning by using the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) v2.0 protocol. Grant access to the AWS accounts by using attribute-based access controls (ABACs).
answers.explanation: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) supports integration with on-premises Active Directory via SAML 2.0, allowing the company to use their existing AD for authentication. Automatic provisioning using SCIM v2.0 allows for centralized identity management, meeting the requirement of managing user identities in a single location. Attribute-based access control (ABAC) supports conditional access based on user groups and roles as required by the security policy. AWS IAM Identity Center is a managed AWS service purpose-built for single sign-on and integrates well with AWS Organizations and multiple accounts.

answers.content: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) by using IAM Identity Center as an identity sourcEnable automatic provisioning by using the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) v2.0 protocol. Grant access to the AWS accounts by using IAM Identity Center permission sets.
answers.explanation: Using IAM Identity Center as an identity source bypasses on-premises AD; does not meet the requirement to use the existing AD for authentication.

answers.content: In one of the company's AWS accounts, configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to use a SAML 2.0 identity provider. Provision IAM users that are mapped to the federated users. Grant access that corresponds to appropriate groups in Active Directory. Grant access to the required AWS accounts by using cross-account IAM users.
answers.explanation: Managing IAM users and cross-account IAM users is complex and does not provide centralized identity management or conditional access via attribute-based controls as well as IAM Identity Center.

answers.content: In one of the company's AWS accounts, configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to use an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider. Provision IAM roles that grant access to the AWS account for the federated users that correspond to appropriate groups in Active Directory. Grant access to the required AWS accounts by using cross-account IAM roles.
answers.explanation: Using an OIDC identity provider is less aligned with on-premises Active Directory and does not leverage managed AWS SSO integration for simplified conditional access and identity management.

questions.content: A company has a serverless application comprised of Amazon CloudFront, Amazon API Gateway, and AWS Lambda functions. The current deployment process of the application code is to create a new version number of the Lambda function and run an AWS CLI script to updatIf the new function version has errors, another CLI script reverts by deploying the previous working version of the function. The company would like to decrease the time to deploy new versions of the application logic provided by the Lambda functions, and also reduce the time to detect and revert when errors are identified. How can this be accomplished?

answers.content: Create and deploy nested AWS CloudFormation stacks with the parent stack consisting of the AWS CloudFront distribution and API Gateway, and the child stack containing the Lambda function. For changes to Lambda, create an AWS CloudFormation change set and deploy; if errors are triggered, revert the AWS CloudFormation change set to the previous version.
answers.explanation: CloudFormation change sets are not optimized for rapid Lambda version traffic shifting and rollback and require manual intervention.

answers.content: Use AWS SAM and built-in AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the new Lambda version, gradually shift traffic to the new version, and use pre-traffic and post-traffic test functions to verify codRollback if Amazon CloudWatch alarms are triggered.
answers.explanation: AWS SAM with AWS CodeDeploy natively supports gradual traffic shifting between Lambda versions, enabling fast detection and rollback of errors. Using pre-traffic and post-traffic test functions integrated with CodeDeploy provides automated verification before and after deployment. CodeDeploy can rollback automatically based on Amazon CloudWatch alarms, improving speed and reliability of rollback. This approach uses managed AWS services built for deployment and rollback, aligning with security and operational best practices.

answers.content: Refactor the AWS CLI scripts into a single script that deploys the new Lambda version. When deployment is completed, the script tests executIf errors are detected, revert to the previous Lambda version.
answers.explanation: Refactoring CLI scripts does not leverage managed deployment services which provide automated traffic shifting and monitoring.

answers.content: Create and deploy an AWS CloudFormation stack that consists of a new API Gateway endpoint that references the new Lambda version. Change the CloudFront origin to the new API Gateway endpoint, monitor errors and if detected, change the AWS CloudFront origin to the previous API Gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: Changing API Gateway endpoints and CloudFront origins is manual and slow, introducing complexity and delay in rollback.

questions.content: A company with global offices has a single 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to a single AWS Region. The company's on-premises network uses the connection to communicate with the company's resources in the AWS Cloud. The connection has a single private virtual interface that connects to a single VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution that adds a redundant Direct Connect connection in the same Region. The solution also must provide connectivity to other Regions through the same pair of Direct Connect connections as the company expands into other Regions. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Provision a Direct Connect gateway. Delete the existing private virtual interface from the existing connection. Create the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new private virtual interface on each connection, and connect both private virtual interfaces to the Direct Connect gateway. Connect the Direct Connect gateway to the single VPC.
answers.explanation: Using a Direct Connect gateway enables redundant Direct Connect connections in the same Region and supports connectivity to multiple VPCs across different Regions through the same Direct Connect connections. Deleting the existing single private virtual interface and creating new private virtual interfaces on both connections connected to the Direct Connect gateway aligns with best practices for redundancy and scalability. The Direct Connect gateway allows for multi-Region connectivity, meeting the requirement to expand access as the company grows. Managed AWS services like Direct Connect gateway are preferred for simplifying and securing connectivity management.

answers.content: Keep the existing private virtual interfacCreate the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new private virtual interface on the new connection, and connect the new private virtual interface to the single VPC.
answers.explanation: Does not provide redundancy on the existing connection for failover or multi-Region connectivity through a single Direct Connect gateway.

answers.content: Keep the existing private virtual interfacCreate the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new public virtual interface on the new connection, and connect the new public virtual interface to the single VPC.
answers.explanation: A public virtual interface cannot connect to a private VPC; it is used for public AWS service access, so it does not meet the private connectivity requirement.

answers.content: Provision a transit gateway. Delete the existing private virtual interface from the existing connection. Create the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new private virtual interface on each connection, and connect both private virtual interfaces to the transit gateway. Associate the transit gateway with the single VPC.
answers.explanation: Transit gateway is used for inter-VPC connectivity rather than directly connecting Direct Connect virtual interfaces; also, Direct Connect gateways are the appropriate service for multi-Region Direct Connect connections.

questions.content: A company used Amazon EC2 instances to deploy a web fleet to host a blog sitThe EC2 instances are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and are configured in an Auto Scaling group. The web application stores all blog content on an Amazon EFS volumThe company recently added a feature for bloggers to add video to their posts, attracting 10 times the previous user traffic. At peak times of day, users report buffering and timeout issues while attempting to reach the site or watch videos. Which is the MOST cost-efficient and scalable deployment that will resolve the issues for users?

answers.content: Reconfigure Amazon EFS to enable maximum I/O.
answers.explanation: Reconfiguring EFS for maximum I/O does not address the core scalability issues and is less cost-efficient than using S3 and CloudFront for video delivery.

answers.content: Update the blog site to use instance store volumes for storagCopy the site contents to the volumes at launch and to Amazon S3 at shutdown.
answers.explanation: Using instance store volumes is ephemeral and not persistent, which is inappropriate for storing blog content and videos, and managing syncing at launch and shutdown is operationally complex.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Point the distribution to an S3 bucket, and migrate the videos from EFS to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a managed content delivery network service that provides caching and lower latency for delivering content globally, which improves video streaming performance and reduces buffering. Using Amazon S3 to store videos is cost-efficient and scalable compared to EFS, which is not optimized for high-throughput video delivery at scalMigrating videos from EFS to S3 and distributing via CloudFront aligns with AWS best practices for scalable, high-throughput media delivery. CloudFront reduces load on the ALB and EC2 instances by serving cached content from edge locations, improving user experience during peak traffic.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution for all site contents, and point the distribution at the ALB.
answers.explanation: Setting up CloudFront only in front of the ALB does not optimize video delivery; the videos remain on EFS, which is not ideal for high-throughput content delivery.

questions.content: A security engineer determined that an existing application retrieves credentials to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database from an encrypted file in Amazon S3. For the next version of the application, the security engineer wants to implement the following application design changes to improve security: The database must use strong, randomly generated passwords stored in a secure AWS managed servicThe application resources must be deployed through AWS CloudFormation. The application must rotate credentials for the database every 90 days. A solutions architect will generate a CloudFormation template to deploy the application. Which resources specified in the CloudFormation template will meet the security engineer's requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answers.content: Generate the database password as a secret resource using AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function resource to rotate the database password. Specify a Secrets Manager RotationSchedule resource to rotate the database password every 90 days.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the preferred AWS managed service for managing database credentials securely. Secrets Manager supports storing strong, randomly generated passwords and built-in rotation with low operational overhead. Using a Secrets Manager RotationSchedule resource to trigger automatic rotation every 90 days aligns with requirements and security best practices. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store does not natively support credential rotation schedules and requires more manual intervention.

answers.content: Generate the database password as a SecureString parameter type using AWS Systems Manager Parameter StorCreate an AWS Lambda function resource to rotate the database password. Specify a Parameter Store RotationSchedule resource to rotate the database password every 90 days.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store does not have a native RotationSchedule resource; rotation requires more custom management increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Generate the database password as a secret resource using AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function resource to rotate the database password. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule resource to trigger the Lambda function password rotation every 90 days.
answers.explanation: Using EventBridge scheduled rule to trigger rotation adds extra complexity compared to automated rotation in Secrets Manager.

answers.content: Generate the database password as a SecureString parameter type using AWS Systems Manager Parameter StorSpecify an AWS AppSync DataSource resource to automatically rotate the database password every 90 days.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store combined with an AppSync DataSource for rotation is not a standard or supported way to rotate secrets and lacks built-in rotation capability.

questions.content: A company uses an on-premises data analytics platform. The system is highly available in a fully redundant configuration across 12 servers in the company's data center. The system runs scheduled jobs, both hourly and daily, in addition to one-time requests from users. Scheduled jobs can take between 20 minutes and 2 hours to finish running and have tight SLAs. The scheduled jobs account for 65% of the system usagUser jobs typically finish running in less than 5 minutes and have no SLA. The user jobs account for 35% of system usagDuring system failures, scheduled jobs must continue to meet SLAs. However, user jobs can be delayed. A solutions architect needs to move the system to Amazon EC2 instances and adopt a consumption-based model to reduce costs with no long-term commitments. The solution must maintain high availability and must not affect the SLAs. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Split the 12 instances across two Availability Zones in the chosen AWS Region. Run two instances in each Availability Zone as On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Run four instances in each Availability Zone as Spot Instances.
answers.explanation: Only two Availability Zones reduce fault tolerance compared to three Availability Zones.

answers.content: Split the 12 instances across three Availability Zones in the chosen AWS Region. In one of the Availability Zones, run all four instances as On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Run the remaining instances as Spot Instances.
answers.explanation: Concentrating all Capacity Reservations in one AZ creates a single point of failure for SLA-critical scheduled jobs.

answers.content: Split the 12 instances across three Availability Zones in the chosen AWS Region. Run two instances in each Availability Zone as On-Demand Instances with a Savings Plan. Run two instances in each Availability Zone as Spot Instances.
answers.explanation: Using Savings Plans implies long-term commitments, conflicting with the requirement for no long-term commitments.

answers.content: Split the 12 instances across three Availability Zones in the chosen AWS Region. Run three instances in each Availability Zone as On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Run one instance in each Availability Zone as a Spot Instance.
answers.explanation: Splitting instances across three Availability Zones maximizes high availability. Using three On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations per AZ ensures guaranteed compute capacity for scheduled jobs to meet tight SLAs during failures. Running one Spot Instance per AZ adds cost-effective capacity that can handle flexible user jobs which can be delayed. Capacity Reservations provide assured resources without long-term commitments, aligning with consumption-based cost reduction. This approach balances cost-effectiveness, guaranteed availability, and SLA adherence according to AWS best practices.

questions.content: A company is planning to store a large number of archived documents and make the documents available to employees through the corporate intranet. Employees will access the system by connecting through a client VPN service that is attached to a VPC. The data must not be accessible to the public. The documents that the company is storing are copies of data that is held on physical media elsewherThe number of requests will be low. Availability and speed of retrieval are not concerns of the company. Which solution will meet these requirements at the LOWEST cost?

answers.content: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket to use the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class as default. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Create an S3 interface endpoint. Configure the S3 bucket to allow access only through that endpoint.
answers.explanation: S3 One Zone-IA is more expensive than Glacier Deep Archive and less suited for long-term archival with low access frequency.

answers.content: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a web server. Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store the archived data in the EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA) storage class Configure the instance security groups to allow access only from private networks.
answers.explanation: Running an EC2 instance with EFS adds compute and storage costs and management overhead, making it more expensive than managed archival storage.

answers.content: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a web server Attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to store the archived data. Use the Cold HDD (sc1) volume typConfigure the instance security groups to allow access only from private networks.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 with EBS Cold HDD involves higher costs due to constant compute resource needs and does not provide as low cost or durable a storage solution as Glacier Deep Archive.

answers.content: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket to use the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class as default. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Create an S3 interface endpoint. Configure the S3 bucket to allow access only through that endpoint.
answers.explanation: Using an Amazon S3 bucket with the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class provides the lowest cost storage option for infrequently accessed data. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term archival data with very low cost, which aligns with the company's requirement where availability and speed are not concerns. Configuring the S3 bucket for website hosting and creating an S3 interface endpoint ensures that access is private and restricted to the VPC without exposing data to the public. This managed solution avoids running and maintaining EC2 instances, which incur higher costs and administrative overhead, and uses a storage class optimized for archival data instead of more expensive options.

questions.content: A company has a web application that allows users to upload short videos. The videos are stored on Amazon EBS volumes and analyzed by custom recognition software for categorization. The website contains static content that has variable traffic with peaks in certain months. The architecture consists of Amazon EC2 instances running in an Auto Scaling group for the web application and EC2 instances running in an Auto Scaling group to process an Amazon SQS queuThe company wants to re-architect the application to reduce operational overhead using AWS managed services where possible and remove dependencies on third-party softwarWhich solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Use Amazon ECS containers for the web application and Spot instances for the Auto Scaling group that processes the SQS queuReplace the custom software with Amazon Rekognition to categorize the videos.
answers.explanation: Uses Spot instances and ECS which still require managing container infrastructure; does not remove all operational overhead.

answers.content: Store the uploaded videos in Amazon EFS and mount the file system to the EC2 instances for the web application. Process the SQS queue with an AWS Lambda function that calls the Amazon Rekognition API to categorize the videos.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EFS and mounting it to EC2 instances maintains dependency on EC2 management and shared file system complexity.

answers.content: Host the web application in Amazon S3. Store the uploaded videos in Amazon S3. Use S3 event notification to publish events to the SQS queuProcess the SQS queue with an AWS Lambda function that calls the Amazon Rekognition API to categorize the videos.
answers.explanation: Hosting the web application and videos on Amazon S3 reduces operational overhead by using a fully managed service designed for static and media content. Using S3 event notifications to trigger processing aligns with event-driven architecture, simplifying integration with other AWS managed services. Processing the SQS queue with AWS Lambda removes the need to manage EC2 instances, thus reducing operational overhead. Replacing the custom software with Amazon Rekognition leverages managed AI services, eliminating dependencies on third-party software.

answers.content: Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the web application and launch a worker environment to process the SQS queuReplace the custom software with Amazon Rekognition to categorize the videos.
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk still requires managing EC2 instances and worker environments, so it does not minimize operational overhead as much as serverless options.

questions.content: A company has a monolithic application that is critical to the company's business. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Amazon Linux 2. The company's application team receives a directive from the legal department to back up the data from the instance's encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application team does not have the administrative SSH key pair for the instancThe application must continue to serve the users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Attach a role to the instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Use the AWS Systems Manager Session Manager option to gain access to the instance and run commands to copy data into Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: correct because attaching an IAM role with S3 permissions and using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager allows secure access to the instance without an SSH key, enabling data copy to S3 while the application continues running.

answers.content: Create an image of the instance with the reboot option turned on. Launch a new EC2 instance from the imagAttach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Creating a new instance with reboot option impacts application availability which violates the requirement to continue serving users.

answers.content: Take a snapshot of the EBS volume by using Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Copy the data to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: incorrect because an EBS snapshot stores data in Amazon S3 internally but does not make the data directly accessible in an S3 bucket as required.

answers.content: Create an image of the instancLaunch a new EC2 instance from the imagAttach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Creating a new instance without reboot still requires manual steps and may risk data consistency; less ideal than snapshot-based backup.

questions.content: A company with several AWS accounts is using AWS Organizations and service control policies (SCPs). An administrator created the following SCP and has attached it to an organizational unit (OU) that contains AWS account 1111-1111-1111: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02/image6.png] Developers working in account 1111-1111-1111 complain that they cannot create Amazon S3 buckets. How should the administrator address this problem?

answers.content: Add s3:CreateBucket with "Allow" effect to the SCP.
answers.explanation: SCPs only set maximum permission boundaries and do not grant permissions themselves, so if s3:CreateBucket is not allowed by the SCP, users cannot create buckets even if their IAM policies allow it. Adding s3:CreateBucket with an Allow effect to the SCP will enable users in the accounts under the OU to create S3 buckets as long as their IAM policies also allow it. Removing the SCP entirely or moving the account is less desirable than adjusting the SCP to allow necessary actions while maintaining governancInstructing developers to add permissions to IAM entities is ineffective if the SCP explicitly denies creating buckets.

answers.content: Remove the account from the OU, and attach the SCP directly to account 1111-1111-1111.
answers.explanation: Moving the account or attaching SCPs directly does not fix the lack of permission in the SCP itself and is less secure.

answers.content: Instruct the developers to add Amazon S3 permissions to their IAM entities.
answers.explanation: IAM policies cannot override SCP restrictions, so adding permissions there won't help if SCP denies the action.

answers.content: Remove the SCP from account 1111-1111-1111.
answers.explanation: Removing the SCP removes all guardrails and is not a best practice for managing permissions effectively.

questions.content: An AWS customer has a web application that runs on premises. The web application fetches data from a third-party API that is behind a firewall. The third party accepts only one public CIDR block in each client's allow list. The customer wants to migrate their web application to the AWS Cloud. The application will be hosted on a set of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC. The ALB is located in public subnets. The EC2 instances are located in private subnets. NAT gateways provide internet access to the private subnets. How should a solutions architect ensure that the web application can continue to call the third-party API after the migration?

answers.content: Associate a block of customer-owned public IP addresses to the VPC. Enable public IP addressing for public subnets in the VPC.
answers.explanation: Enabling public IP addressing for public subnets does not control outbound IP for instances in private subnets using NAT gateways.

answers.content: Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address block and assign them to the NAT gateways in the VPC.
answers.explanation: The third party requires allowing a single public CIDR block for the client's API calls. The web application runs in private subnets with NAT gateways providing internet access. Assigning Elastic IP addresses from a customer-owned block to NAT gateways ensures that outbound calls use these static, identifiable IPs. This meets the requirement of a fixed IP address range visible to the third party for allow listing while following AWS best practices.

answers.content: Create Elastic IP addresses from the block of customer-owned IP addresses. Assign the static Elastic IP addresses to the ALB.
answers.explanation: Elastic IPs cannot be assigned directly to an ALB; ALBs do not support static Elastic IP attachments.

answers.content: Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Set up AWS Global Accelerator to use Elastic IP addresses from the address block. Set the ALB as the accelerator endpoint.
answers.explanation: Global Accelerator is generally used for improving global availability and performance, not for specifying a fixed static IP block for NAT functionality or third-party API allow lists.

questions.content: A company's factory and automation applications are running in a single VPC. More than 20 applications run on a combination of Amazon EC2, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), and Amazon RDS. The company has software engineers spread across three teams. One of the three teams owns each application, and each time is responsible for the cost and performance of all of its applications. Team resources have tags that represent their application and team. The teams use IAM access for daily activities. The company needs to determine which costs on the monthly AWS bill are attributable to each application or team. The company also must be able to create reports to compare costs from the last 12 months and to help forecast costs for the next 12 months. A solutions architect must recommend an AWS Billing and Cost Management solution that provides these cost reports. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Activate the user-define cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team.
answers.explanation: correct because activating user-defined cost allocation tags (for application and team) allows AWS to include those tags in cost reports and attribute spending accurately.

answers.content: Activate the AWS generated cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS-generated tags do not represent custom application or team ownership unless specifically created as user-defined tags.

answers.content: Create a cost category for each application in Billing and Cost Management.
answers.explanation: incorrect because cost categories are optional and not required when user-defined cost allocation tags already provide the needed cost breakdown.

answers.content: Activate IAM access to Billing and Cost Management.
answers.explanation: correct because IAM access to Billing and Cost Management must be enabled to allow teams to access billing data and generate reports.

answers.content: Create a cost budget.
answers.explanation: incorrect because budgets are used for alerts and spending thresholds, not for generating historical comparison and forecasting reports.

answers.content: Enable Cost Explorer.
answers.explanation: correct because Cost Explorer provides historical cost analysis (up to 12 months), filtering by tags, and forecasting capabilities for future spending.

questions.content: A company runs a new application as a static website in Amazon S3. The company has deployed the application to a production AWS account and uses Amazon CloudFront to deliver the websitThe website calls an Amazon API Gateway REST API. An AWS Lambda function backs each API method. The company wants to create a CSV report every 2 weeks to show each API Lambda function's recommended configured memory, recommended cost, and the price difference between current configurations and the recommendations. The company will store the reports in an S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development time?

answers.content: Create a Lambda function that extracts metrics data for each API Lambda function from Amazon CloudWatch Logs for the 2-week period. Collate the data into tabular format. Store the data as a .csv file in an S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function to run every 2 weeks.
answers.explanation: Requires custom metric extraction and data collation from CloudWatch Logs, increasing development time.

answers.content: Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer. Create a Lambda function that calls the ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations operation. Export the .csv file to an S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function to run every 2 weeks.
answers.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer provides Lambda function recommendations including memory and cost efficiencies. The ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations operation can export these recommendations as a CSV filUsing a Lambda function to call this operation and store the CSV in S3, scheduled by EventBridge for biweekly execution, minimizes development timThis approach leverages managed AWS services designed for this purpose, ensuring security and best practice compliance.

answers.content: Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer. Set up enhanced infrastructure metrics. Within the Compute Optimizer console, schedule a job to export the Lambda recommendations to a .csv filStore the file in an S3 bucket every 2 weeks.
answers.explanation: No facts confirm Compute Optimizer console can schedule biweekly exports to S3 natively, so it may not meet the 'least development time' requirement.

answers.content: Purchase the AWS Business Support plan for the production account. Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer for AWS Trusted Advisor checks. In the Trusted Advisor console, schedule a job to export the cost optimization checks to a .csv filStore the file in an S3 bucket every 2 weeks.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks do not provide Lambda-specific memory and cost recommendations; Business Support and Trusted Advisor are not necessary for this use case.

questions.content: A company is running a web application in the AWS Cloud. The application consists of dynamic content that is created on a set of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that is configured as a target group for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company is using an Amazon CloudFront distribution to distribute the application globally. The CloudFront distribution uses the ALB as an origin. The company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS and has created an A record of www.example.com for the CloudFront distribution. A solutions architect must configure the application so that itis highly available and fault tolerant. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Provision a full, secondary application deployment in a different AWS Region. Update the Route 53 A record to be a failover record. Add both of the CloudFront distributions as values. Create Route 53 health checks.
answers.explanation: Using Route 53 failover between two CloudFront distributions adds complexity and DNS-level delays; managed CloudFront origin failover is preferable.

answers.content: Provision an ALB, an Auto Scaling group, and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region. Update the CloudFront distribution, and create a second origin for the new ALCreate an origin group for the two origins. Configure one origin as primary and one origin as secondary.
answers.explanation: Configuring an ALB, Auto Scaling group, and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region and updating the CloudFront distribution to have two origins with origin failover provides high availability and fault tolerance at the global level. CloudFront origin groups allow automatic failover between origins based on health, ensuring traffic is routed only to healthy endpoints. This approach leverages managed AWS services designed for scaling and health checks, improving resilience without manual DNS failover. Using origin groups aligns with best practices for fault tolerance and managed failover under CloudFront.

answers.content: Provision an Auto Scaling group and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region. Create a second target for the new Auto Scaling group in the ALB. Set up the failover routing algorithm on the ALB.
answers.explanation: An ALB cannot have targets across different AWS Regions, so creating a second target in a different Region is not supported.

answers.content: Provision a full, secondary application deployment in a different AWS Region. Create a second CloudFront distribution, and add the new application setup as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator. Add both of the CloudFront distributions as endpoints.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Global Accelerator with multiple CloudFront distributions is more complex and unnecessary when CloudFront origin failover can achieve fault tolerance.

questions.content: A health insurance company stores personally identifiable information (PII) in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to encrypt the objects. According to a new requirement, all current and future objects in the S3 bucket must be encrypted by keys that the company's security team manages. The S3 bucket does not have versioning enabled. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to SSE-S3 with a customer managed key. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket. Set an S3 bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests.
answers.explanation: SSE-S3 uses Amazon-managed keys, not customer managed keys, so it does not meet the requirement.

answers.content: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Set an S3 bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: The requirement is that all objects must be encrypted with keys managed by the company's security team, which means using AWS KMS Customer Managed Keys (CMKs), not SSE-S3. Changing the default encryption to SSE-KMS ensures all future objects are encrypted with the customer managed key automatically. Re-uploading all existing objects with the AWS CLI ensures current objects are re-encrypted with the new CMK. Setting a bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests enforces encryption compliance for future uploads. Answer B explicitly uses SSE-KMS with customer managed keys, re-uploads objects, and applies a bucket policy to enforce encryption, meeting all requirements.

answers.content: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Set an S3 bucket policy to automatically encrypt objects on GetObject and PutObject requests.
answers.explanation: Bucket policies cannot automatically encrypt objects on GetObject requests; encryption occurs on upload, so this is invalid.

answers.content: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to AES-256 with a customer managed key. Attach a policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests to any entities that access the S3 bucket. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: AES-256 is a cipher, not a valid option for server-side encryption with customer managed keys in S3 properties; also 'customer managed key' is ambiguous and not correctly applied here.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate its data analytics environment from on premises to AWS. The environment consists of two simple Node.js applications. One of the applications collects sensor data and loads it into a MySQL databasThe other application aggregates the data into reports. When the aggregation jobs run, some of the load jobs fail to run correctly. The company must resolve the data loading issuThe company also needs the migration to occur without interruptions or changes for the company's customers. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL database as a replication target for the on-premises databasCreate an Aurora Replica for the Aurora MySQL database, and move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora Replica. Set up collection endpoints as AWS Lambda functions behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB), and use Amazon RDS Proxy to write to the Aurora MySQL databasWhen the databases are synced, disable the replication job and restart the Aurora Replica as the primary instancPoint the collector DNS record to the NLB.
answers.explanation: Using a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with Lambda is not optimal for HTTP/HTTPS workloads compared to ALB; setting up an Aurora Replica before migration start is less appropriate.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL databasUse AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to perform continuous data replication from the on-premises database to Aurora. Move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora MySQL databasSet up collection endpoints behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. When the databases are synced, point the collector DNS record to the ALDisable the AWS DMS sync task after the cutover from on premises to AWS.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 instances instead of Lambda functions adds unnecessary operational overhead and less security; no use of RDS Proxy reduces security and scalability.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL databasUse AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to perform continuous data replication from the on-premises database to Aurora. Create an Aurora Replica for the Aurora MySQL database, and move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora Replica. Set up collection endpoints as AWS Lambda functions behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB), and use Amazon RDS Proxy to write to the Aurora MySQL databasWhen the databases are synced, point the collector DNS record to the ALB. Disable the AWS DMS sync task after the cutover from on premises to AWS.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon Aurora MySQL with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) for continuous replication aligns with best practices for data migration without interruption. Creating an Aurora Replica and running aggregation jobs against it offloads read workload and improves availability. Using AWS Lambda functions behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Amazon RDS Proxy ensures scalable, managed, and secure access to the databasDisabling the AWS DMS sync task after cutover prevents conflicts once migration is completThis solution maintains service continuity, uses managed AWS services designed for migration and scaling, and applies best security practices by using proxies and managed Lambda endpoints.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL databasCreate an Aurora Replica for the Aurora MySQL database, and move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora Replica. Set up collection endpoints as an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to replicate the data to the Aurora MySQL databasWhen the databases are synced, disable the replication job and restart the Aurora Replica as the primary instancPoint the collector DNS record to the Kinesis data stream.
answers.explanation: Using Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose for data ingestion into Aurora is unnecessarily complex and less suitable than DMS for continuous replication from MySQL; also lacks use of RDS Proxy and Lambda for secure and scalable access.

questions.content: A company is planning to host a web application on AWS and wants to load balance the traffic across a group of Amazon EC2 instances. One of the security requirements is to enable end-to-end encryption in transit between the client and the web server. Which solution will meet this requirement?

answers.content: Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Provision an SSL certificate using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), and associate the SSL certificate with the ALB. Export the SSL certificate and install it on each EC2 instancConfigure the ALB to listen on port 443 and to forward traffic to port 443 on the instances.
answers.explanation: Using an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with an SSL certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) aligns with AWS best practices for managing SSL certificates securely. Installing the same SSL certificate on both the ALB and EC2 instances enables end-to-end encryption in transit from the client to the web server. AWS managed certificates (ACM) are preferred over third-party certificates for ease of management and security. Configuring the ALB to listen on port 443 and forward traffic on port 443 ensures encrypted communication through to the instances.

answers.content: Associate the EC2 instances with a target group. Provision an SSL certificate using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and configure it to use the SSL certificatSet CloudFront to use the target group as the origin server.
answers.explanation: CloudFront does not natively associate with a target group as an origin; this is not a valid configuration for end-to-end encryption to EC2.

answers.content: Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) Provision an SSL certificate using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), and associate the SSL certificate with the ALB. Provision a third-party SSL certificate and install it on each EC2 instancConfigure the ALB to listen on port 443 and to forward traffic to port 443 on the instances.
answers.explanation: Using third-party certificates on EC2 instances adds operational complexity and security risk compared to using ACM certificates.

answers.content: Place the EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Provision a third-party SSL certificate and install it on the NLB and on each EC2 instancConfigure the NLB to listen on port 443 and to forward traffic to port 443 on the instances.
answers.explanation: Network Load Balancer does not natively handle SSL certificates and managing third-party certificates on the NLB and instances is not best practice.

questions.content: A solutions architect has developed a web application that uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional endpoint and an AWS Lambda function. The consumers of the web application are all close to the AWS Region where the application will be deployed. The Lambda function only queries an Amazon Aurora MySQL databasThe solutions architect has configured the database to have three read replicas. During testing, the application does not meet performance requirements. Under high load, the application opens a large number of database connections. The solutions architect must improve the application's performancWhich actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use the cluster endpoint of the Aurora database.
