answers.explanation: incorrect because the Aurora cluster endpoint primarily directs traffic to the writer instance and does not solve the excessive connection problem or efficiently distribute read traffic to replicas.

answers.content: Use RDS Proxy to set up a connection pool to the reader endpoint of the Aurora database.
answers.explanation: correct because RDS Proxy manages and pools database connections, reducing the number of concurrent connections opened by Lambda functions and improving performance under high load.

answers.content: Use the Lambda Provisioned Concurrency feature.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Provisioned Concurrency reduces cold starts but does not address the database connection exhaustion issue.

answers.content: Move the code for opening the database connection in the Lambda function outside of the event handler.
answers.explanation: correct because moving the database connection initialization outside the Lambda handler allows connection reuse across invocations within the same execution environment, reducing connection overhead.

answers.content: Change the API Gateway endpoint to an edge-optimized endpoint.
answers.explanation: incorrect because an edge-optimized endpoint benefits globally distributed clients, but the users are already near the Region and this does not solve database connection scaling issues.

questions.content: A company is building a serverless application that runs on an AWS Lambda function that is attached to a VPC. The company needs to integrate the application with a new service from an external provider. The external provider supports only requests that come from public IPv4 addresses that are in an allow list. The company must provide a single public IP address to the external provider before the application can start using the new servicWhich solution will give the application the ability to access the new service?

answers.content: Deploy a NAT gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the NAT gateway. Configure the VPC to use the NAT gateway.
answers.explanation: A NAT gateway with an associated Elastic IP provides a single public IPv4 address that serverless functions in a VPC can use for outbound internet access. Lambda functions attached to a VPC do not have public IP addresses by default and require a NAT gateway for internet-bound traffic. The NAT gateway ensures all outbound requests from Lambda use the Elastic IP, fulfilling the requirement of a single static public IP for allow listing. Using managed NAT gateway service is preferred over other manual routing or gateway configurations to provide secure and reliable internet access.

answers.content: Deploy an egress-only internet gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the egress-only internet gateway. Configure the elastic network interface on the Lambda function to use the egress-only internet gateway.
answers.explanation: Egress-only internet gateways are for IPv6 traffic only and cannot be associated with Elastic IPs or used for IPv4 public IP requirements.

answers.content: Deploy an internet gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the internet gateway. Configure the Lambda function to use the internet gateway.
answers.explanation: Internet gateways cannot have Elastic IP addresses associated directly; they provide general internet access but do not provide a single static public IP.

answers.content: Deploy an internet gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the internet gateway. Configure the default route in the public VPC route table to use the internet gateway.
answers.explanation: Associating an Elastic IP with an internet gateway or using a default route does not assign a static public IP for outbound traffic from private subnets or Lambda within a VPC.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate 1,000 on-premises servers to AWS. The servers run on several VMware clusters in the company's data center. As part of the migration plan, the company wants to gather server metrics such as CPU details, RAM usage, operating system information, and running processes. The company then wants to query and analyze the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Deploy and configure the AWS Agentless Discovery Connector virtual appliance on the on-premises hosts. Configure Data Exploration in AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Glue to perform an ETL job against the data. Query the data by using Amazon S3 Select.
answers.explanation: Agentless Discovery Connector does not collect detailed server metrics such as running processes; also, using AWS Glue and S3 Select is less direct and involves more manual setup.

answers.content: Export only the VM performance information from the on-premises hosts. Directly import the required data into AWS Migration Hub. Update any missing information in Migration Hub. Query the data by using Amazon QuickSight.
answers.explanation: Exporting only VM performance data is incomplete and importing directly into Migration Hub lacks automatic detailed data collection and integration.

answers.content: Create a script to automatically gather the server information from the on-premises hosts. Use the AWS CLI to run the put-resource-attributes command to store the detailed server data in AWS Migration Hub. Query the data directly in the Migration Hub console.
answers.explanation: Using custom scripts and manual put-resource-attributes commands is less secure and operationally intensive compared to AWS managed discovery agents.

answers.content: Deploy the AWS Application Discovery Agent to each on-premises server. Configure Data Exploration in AWS Migration Hub. Use Amazon Athena to run predefined queries against the data in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Agent is designed to collect detailed on-premises server information including CPU, RAM, OS, and running processes. Configuring Data Exploration in AWS Migration Hub allows aggregation of discovered data. Using Amazon Athena to query data stored in Amazon S3 is a managed and scalable solution to analyze gathered metrics. This approach aligns with AWS best practices by using an agent designed for discovery, managed services for data aggregation and querying, and avoids manual or partial data gathering.

questions.content: A company hosts a Git repository in an on-premises data center. The company uses webhooks to invoke functionality that runs in the AWS Cloud. The company hosts the webhook logic on a set of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group that the company set as a target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The Git server calls the ALB for the configured webhooks. The company wants to move the solution to a serverless architecturWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: For each webhook, create and configure an AWS Lambda function URL. Update the Git servers to call the individual Lambda function URLs.
answers.explanation: Using individual Lambda function URLs would require managing many URLs and updating Git servers, increasing operational overhead and complexity.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API. Implement each webhook logic in a separate AWS Lambda function. Update the Git servers to call the API Gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: An API Gateway HTTP API combined with Lambda functions offers a fully managed, serverless architecture with minimal operational overhead. API Gateway efficiently routes webhooks to individual Lambda functions, aligning with microservices best practices. Lambda functions handle execution and scaling, eliminating the need for managing infrastructure such as EC2 instances or containers. This approach ensures secure, scalable, and decoupled webhook processing with low management effort.

answers.content: Deploy the webhook logic to AWS App Runner. Create an ALB, and set App Runner as the target. Update the Git servers to call the ALB endpoint.
answers.explanation: Using App Runner with an ALB reintroduces server and load balancer management, increasing operational overhead compared to a fully serverless solution.

answers.content: Containerize the webhook logic. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster, and run the webhook logic in AWS FargatCreate an Amazon API Gateway REST API, and set Fargate as the target. Update the Git servers to call the API Gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: Deploying in ECS Fargate with API Gateway involves container management and adds complexity compared to direct Lambda invocation.

questions.content: A company has 10 accounts that are part of an organization in AWS Organizations. AWS Config is configured in each account. All accounts belong to either the Prod OU or the NonProd OU. The company has set up an Amazon EventBridge rule in each AWS account to notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when an Amazon EC2 security group inbound rule is created with 0.0.0.0/0 as the sourcThe company's security team is subscribed to the SNS topic. For all accounts in the NonProd OU, the security team needs to remove the ability to create a security group inbound rule that includes 0.0.0.0/0 as the sourcWhich solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Modify the EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to remove the security group inbound rule and to publish to the SNS topic. Deploy the updated rule to the NonProd OU.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda to remove rules after creation is reactive and has greater operational overhead than proactive prevention via SCPs.

answers.content: Add the vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports AWS Config managed rule to the NonProd OU.
answers.explanation: While AWS Config rules can monitor compliance, they do not prevent creation, thus failing the requirement to remove ability to create such rules.

answers.content: Configure an SCP to allow the ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress action when the value of the aws:SourceIp condition key is not 0.0.0.0/0. Apply the SCP to the NonProd OU.
answers.explanation: An SCP allowing the action only when source IP is not 0.0.0.0/0 could be complex and less straightforward than directly denying the unwanted action.

answers.content: Configure an SCP to deny the ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress action when the value of the aws:SourceIp condition key is 0.0.0.0/0. Apply the SCP to the NonProd OU.
answers.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) applied to the NonProd OU can restrict the ability to create security group inbound rules with 0.0.0.0/0 as the source, effectively preventing this action at the account or organizational unit level. The SCP denying ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress when aws:SourceIp is 0.0.0.0/0 directly enforces the security requirement with the least operational overhead. Using SCPs is a managed service feature of AWS Organizations and is preferred over custom or manual solutions like Lambda for enforcement. It prevents the creation of unwanted inbound rules proactively rather than reacting after their creation.

questions.content: A company is using Amazon OpenSearch Service to analyze data. The company loads data into an OpenSearch Service cluster with 10 data nodes from an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard storagThe data resides in the cluster for 1 month for read-only analysis. After 1 month, the company deletes the index that contains the data from the cluster. For compliance purposes, the company must retain a copy of all input data. The company is concerned about ongoing costs and asks a solutions architect to recommend a new solution. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Replace all the data nodes with UltraWarm nodes to handle the expected capacity. Transition the input data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive when the company loads the data into the cluster.
answers.explanation: Transitions input data to Glacier Deep Archive immediately on load, which is impractical and UltraWarm nodes alone may not be sufficient without reducing data nodes.

answers.content: Reduce the number of data nodes in the cluster to 2 Add UltraWarm nodes to handle the expected capacity. Configure the indexes to transition to UltraWarm when OpenSearch Service ingests the data. Transition the input data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month by using an S3 Lifecycle policy.
answers.explanation: Reducing the number of data nodes and adding UltraWarm nodes optimizes cost while meeting capacity needs. Configuring indexes to transition to UltraWarm on ingestion leverages the managed UltraWarm storage for cost efficiency. Transitioning input data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive with Lifecycle policy ensures compliance by retaining input data cost-effectively. Deleting the input data after 1 month from S3 with Lifecycle policy avoids unnecessary storage costs while meeting compliance.

answers.content: Reduce the number of data nodes in the cluster to 2. Add UltraWarm nodes to handle the expected capacity. Configure the indexes to transition to UltraWarm when OpenSearch Service ingests the data. Add cold storage nodes to the cluster Transition the indexes from UltraWarm to cold storagDelete the input data from the S3 bucket after 1 month by using an S3 Lifecycle policy.
answers.explanation: Deletes input data after 1 month, violating compliance requirement to retain a copy; also adds unnecessary complex cold storage nodes.

answers.content: Reduce the number of data nodes in the cluster to 2. Add instance-backed data nodes to handle the expected capacity. Transition the input data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive when the company loads the data into the cluster.
answers.explanation: Using instance-backed nodes instead of UltraWarm for cost savings is less optimal; immediately transitions input data to Glacier Deep Archive without Lifecycle policy automation.

questions.content: A solutions architect needs to advise a company on how to migrate its on-premises data processing application to the AWS Cloud. Currently, users upload input files through a web portal. The web server then stores the uploaded files on NAS and messages the processing server over a message queuEach media file can take up to 1 hour to process. The company has determined that the number of media files awaiting processing is significantly higher during business hours, with the number of files rapidly declining after business hours. What is the MOST cost-effective migration recommendation?

answers.content: Create a queue using Amazon SQS. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queuWhen there are messages in the queue, invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: AWS Lambda is impractical for long-running processes (up to 1 hour), as Lambda has a maximum execution limit far less than an hour.

answers.content: Create a queue using Amazon MQ. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queuWhen there are messages in the queue, create a new Amazon EC2 instance to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in Amazon EFS. Shut down the EC2 instance after the task is complete.
answers.explanation: Manually creating and shutting down EC2 instances is less efficient and with Amazon MQ adds unnecessary complexity and cost compared to SQS; storing processed files in EFS is more costly and less optimal than S3 for media files.

answers.content: Create a queue using Amazon MQ. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queuWhen there are messages in the queue, invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in Amazon EFS.
answers.explanation: Combining Amazon MQ and Lambda is suboptimal due to Lambda's short execution time limits and Amazon MQ's higher cost compared to SQS; storing processed files in EFS is also less cost-effective than S3.

answers.content: Create a queue using Amazon SQS. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queuUse Amazon EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Scale the EC2 instances based on the SQS queue length. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SQS as the queue service is a cost-effective, fully managed, and scalable solution for decoupling the web server from the processing servers. Employing EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group allows the system to scale processing capacity based on demand (e.g., scaling up during business hours and down after hours), optimizing cost-efficiency. Storing processed files in Amazon S3 provides a durable, cost-effective, and managed storage solution suitable for large media files. This approach leverages managed AWS services (SQS, EC2 Auto Scaling, S3) that align with security best practices and cost optimization.

questions.content: A company recently deployed an application on AWS. The application uses Amazon DynamoDB. The company measured the application load and configured the RCUs and WCUs on the DynamoDB table to match the expected peak load. The peak load occurs once a week for a 4-hour period and is double the average load. The application load is close to the average load for the rest of the week. The access pattern includes many more writes to the table than reads of the tablA solutions architect needs to implement a solution to minimize the cost of the tablWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Application Auto Scaling to increase capacity during the peak period. Purchase reserved RCUs and WCUs to match the average load.
answers.explanation: Reserved capacity is less flexible and can lead to higher costs due to over-provisioning, especially if the load spikes only occur once a week.

answers.content: Configure on-demand capacity mode for the table.
answers.explanation: On-demand capacity mode in DynamoDB automatically adjusts to workload changes and is cost-effective for unpredictable or variable workloads. The peak load occurs once a week for a short period and is double the average load, making provisioned capacity with reserved capacity less cost-effective due to over-provisioning. DynamoDB is fully managed and serverless, so on-demand mode leverages its automatic scaling capabilities without manual capacity adjustments. DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) only benefits read-intensive workloads and will not reduce costs for write-heavy access patterns. Purchasing reserved capacity is best when load is consistent and predictable, but here weekly spikes make on-demand a better fit.

answers.content: Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the tablReduce the provisioned read capacity to match the new peak load on the table.
answers.explanation: DAX accelerates reads and is not beneficial for a write-heavy workload; reducing provisioned read capacity could cause throttling on reads during peaks.

answers.content: Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the tablConfigure on-demand capacity mode for the table.
answers.explanation: Using DAX with on-demand capacity mode adds unnecessary complexity and cost, and DAX does not help reduce write costs.

questions.content: A company is hosting an image-processing service on AWS in a VPC. The VPC extends across two Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone contains one public subnet and one private subnet. The service runs on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. An Application Load Balancer in the public subnets is in front of the servicThe service needs to communicate with the internet and does so through two NAT gateways. The service uses Amazon S3 for image storagThe EC2 instances retrieve approximately 1 ТВ of data from an S3 bucket each day. The company has promoted the service as highly securA solutions architect must reduce cloud expenditures as much as possible without compromising the service's security posture or increasing the time spent on ongoing operations. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Replace the NAT gateways with NAT instances. In the VPC route table, create a route from the private subnets to the NAT instances.
answers.explanation: NAT instances require management and do not reduce operational overhead or significantly improve security over NAT gateways.

answers.content: Move the EC2 instances to the public subnets. Remove the NAT gateways.
answers.explanation: Moving EC2 instances to public subnets exposes them directly to the internet, compromising the security posture.

answers.content: Set up an S3 gateway VPC endpoint in the VPAttach an endpoint policy to the endpoint to allow the required actions on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Using an S3 gateway VPC endpoint enables EC2 instances in private subnets to access S3 without using NAT gateways, thus reducing NAT gateway data processing charges. Gateway endpoints are managed by AWS and provide secure, scalable, and highly available connectivity to S3 without exposing traffic to the internet, maintaining security posturThe solution reduces costs by eliminating charged data processed through NAT gateways and minimizes operational overhead by using a managed AWS servicMounting an EFS volume or moving EC2 instances to public subnets would not reduce NAT gateway costs or maintain security best practices. Replacing NAT gateways with NAT instances adds operational complexity and potential security concerns, going against best practices.

answers.content: Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume to the EC2 instances. Host the images on the EFS volume.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EFS for image storage instead of S3 is not cost-effective given the large data volume and does not reduce NAT gateway costs.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate its workloads from on premises to AWS. The workloads run on Linux and Windows. The company has a large on-premises infrastructure that consists of physical machines and VMs that host numerous applications. The company must capture details about the system configuration, system performance, running processes, and network connections of its on-premises workloads. The company also must divide the on-premises applications into groups for AWS migrations. The company needs recommendations for Amazon EC2 instance types so that the company can run its workloads on AWS in the most cost-effective manner. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Assess the existing applications by installing AWS Application Discovery Agent on the physical machines and VMs.
answers.explanation: correct because installing the AWS Application Discovery Agent collects detailed information about system configuration, performance, running processes, and network dependencies needed for migration planning.

answers.content: Assess the existing applications by installing AWS Systems Manager Agent on the physical machines and VMs.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Systems Manager Agent is used for management and operations, not for collecting detailed discovery data for migration assessment.

answers.content: Group servers into applications for migration by using AWS Systems Manager Application Manager.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Systems Manager Application Manager is not designed to group servers for migration planning across on-premises environments.

answers.content: Group servers into applications for migration by using AWS Migration Hub.
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Migration Hub allows grouping discovered servers into applications to plan and track migration waves effectively.

answers.content: Generate recommended instance types and associated costs by using AWS Migration Hub.
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Migration Hub (with Application Discovery Service data) provides EC2 instance type recommendations and cost estimates for right-sizing in AWS.

answers.content: Import data about server sizes into AWS Trusted Advisor. Follow the recommendations for cost optimization.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Trusted Advisor does not import on-premises server data for migration sizing recommendations.

questions.content: A company recently completed the migration from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud by using a replatforming strategy. One of the migrated servers is running a legacy Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) service that a critical application relies upon. The application sends outbound email messages to the company's customers. The legacy SMTP server does not support TLS encryption and uses TCP port 25. The application can use SMTP only. The company decides to use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) and to decommission the legacy SMTP server. The company has created and validated the SES domain. The company has lifted the SES limits. What should the company do to modify the application to send email messages from Amazon SES?

answers.content: Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using TLS Wrapper. Create an IAM role that has ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions. Attach the IAM role to an Amazon EC2 instance.
answers.explanation: Amazon SES SMTP interface does not use TLS Wrapper or IAM roles for authentication.

answers.content: Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using STARTTLS. Obtain Amazon SES SMTP credentials. Use the credentials to authenticate with Amazon SES.
answers.explanation: Amazon SES supports sending email via its SMTP interface, which requires obtaining specific SMTP credentials. The SMTP credentials for Amazon SES are distinct from AWS access keys and are used for authenticating SMTP connections. Using STARTTLS with Amazon SES SMTP interface is a supported way to secure SMTP connections and send email. The application uses SMTP only, so using the SMTP interface with STARTTLS and SMTP credentials aligns with AWS best practices for secure email sending.

answers.content: Configure the application to use the SES API to send email messages. Create an IAM role that has ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions. Use the IAM role as a service role for Amazon SES.
answers.explanation: Using the SES API is not possible if the application supports SMTP only.

answers.content: Configure the application to use AWS SDKs to send email messages. Create an IAM user for Amazon SES. Generate API access keys. Use the access keys to authenticate with Amazon SES.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users and using AWS SDKs is not applicable if the application supports only SMTP.

questions.content: Example Corp. has an on-premises data center and a VPC named VPC A in the Example Corp. AWS account. The on-premises network connects to VPC A through an AWS Site-To-Site VPN. The on-premises servers can properly access VPC A. Example Corp. just acquired AnyCompany, which has a VPC named VPC B. There is no IP address overlap among these networks. Example Corp. has peered VPC A and VPC B. Example Corp. wants to connect from its on-premise servers to VPC B. Example Corp. has properly set up the network ACL and security groups. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

answers.content: Create a transit gateway. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN, VPC A, and VPC B to the transit gateway. Update the transit gateway route tables for all networks to add IP range routes for all other networks.
answers.explanation: Using a transit gateway to attach the Site-to-Site VPN, VPC A, and VPC B centralizes and simplifies network management. It requires updating the transit gateway route tables once to enable connectivity between all networks, minimizing operational effort. This approach uses a managed AWS service designed for scalable inter-VPC and on-premises connectivity, adhering to best practices. Option A avoids creating multiple VPNs or complex VPN endpoint modifications, reducing configuration complexity and risk.

answers.content: Create a transit gateway. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises network and VPC B, and connect the VPN connection to the transit gateway. Add a route to direct traffic to the peered VPCs, and add an authorization rule to give clients access to the VPCs A and B.
answers.explanation: Creating an additional Site-to-Site VPN connection to VPC B increases operational overhead and complexity unnecessarily.

answers.content: Update the route tables for the Site-to-Site VPN and both VPCs for all three networks. Configure BGP propagation for all three networks. Wait for up to 5 minutes for BGP propagation to finish.
answers.explanation: Manually updating all route tables and relying solely on BGP propagation is operationally heavy and less scalable.

answers.content: Modify the Site-to-Site VPN's virtual private gateway definition to include VPC A and VPC B. Split the two routers of the virtual private getaway between the two VPCs.
answers.explanation: Modifying the existing VPN's virtual private gateway to include two VPCs is not supported and is operationally complex.

questions.content: A retail company is hosting an ecommerce website on AWS across multiple AWS Regions. The company wants the website to be operational at all times for online purchases. The website stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instancWhich solution will provide the HIGHEST availability for the database?

answers.content: Configure automated backups on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, promote an automated backup to be a standalone DB instancDirect database traffic to the promoted DB instancCreate a replacement read replica that has the promoted DB instance as its source.
answers.explanation: Promoting automated backups involves manual intervention and slower recovery compared to using read replicas for failover.

answers.content: Configure global tables and read replicas on Amazon RDS. Activate the cross-Region scopIn the case of disruption, use AWS Lambda to copy the read replicas from one Region to another Region.
answers.explanation: There is no global tables feature for RDS; using Lambda to copy read replicas adds unnecessary complexity and delayed recovery.

answers.content: Configure global tables and automated backups on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, use AWS Lambda to copy the read replicas from one Region to another Region.
answers.explanation: Combining global tables and automated backups is invalid for RDS; Lambda-based replica copying is not a standard managed availability solution.

answers.content: Configure read replicas on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, promote a cross-Region and read replica to be a standalone DB instancDirect database traffic to the promoted DB instancCreate a replacement read replica that has the promoted DB instance as its source.
answers.explanation: Configuring read replicas in Amazon RDS across multiple AWS Regions and promoting a cross-Region read replica to standalone in case of disruption optimizes availability and failover capabilities. Promoting a read replica ensures the database remains operational without manual restoration from backups, providing near-continuous availability. Creating replacement read replicas after failover maintains the replication hierarchy and availability posturOptions involving AWS Lambda to copy replicas or to manage backups manually add complexity and do not leverage AWS managed automated failover features.

questions.content: A solutions architect is designing the data storage and retrieval architecture for a new application that a company will be launching soon. The application is designed to ingest millions of small records per minute from devices all around the world. Each record is less than 4 KB in size and needs to be stored in a durable location where it can be retrieved with low latency. The data is ephemeral and the company is required to store the data for 120 days only, after which the data can be deleted. The solutions architect calculates that, during the course of a year, the storage requirements would be about 10-15 TB. Which storage strategy is the MOST cost-effective and meets the design requirements?

answers.content: Design the application to store each incoming record as a single .csv file in an Amazon S3 bucket to allow for indexed retrieval. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete data older than 120 days.
answers.explanation: Storing each record as a single .csv file in S3 is inefficient and not optimized for low latency retrieval of millions of small records.

answers.content: Design the application to store each incoming record in an Amazon DynamoDB table properly configured for the scalConfigure the DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) feature to delete records older than 120 days.
answers.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is designed to handle high-scale ingestion of millions of small records with low latency retrieval, fitting the need for storing millions of sub-4 KB records from devices worldwidDynamoDB's Time to Live (TTL) feature natively supports automatic deletion of expired items, meeting the 120 days retention requirement without manual intervention. DynamoDB is a managed service optimized for performance and scaling, providing durability and low latency retrieval over large datasets, making it a cost-effective and operationally efficient choice over managing files in S3 or RDS cron jobs. Storing individual records as separate S3 objects (Option A) or batching them inefficiently (Option D) would increase costs and reduce retrieval performance due to the nature of object storage being less suited for rapid, item-level access. Using RDS with nightly jobs for deletion (Option C) adds operational complexity, is less scalable for millions of writes per minute, and does not provide native TTL features.

answers.content: Design the application to store each incoming record in a single table in an Amazon RDS MySQL databasRun a nightly cron job that runs a query to delete any records older than 120 days.
answers.explanation: RDS MySQL is not well suited for ingesting millions of small records per minute and requires manual deletion jobs increasing complexity and latency.

answers.content: Design the application to batch incoming records before writing them to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the metadata for the object to contain the list of records in the batch and use the Amazon S3 metadata search feature to retrieve the data. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete the data after 120 days.
answers.explanation: Batching records in S3 and relying on metadata search is less efficient for low latency retrieval and adds complexity without native TTL for deletions.

questions.content: A company is running several workloads in a single AWS account. A new company policy states that engineers can provision only approved resources and that engineers must use AWS CloudFormation to provision these resources. A solutions architect needs to create a solution to enforce the new restriction on the IAM role that the engineers use for access. What should the solutions architect do to create the solution?

answers.content: Upload AWS CloudFormation templates that contain approved resources to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the IAM policy for the engineers' IAM role to only allow access to Amazon S3 and AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to provision resources.
answers.explanation: Restricting engineers to S3 and CloudFormation access does not enforce which resources can be provisioned and is insecure as templates can be replaced or manipulated.

answers.content: Update the IAM policy for the engineers' IAM role with permissions to only allow provisioning of approved resources and AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create stacks with approved resources.
answers.explanation: Granting engineers direct permission to provision approved resources reduces control and bypasses the enforcement via CloudFormation roles, weakening security.

answers.content: Update the IAM policy for the engineers' IAM role with permissions to only allow AWS CloudFormation actions. Create a new IAM policy with permission to provision approved resources, and assign the policy to a new IAM service rolAssign the IAM service role to AWS CloudFormation during stack creation.
answers.explanation: This approach uses a combination of IAM policies to restrict engineers to only use CloudFormation and only provision approved resources via a service role, which aligns with security best practices to enforce resource provisioning constraints. By restricting permissions on the engineers' IAM role to CloudFormation actions only and assigning a service role with specific resource permissions, it uses managed AWS mechanisms to enforce policy. Managed roles and policies tied to CloudFormation stacks are preferred over restricting access to S3 buckets or allowing direct permissions within engineers' roles to provision resources, ensuring least privilege and separation of duties.

answers.content: Provision resources in AWS CloudFormation stacks. Update the IAM policy for the engineers' IAM role to only allow access to their own AWS CloudFormation stack.
answers.explanation: Allowing engineers access only to their own stacks does not restrict what resources can be provisioned and does not enforce the approval policy.

questions.content: A company is building a solution in the AWS Cloud. Thousands or devices will connect to the solution and send data. Each device needs to be able to send and receive data in real time over the MQTT protocol. Each device must authenticate by using a unique X.509 certificatWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Set up AWS IoT CorFor each device, create a corresponding Amazon MQ queue and provision a certificatConnect each device to Amazon MQ.
answers.explanation: Amazon MQ is not optimized for MQTT with X.509 authentication at scale and would increase operational overhead.

answers.content: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and configure it with an AWS Lambda authorizer. Run an MQTT broker on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Set the Auto Scaling group as the target for the NLConnect each device to the NLB.
answers.explanation: Running a custom MQTT broker on EC2 with NLB and Lambda authorizer adds significant operational overhead and complexity.

answers.content: Set up AWS IoT CorFor each device, create a corresponding AWS IoT thing and provision a certificatConnect each device to AWS IoT Core.
answers.explanation: AWS IoT Core natively supports MQTT protocol and authentication with unique X.509 certificates per device, minimizing operational overhead. Creating an AWS IoT Thing for each device and provisioning a certificate aligns with AWS best practices for security and device management. AWS IoT Device SDKs are recommended for connecting devices securely using MQTT and certificates without needing to manage infrastructurUsing AWS IoT Core avoids the complexity and overhead of managing EC2 brokers, Amazon MQ queues, or custom authorizers.

answers.content: Set up an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API and a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Create integration between API Gateway and the NLB. Configure a mutual TLS certificate authorizer on the HTTP API. Run an MQTT broker on an Amazon EC2 instance that the NLB targets. Connect each device to the NLB.
answers.explanation: Using API Gateway and NLB with mutual TLS to front a broker on EC2 is unnecessarily complex and operationally heavy compared to AWS IoT Core.

questions.content: An application is using an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance in the us-east-1 Region. After a failover test, the application lost the connections to the database and could not re-establish the connections. After a restart of the application, the application re-established the connections. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the application can re-establish connections to the database without requiring a restart. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v1 DB instancMigrate the RDS DB instance to the Aurora Serverless v1 DB instancUpdate the connection settings in the application to point to the Aurora reader endpoint.
answers.explanation: Aurora Serverless v1 is not designed for Multi-AZ failover handling with the same predictable failover behavior and would require migration and code changes; also, it uses different endpoints and is not the simplest failover solution.

answers.content: Create an RDS proxy. Configure the existing RDS endpoint as a target. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the RDS proxy endpoint.
answers.explanation: RDS Proxy provides connection pooling and manages failovers transparently to the application, allowing it to re-establish connections without requiring a restart. The application currently uses an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance which can experience failover causing connection loss. Using RDS Proxy as a managed service abstracts failover complexities and maintains connection continuity during failovers, aligning with AWS best practices for high availability and resilience.

answers.content: Create a two-node Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. Migrate the RDS DB instance to the Aurora DB cluster. Create an RDS proxy. Configure the existing RDS endpoint as a target. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the RDS proxy endpoint.
answers.explanation: While creating an Aurora cluster and RDS Proxy is possible, it is more complex than necessary, and the combination is not required; migrating to Aurora and then adding proxy adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Export the database to Amazon S3 by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Configure Amazon Athena to use the S3 bucket as a data storInstall the latest Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver for the application. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the Athena endpoint
answers.explanation: Exporting the database to S3 and querying with Athena is not suitable for transactional database applications and does not address failover reconnection issues.

questions.content: A video streaming company recently launched a mobile app for video sharing. The app uploads various files to an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The files range in size from 1 GB to 10 GB. Users who access the app from Australia have experienced uploads that take long periods of timSometimes the files fail to completely upload for these users. A solutions architect must improve the app's performance for these uploads. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket. Configure the app to use the Transfer Acceleration endpoint for uploads.
answers.explanation: correct because S3 Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest AWS edge location and then across the AWS backbone network to us-east-1, significantly improving upload speed and reliability for users in distant locations such as Australia.

answers.content: Configure an S3 bucket in each Region to receive the uploads. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy the files to the distribution S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: incorrect because creating multiple regional buckets and replicating objects increases architectural complexity and does not directly optimize long-distance upload performance to the primary bucket.

answers.content: Set up Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing to route the uploads to the nearest S3 bucket Region.
answers.explanation: incorrect because latency-based routing applies to DNS resolution across multiple endpoints, and this scenario uses a single S3 bucket in one Region.

answers.content: Configure the app to break the video files into chunks. Use a multipart upload to transfer files to Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: correct because multipart upload improves performance and reliability for large files (1–10 GB) by uploading parts in parallel and allowing failed parts to be retried without restarting the entire upload.

answers.content: Modify the app to add random prefixes to the files before uploading.
answers.explanation: incorrect because adding random prefixes helps prevent partition hot spots but does not address high latency or failed uploads due to long-distance transfers.

questions.content: A company has an environment that has a single AWS account. A solutions architect is reviewing the environment to recommend what the company could improve specifically in terms of access to the AWS Management ConsolThe company's IT support workers currently access the console for administrative tasks, authenticating with named IAM users that have been mapped to their job rolThe IT support workers no longer want to maintain both their Active Directory and IAM user accounts. They want to be able to access the console by using their existing Active Directory credentials. The solutions architect is using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to implement this functionality. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on the IAM Identity Center feature in Organizations. Create and configure a directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) with a two-way trust to the company's on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and set the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory as the identity sourcCreate permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.
answers.explanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD involves higher operational cost and complexity compared to AD Connector, which is more cost-effective.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on the IAM Identity Center feature in Organizations. Create and configure an AD Connector to connect to the company's on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and select the AD Connector as the identity sourcCreate permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the company's Active Directory.
answers.explanation: Using federation with an identity provider is a best practice to avoid managing long-term credentials. AD Connector is a cost-effective hybrid solution to connect on-premises Active Directory to AWS IAM Identity Center without running an additional managed directory. IAM Identity Center supports AD Connector as an identity source, enabling users to sign in with existing Active Directory credentials. Turning on IAM Identity Center in AWS Organizations and mapping existing AD groups aligns with the requirement to avoid maintaining separate IAM user accounts.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on all features for the organization. Create and configure a directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) with a two-way trust to the company's on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and select the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory as the identity sourcCreate permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.
answers.explanation: Enabling all features is unnecessary; only enabling IAM Identity Center is required, adding extra overhead.

answers.content: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on all features for the organization. Create and configure an AD Connector to connect to the company's on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and set the AD Connector as the identity sourcCreate permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the company's Active Directory.
answers.explanation: Turning on all features is not needed and adds complexity; least required features should be enabled for cost-effectiveness.

questions.content: A financial services company in North America plans to release a new online web application to its customers on AWS. The company will launch the application in the us-east-1 Region on Amazon EC2 instances. The application must be highly available and must dynamically scale to meet user traffic. The company also wants to implement a disaster recovery environment for the application in the us-west-1 Region by using active-passive failover. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. Configure VPC peering. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Create an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Place the Auto Scaling group behind the ALB.
answers.explanation: ALB cannot extend across multiple VPCs via VPC peering; this is not supported and violates design best practices.

answers.content: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in that VPC. Create an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in the us-east-1 VPC. Place the Auto Scaling group behind the ALSet up the same configuration in the us-west-1 VPC. Create an Amazon Route 53 hosted zonCreate separate records for each ALEnable health checks to ensure high availability between Regions.
answers.explanation: Does not mention using a failover routing policy with Route 53 which is essential for active-passive failover, just health checks alone are insufficient.

answers.content: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in that VPCreate an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in the us-east-1 VPPlace the Auto Scaling group behind the ALB. Set up the same configuration in the us-west-1 VPCreate an Amazon Route 53 hosted zonCreate separate records for each ALB. Enable health checks and configure a failover routing policy for each record.
answers.explanation: Option C correctly uses separate VPCs in us-east-1 and us-west-1, each with an Application Load Balancer and Auto Scaling group spread across multiple Availability Zones, ensuring high availability and scalability in each region independently. It implements a disaster recovery strategy with active-passive failover via Route 53 by creating separate records for each ALB, enabling health checks, and configuring failover routing policy, which aligns with best practices for disaster recovery. This solution avoids improper multi-VPC ALB extensions and peering which is not a supported or recommended design. The use of Route 53 failover routing policy with health checks ensures Route 53 only routes traffic to healthy primary resources and fails over to secondary only when the primary is unhealthy, which meets the active-passive disaster recovery requirements.

answers.content: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. Configure VPC peering. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Create an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Place the Auto Scaling group behind the ALB. Create an Amazon Route 53 hosted zonCreate a record for the ALB.
answers.explanation: Uses ALB spanning multiple VPCs which is unsupported and lacks failover routing policy configuration for disaster recovery.

questions.content: A company runs a Python script on an Amazon EC2 instance to process data. The script runs every 10 minutes. The script ingests files from an Amazon S3 bucket and processes the files. On average, the script takes approximately 5 minutes to process each file The script will not reprocess a file that the script has already processed. The company reviewed Amazon CloudWatch metrics and noticed that the EC2 instance is idle for approximately 40% of the time because of the file processing speed. The company wants to make the workload highly available and scalablThe company also wants to reduce long-term management overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Migrate the data processing script to an AWS Lambda function. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function to process the objects when the company uploads the objects.
answers.explanation: Lambda functions have a maximum execution time of 15 minutes, which may be insufficient if files vary or processing sometimes exceeds 5 minutes; also, running long or compute-intensive processing in Lambda can be less cost-effective.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuConfigure Amazon S3 to send event notifications to the SQS queuCreate an EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum size of one instancUpdate the data processing script to poll the SQS queuProcess the S3 objects that the SQS message identifies.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 Auto Scaling groups and polling the SQS queue still requires managing EC2 instances, increasing management overhead and costs compared to serverless container solutions.

answers.content: Migrate the data processing script to a container imagRun the data processing container on an EC2 instancConfigure the container to poll the S3 bucket for new objects and to process the resulting objects.
answers.explanation: Running containers on EC2 instances involves manual infrastructure management and is less scalable and highly available than using ECS with Fargate.

answers.content: Migrate the data processing script to a container image that runs on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS FargatCreate an AWS Lambda function that calls the Fargate RunTaskAPI operation when the container processes the filUse an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Running the containerized data processing in Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate provides high availability and scalability with managed infrastructure, reducing long-term management overhead compared to managing EC2 instances directly. Using an S3 event notification to trigger a Lambda function that runs the Fargate task ensures processing is event-driven and starts promptly when files arrive, improving efficiency and reducing idle timThis solution avoids managing EC2 Auto Scaling groups manually and is more scalable and cost-effective than running constantly polling EC2 instances or containers. This aligns with AWS best practices to prefer managed services (Fargate, Lambda) and event-driven architectures for scalable, highly available workloads.

questions.content: A company has applications in an AWS account that is named SourcThe account is in an organization in AWS Organizations. One of the applications uses AWS Lambda functions and stores inventory data in an Amazon Aurora databasThe application deploys the Lambda functions by using a deployment packagThe company has configured automated backups for Aurora. The company wants to migrate the Lambda functions and the Aurora database to a new AWS account that is named Target. The application processes critical data, so the company must minimize downtimWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Download the Lambda function deployment package from the Source account. Use the deployment package and create new Lambda functions in the Target account. Share the automated Aurora DB cluster snapshot with the Target account.
answers.explanation: Aurora automated backups can be shared as DB cluster snapshots with the target account for migration. Lambda function deployment packages must be manually moved and recreated in the target account. AWS RAM does not support sharing Lambda functions. Sharing automated snapshots is the appropriate method for migrating Aurora DB clusters across accounts. Migrating using shared Aurora DB cluster snapshots aligns with AWS best practices for minimizing downtime.

answers.content: Download the Lambda function deployment package from the Source account. Use the deployment package and create new Lambda functions in the Target account. Share the Aurora DB cluster with the Target account by using AWS Resource Access Manager {AWS RAM). Grant the Target account permission to clone the Aurora DB cluster.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM cannot be used to share Aurora DB clusters across accounts; sharing snapshots is the correct method.

answers.content: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Lambda functions and the Aurora DB cluster with the Target account. Grant the Target account permission to clone the Aurora DB cluster.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM cannot share Lambda functions or Aurora DB clusters; thus this option is invalid.

answers.content: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Lambda functions with the Target account. Share the automated Aurora DB cluster snapshot with the Target account.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM cannot share Lambda functions; sharing only snapshots without redeploying Lambdas is insufficient.

questions.content: A company that uses AWS Organizations allows developers to experiment on AWS. As part of the landing zone that the company has deployed, developers use their company email address to request an account. The company wants to ensure that developers are not launching costly services or running services unnecessarily. The company must give developers a fixed monthly budget to limit their AWS costs. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create an SCP to set a fixed monthly account usage limit. Apply the SCP to the developer accounts.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Service Control Policies (SCPs) cannot enforce a fixed monthly spending limit; SCPs control permissions, not billing thresholds.

answers.content: Use AWS Budgets to create a fixed monthly budget for each developer's account as part of the account creation process.
answers.explanation: correct because AWS Budgets can be configured during account creation to define a fixed monthly spending limit per developer account.

answers.content: Create an SCP to deny access to costly services and components. Apply the SCP to the developer accounts.
answers.explanation: correct because an SCP can restrict access to specific costly services across developer accounts at the organization level.

answers.content: Create an IAM policy to deny access to costly services and components. Apply the IAM policy to the developer accounts.
answers.explanation: incorrect because IAM policies can be modified by users with sufficient permissions, whereas SCPs enforce guardrails at the organization level and are more appropriate for centralized control.

answers.content: Create an AWS Budgets alert action to terminate services when the budgeted amount is reached. Configure the action to terminate all services.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Budgets does not natively terminate all services automatically without an integration mechanism; it requires additional automation.

answers.content: Create an AWS Budgets alert action to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification when the budgeted amount is reached. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to terminate all services.
answers.explanation: correct because an AWS Budgets alert can publish to SNS, which can invoke a Lambda function to programmatically shut down resources when the budget threshold is reached.

questions.content: A startup company hosts a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets using the latest Amazon Linux 2 AMI. The company's engineers rely heavily on SSH access to the instances for troubleshooting. The company's existing architecture includes the following: • A VPC with private and public subnets, and a NAT gateway. • Site-to-Site VPN for connectivity with the on-premises environment. • EC2 security groups with direct SSH access from the on-premises environment. The company needs to increase security controls around SSH access and provide auditing of commands run by the engineers. Which strategy should a solutions architect use?

answers.content: Install and configure EC2 Instance Connect on the fleet of EC2 instances. Remove all security group rules attached to EC2 instances that allow inbound TCP on port 22. Advise the engineers to remotely access the instances by using the EC2 Instance Connect CLI.
answers.explanation: EC2 Instance Connect on instances in private subnets requires port 22 inbound access, which is less secure than removing SSH access entirely.

answers.content: Update the EC2 security groups to only allow inbound TCP on port 22 to the IP addresses of the engineer's devices. Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all EC2 instances and send operating system audit logs to CloudWatch Logs.
answers.explanation: Restricting SSH by IP and sending OS audit logs does not eliminate the security risk of open SSH ports and is less secure than using Session Manager.

answers.content: Update the EC2 security groups to only allow inbound TCP on port 22 to the IP addresses of the engineer's devices. Enable AWS Config for EC2 security group resource changes. Enable AWS Firewall Manager and apply a security group policy that automatically remediates changes to rules.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Config and Firewall Manager to monitor and remediate security group changes does not prevent exposure via SSH and does not provide session auditing.

answers.content: Create an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy attached. Attach the IAM role to all the EC2 instances. Remove all security group rules attached to the EC2 instances that allow inbound TCP on port 22. Have the engineers install the AWS Systems Manager Session Manager plugin for their devices and remotely access the instances by using the start-session API call from Systems Manager.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides secured, auditable, and centralized access to EC2 instances without opening SSH ports in security groups. Removing inbound TCP port 22 rules in security groups enhances security by eliminating direct SSH exposurSession Manager records sessions for auditing, meeting the requirement for command auditing by engineers. Attaching the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore IAM role to EC2 instances enables integration with Systems Manager, a managed AWS service providing secure access.

questions.content: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations. The company is using AWS Control Tower to deploy a landing zone for the organization. The company wants to implement governance and policy enforcement. The company must implement a policy that will detect Amazon RDS DB instances that are not encrypted at rest in the company's production OU. Which solution will meet this requirement?

answers.content: Turn on mandatory guardrails in AWS Control Tower. Apply the mandatory guardrails to the production OU.
answers.explanation: Mandatory guardrails are fixed and may not cover the specific RDS encryption detection required.

answers.content: Enable the appropriate guardrail from the list of strongly recommended guardrails in AWS Control Tower. Apply the guardrail to the production OU.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower provides strongly recommended guardrails for governance and policy enforcement, making it the preferred managed service solution for detecting non-compliant resources such as unencrypted RDS instances. Enabling the appropriate guardrail in Control Tower ensures automatic detection within the production OU with minimal custom effort and aligns with AWS best practices favoring managed enforcement. Turned on mandatory guardrails (option A) may not include the needed check as mandatory guardrails are fixed and cannot be customized, while B allows selection of a guardrail designed specifically to detect unencrypted RDS. AWS Config can remediate unencrypted RDS (from key facts), but creating a new mandatory guardrail via Config manually is not standard and less integrated with Control Tower governancSCPs cannot detect resource states like encryption and only restrict API actions, so they cannot enforce a detection policy for unencrypted RDS instances.

answers.content: Use AWS Config to create a new mandatory guardrail. Apply the rule to all accounts in the production OU.
answers.explanation: AWS Config alone does not create 'mandatory guardrails' and using Config outside the managed Control Tower guardrails is less preferable.

answers.content: Create a custom SCP in AWS Control Tower. Apply the SCP to the production OU.
answers.explanation: SCPs restrict actions but cannot detect or enforce resource encryption states.

questions.content: A video processing company has an application that downloads images from an Amazon S3 bucket, processes the images, stores a transformed image in a second S3 bucket, and updates metadata about the image in an Amazon DynamoDB tablThe application is written in Node.js and runs by using an AWS Lambda function. The Lambda function is invoked when a new image is uploaded to Amazon S3. The application ran without incident for a whilHowever, the size of the images has grown significantly. The Lambda function is now failing frequently with timeout errors. The function timeout is set to its maximum valuA solutions architect needs to refactor the application's architecture to prevent invocation failures. The company does not want to manage the underlying infrastructurWhich combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Modify the application deployment by building a Docker image that contains the application codPublish the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR).
answers.explanation: correct because packaging the application as a Docker image and storing it in Amazon ECR enables running the workload in a container environment that supports longer processing times than Lambda.

answers.content: Create a new Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task definition with a compatibility type of AWS FargatConfigure the task definition to use the new image in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Adjust the Lambda function to invoke an ECS task by using the ECS task definition when a new file arrives in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: correct because running the container as an ECS task on AWS Fargate removes Lambda timeout limitations while remaining serverless and eliminating infrastructure management, and the Lambda function can trigger the Fargate task when a new object is uploaded.

answers.content: Create an AWS Step Functions state machine with a Parallel state to invoke the Lambda function. Increase the provisioned concurrency of the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: incorrect because increasing provisioned concurrency does not resolve Lambda timeout limits, and Step Functions parallelization does not solve long-running processing constraints.

answers.content: Create a new Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task definition with a compatibility type of Amazon EC2. Configure the task definition to use the new image in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Adjust the Lambda function to invoke an ECS task by using the ECS task definition when a new file arrives in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: incorrect because ECS with EC2 launch type requires managing underlying EC2 instances, which violates the requirement to avoid managing infrastructure.

answers.content: Modify the application to store images on Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) and to store metadata on an Amazon RDS DB instancAdjust the Lambda function to mount the EFS file share.
answers.explanation: incorrect because moving to EFS and RDS does not address the Lambda timeout issue and introduces additional infrastructure and operational overhead.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate an application to Amazon EC2 from VMware Infrastructure that runs in an on-premises data center. A solutions architect must preserve the software and configuration settings during the migration. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure the AWS DataSync agent to start replicating the data store to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Use the SMB share to host the VMware data storUse VM Import/Export to move the VMs to Amazon EC2.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync and FSx for Windows File Server are for file storage data transfer, not VM image migration.

answers.content: Use the VMware vSphere client to export the application as an image in Open Virtualization Format (OVF) format. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the image in the destination AWS Region. Create and apply an IAM role for VM Import. Use the AWS CLI to run the EC2 import command.
answers.explanation: The best practice for migrating VMware VMs to EC2 is to export them as OVF format and use VM Import/Export features to preserve software and configuration. Creating an IAM role and using the AWS CLI to run the import command aligns with managed AWS services. Storing the image in S3 is secure and standard practice for import operations. This option directly addresses migrating VMs and preserving settings without manual or unsupported backup methods.

answers.content: Configure AWS Storage Gateway for files service to export a Common Internet File System (CIFS) sharCreate a backup copy to the shared folder. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and create an AMI from the backup copy. Launch an EC2 instance that is based on the AMI.
answers.explanation: Storage Gateway files service and creating AMI from a backup copy is not a supported or reliable method for migrating VMs preserving configurations.

answers.content: Create a managed-instance activation for a hybrid environment in AWS Systems Manager. Download and install Systems Manager Agent on the on-premises VM. Register the VM with Systems Manager to be a managed instancUse AWS Backup to create a snapshot of the VM and create an AMI. Launch an EC2 instance that is based on the AMI.
answers.explanation: Using Systems Manager and AWS Backup to snapshot an on-prem VM to create an AMI is not a supported or documented approach for VM migration.

questions.content: A finance company hosts a data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives financial data records over SFTP each night from several third parties. The company runs its own SFTP server on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet of a VPC. After the files are uploaded, they are moved to the data lake by a cron job that runs on the same instancThe SFTP server is reachable on DNS sftp.example.com through the use of Amazon Route 53. What should a solutions architect do to improve the reliability and scalability of the SFTP solution?

answers.content: Move the EC2 instance into an Auto Scaling group. Place the EC2 instance behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the DNS record sftp.example.com in Route 53 to point to the ALB.
answers.explanation: An Auto Scaling group with an ALB is not ideal for SFTP since ALBs do not support the SFTP protocol natively, leading to potential issues.

answers.content: Migrate the SFTP server to AWS Transfer for SFTP. Update the DNS record sftp.example.com in Route 53 to point to the server endpoint hostname.
answers.explanation: AWS Transfer for SFTP is a managed service designed specifically for SFTP workloads, improving reliability and scalability without the need to manage EC2 instances. Moving to AWS Transfer for SFTP removes the burden of maintaining and scaling an EC2-based SFTP server, aligning with best practices favoring managed services. Updating the DNS record to point to the managed service endpoint is straightforward and maintains the current connectivity model. This option avoids complexities and potential bottlenecks associated with using load balancers with custom EC2 SFTP servers.

answers.content: Migrate the SFTP server to a file gateway in AWS Storage Gateway. Update the DNS record sftp.example.com in Route 53 to point to the file gateway endpoint.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway file gateway is not designed to host an SFTP server or handle SFTP traffic, making it unsuitable for this use case.

answers.content: Place the EC2 instance behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Update the DNS record sftp.example.com in Route 53 to point to the NLB.
answers.explanation: Placing the EC2 instance behind an NLB adds complexity but does not inherently solve reliability or scalability issues of the EC2-based SFTP server.

questions.content: A company built an application based on AWS Lambda deployed in an AWS CloudFormation stack. The last production release of the web application introduced an issue that resulted in an outage lasting several minutes. A solutions architect must adjust the deployment process to support a canary releasWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an alias for every new deployed version of the Lambda function. Use the AWS CLI update-alias command with the routing-config parameter to distribute the load.
answers.explanation: Lambda supports alias-based traffic shifting with routing configurations to enable canary deployments. Using aliases and the update-alias command with routing-config is an AWS best practice for gradual Lambda version traffic shifting. This approach leverages managed Lambda features for canary releases without manual or complex routing setup.

answers.content: Deploy the application into a new CloudFormation stack. Use an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy to distribute the load.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because using separate CloudFormation stacks and Route 53 weighted routing is more complex and less integrated with Lambda deployment mechanisms.

answers.content: Create a version for every new deployed Lambda function. Use the AWS CLI update-function-configuration command with the routing-config parameter to distribute the load.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because update-function-configuration does not support routing-config parameter; routing is handled via aliases.

answers.content: Configure AWS CodeDeploy and use CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime in the Deployment configuration to distribute the load.
answers.explanation: Incorrect because CodeDeployOneAtATime is a linear deployment, not a traffic-shifting canary deployment.

questions.content: A solutions architect needs to copy data from an Amazon S3 bucket m an AWS account to a new S3 bucket in a new AWS account. The solutions architect must implement a solution that uses the AWS CLI. Which combination of steps will successfully copy the data? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a bucket policy to allow the source bucket to list its contents and to put objects and set object ACLs in the destination bucket. Attach the bucket policy to the destination bucket.
answers.explanation: incorrect because a bucket policy on the destination bucket cannot grant permissions for listing and reading objects from the source bucket; access to the source bucket must be granted in the source account.

answers.content: Create a bucket policy to allow a user in the destination account to list the source bucket's contents and read the source bucket's objects. Attach the bucket policy to the source bucket.
answers.explanation: correct because the source bucket must have a bucket policy that allows the destination account (or user) to list and read objects for cross-account access.

answers.content: Create an IAM policy in the source account. Configure the policy to allow a user in the source account to list contents and get objects in the source bucket, and to list contents, put objects, and set object ACLs in the destination bucket. Attach the policy to the user.
answers.explanation: incorrect because permissions in the source account alone are insufficient to write to a bucket in another account without proper permissions granted in the destination account.

answers.content: Create an IAM policy in the destination account. Configure the policy to allow a user in the destination account to list contents and get objects in the source bucket, and to list contents, put objects, and set objectACLs in the destination bucket. Attach the policy to the user.
answers.explanation: correct because the user in the destination account needs IAM permissions to read from the source bucket and write (put objects and set ACLs) to the destination bucket.

answers.content: Run the aws s3 sync command as a user in the source account. Specify the source and destination buckets to copy the data.
answers.explanation: incorrect because running the sync command from the source account would require cross-account write permissions that are not established in this option set.

answers.content: Run the aws s3 sync command as a user in the destination account. Specify the source and destination buckets to copy the data.
answers.explanation: correct because running aws s3 sync as a user in the destination account with proper cross-account read permissions on the source bucket and write permissions on the destination bucket enables successful data copy.

questions.content: A company has an organization that has many AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. A solutions architect must improve how the company manages common security group rules for the AWS accounts in the organization. The company has a common set of IP CIDR ranges in an allow list in each AWS account to allow access to and from the company's on-premises network. Developers within each account are responsible for adding new IP CIDR ranges to their security groups. The security team has its own AWS account. Currently, the security team notifies the owners of the other AWS accounts when changes are made to the allow list. The solutions architect must design a solution that distributes the common set of CIDR ranges across all accounts. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answers.content: Set up an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in the security team's AWS account. Deploy an AWS Lambda function in each AWS account. Configure the Lambda function to run every time an SNS topic receives a messagConfigure the Lambda function to take an IP address as input and add it to a list of security groups in the account. Instruct the security team to distribute changes by publishing messages to its SNS topic.
answers.explanation: Deploying Lambda functions in each account with SNS integration increases operational overhead and complexity.

answers.content: Create new customer-managed prefix lists in each AWS account within the organization. Populate the prefix lists in each account with all internal CIDR ranges. Notify the owner of each AWS account to allow the new customer-managed prefix list IDs in their accounts in their security groups. Instruct the security team to share updates with each AWS account owner.
answers.explanation: Creating prefix lists in each account individually duplicates effort and requires manual updates by account owners.
