answers.content: Create a new customer-managed prefix list in the security team's AWS account. Populate the customer-managed prefix list with all internal CIDR ranges. Share the customer-managed prefix list with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager. Notify the owner of each AWS account to allow the new customer-managed prefix list ID in their security groups.
answers.explanation: Using a customer-managed prefix list in the security team's AWS account allows centralized management of common CIDR ranges. Sharing the prefix list with all accounts in the organization through AWS Resource Access Manager ensures consistent and secure distribution. Notifying account owners to reference the shared prefix list maintains security best practices by avoiding direct edits or manual updates to each account's security groups. This approach minimizes operational overhead compared to deploying Lambda functions or requiring cross-account role assumptions. It leverages managed AWS services designed for sharing and managing network configuration data with least complexity.

answers.content: Create an IAM role in each account in the organization. Grant permissions to update security groups. Deploy an AWS Lambda function in the security team's AWS account. Configure the Lambda function to take a list of internal IP addresses as input, assume a role in each organization account, and add the list of IP addresses to the security groups in each account.
answers.explanation: Cross-account role assumptions and Lambda updates from the security team's account add operational complexity and risk.

questions.content: A company has developed a web application. The company is hosting the application on a group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to improve the security posture of the application and plans to use AWS WAF web ACLs. The solution must not adversely affect legitimate traffic to the application. How should a solutions architect configure the web ACLs to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Set the action of the web ACL rules to Count. Enable AWS WAF logging. Analyze the requests for false positives. Modify the rules to avoid any false positivOver time, change the action of the web ACL rules from Count to Block.
answers.explanation: Setting the web ACL rules to Count initially allows monitoring without blocking legitimate traffic, which helps to identify false positives. Enabling AWS WAF logging and analyzing requests supports refinement of rules to minimize impact on legitimate traffic. Gradually changing the action from Count to Block follows a security best practice of testing before enforcement, ensuring improved security posture without adversely affecting users. This approach aligns with security best practices prioritizing careful rule deployment and managed AWS WAF features.

answers.content: Use only rate-based rules in the web ACLs, and set the throttle limit as high as possiblTemporarily block all requests that exceed the limit. Define nested rules to narrow the scope of the rate tracking.
answers.explanation: Using only rate-based rules with high throttle limits and temporary blocks can disrupt legitimate traffic without reliable assessment and refinement.

answers.content: Set the action of the web ACL rules to Block. Use only AWS managed rule groups in the web ACLs. Evaluate the rule groups by using Amazon CloudWatch metrics with AWS WAF sampled requests or AWS WAF logs.
answers.explanation: Setting rules directly to Block without prior analysis risks blocking legitimate traffic and does not allow for tuning to avoid false positives.

answers.content: Use only custom rule groups in the web ACLs, and set the action to Allow. Enable AWS WAF logging. Analyze the requests for false positives. Modify the rules to avoid any false positivOver time, change the action of the web ACL rules from Allow to Block.
answers.explanation: Using only custom rule groups with Allow action and later switching to Block could inadvertently allow malicious traffic initially and is less secure.

questions.content: A solutions architect needs to implement a client-side encryption mechanism for objects that will be stored in a new Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect created a CMK that is stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) for this purposThe solutions architect created the following IAM policy and attached it to an IAM role: [https://img.examtopics.com/aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02/image7.png] During tests, the solutions architect was able to successfully get existing test objects in the S3 bucket. However, attempts to upload a new object resulted in an error messagThe error message stated that the action was forbidden. Which action must the solutions architect add to the IAM policy to meet all the requirements?

answers.content: kms:GenerateDataKey
answers.explanation: Uploading new objects using client-side encryption with a CMK in AWS KMS requires permission to generate data keys. The IAM policy must include the kms:GenerateDataKey action to allow the encryption process to generate the data key used to encrypt objects client-side before uploading. The provided key facts explicitly show that kms:GenerateDataKey is necessary when using CMKs with S3 for encryption and decryption operations.

answers.content: kms:GetKeyPolicy
answers.explanation: kms:GetKeyPolicy is not required for encrypting or uploading objects; it is used for retrieving the key policy itself.

answers.content: kms:GetPublicKey
answers.explanation: kms:GetPublicKey is for asymmetric CMKs and not needed for standard client-side encryption with symmetric CMKs.

answers.content: kms:Sign
answers.explanation: kms:Sign is related to digital signature operations, not required for encryption or object uploads to S3.

questions.content: A company is refactoring its on-premises order-processing platform in the AWS Cloud. The platform includes a web front end that is hosted on a fleet of VMs, RabbitMQ to connect the front end to the backend, and a Kubernetes cluster to run a containerized backend system to process the orders. The company does not want to make any major changes to the application. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an AMI of the web server VM. Create an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI and an Application Load Balancer. Set up Amazon MQ to replace the on-premises messaging queuConfigure Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to host the order-processing backend.
answers.explanation: Option A uses Amazon MQ, a managed service designed to replace RabbitMQ with minimal changes. It uses Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Load Balancer to replicate the existing VM-based web front end with minimal application changAmazon EKS is used for the containerized backend, avoiding manual Kubernetes management and reducing operational overhead compared to self-managed Kubernetes. This solution aligns with the requirement to avoid major application changes and minimizes operational effort by leveraging managed services.

answers.content: Create a custom AWS Lambda runtime to mimic the web server environment. Create an Amazon API Gateway API to replace the front-end web servers. Set up Amazon MQ to replace the on-premises messaging queuConfigure Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to host the order-processing backend.
answers.explanation: Replacing the web front end with Lambda and API Gateway requires code changes and refactoring, violating the minimal change requirement.

answers.content: Create an AMI of the web server VM. Create an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI and an Application Load Balancer. Set up Amazon MQ to replace the on-premises messaging queuInstall Kubernetes on a fleet of different EC2 instances to host the order-processing backend.
answers.explanation: Installing Kubernetes manually on EC2 instances increases operational overhead compared to using Amazon EKS.

answers.content: Create an AMI of the web server VM. Create an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI and an Application Load Balancer. Set up an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to replace the on-premises messaging queuConfigure Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to host the order-processing backend.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SQS requires changing the messaging pattern because SQS is a different type of service than RabbitMQ, likely causing more application changes.

questions.content: A company has migrated Its forms-processing application to AWS. When users interact with the application, they upload scanned forms as files through a web application. A database stores user metadata and references to files that are stored in Amazon S3. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databasWhen forms are uploaded, the application sends notifications to a team through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). A team member then logs in and processes each form. The team member performs data validation on the form and extracts relevant data before entering the information into another system that uses an API. A solutions architect needs to automate the manual processing of the forms. The solution must provide accurate form extraction. minimize time to market, and minimize tong-term operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Develop custom libraries to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms. Deploy the libraries to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster as an application tier. Use this tier to process the forms when forms are uploaded. Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data into an Amazon DynamoDB tablSubmit the data to the target system's APL. Host the new application tier on EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Involves developing custom OCR libraries and managing Kubernetes and EC2 manually, increasing operational overhead and time to market.

answers.content: Extend the system with an application tier that uses AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Configure this tier to use artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) models that are trained and hosted on an EC2 instance to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms when forms are uploaded. Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.
answers.explanation: Requires training and hosting AI/ML models on EC2, increasing operational overhead and complexity compared to managed services.

answers.content: Host a new application tier on EC2 instances. Use this tier to call endpoints that host artificial intelligence and machine teaming (AI/ML) models that are trained and hosted in Amazon SageMaker to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms. Store the output in Amazon ElastiCachParse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.
answers.explanation: Uses EC2 and SageMaker-hosted models requiring management of infrastructure and does not minimize operational overhead like managed services.

answers.content: Extend the system with an application tier that uses AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Configure this tier to use Amazon Textract and Amazon Comprehend to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms when forms are uploaded. Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.
answers.explanation: Amazon Textract is a managed AWS service specifically designed for optical character recognition (OCR) and extracting text and data from scanned documents. Amazon Comprehend can be used to analyze and understand the extracted text, providing improved data processing. Using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda allows for serverless orchestration and automation, reducing operational overhead and minimizing time to market. This solution leverages fully managed AWS services, aligning with best practices for security, maintainability, and reducing long-term operational overhead.

questions.content: A video processing company wants to build a machine learning (ML) model by using 600 TB of compressed data that is stored as thousands of files in the company's on-premises network attached storage system. The company does not have the necessary compute resources on premises for ML experiments and wants to use AWS. The company needs to complete the data transfer to AWS within 3 weeks. The data transfer will be a one-time transfer. The data must be encrypted in transit. The measured upload speed of the company's internet connection is 100 Mbps. and multiple departments share the connection. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Order several AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices by using the AWS Management ConsolConfigure the devices with a destination S3 bucket. Copy the data to the devices. Ship the devices back to AWS.
answers.explanation: The data transfer is large (600 TB) and needs to be done within 3 weeks, which is not feasible over a 100 Mbps shared internet connection. AWS Snowball Edge devices provide a physical transport method that encrypts data in transit and is designed for large one-time data transfers. Order and return of Snowball Edge devices is cost-effective compared to the expense of setting up Direct Connect or relying solely on internet VPNs for such large amounts of data. Snowball Edge meets the requirement of encrypted data transfer using AES-256 encryption at both virtual and physical layers according to the provided facts.

answers.content: Set up a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the company location and the nearest AWS Region. Transfer the data over a VPN connection into the Region to store the data in Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Setting up Direct Connect is costly and may take more time; also, the upload speed is limited by shared internet connection for VPN, making it impractical within 3 weeks.

answers.content: Create a VPN connection between the on-premises network attached storage and the nearest AWS Region. Transfer the data over the VPN connection.
answers.explanation: VPN over the existing 100 Mbps internet connection is too slow to transfer 600 TB within 3 weeks.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway on premises. Configure the file gateway with a destination S3 bucket. Copy the data to the file gateway.
answers.explanation: Storage Gateway file gateway requires data transfer over the internet connection, which is too slow for 600 TB within 3 weeks and is not optimized for large one-time transfers.

questions.content: A company is running an application in the AWS Cloud. The application collects and stores a large amount of unstructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The S3 bucket contains several terabytes of data and uses the S3 Standard storage class. The data increases in size by several gigabytes every day. The company needs to query and analyze the data. The company does not access data that is more than 1 year old. However, the company must retain all the data indefinitely for compliance reasons. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Use S3 Select to query the data. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition data that is more than 1 year old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: S3 Select is limited to querying individual objects and is not suitable for querying large datasets across many objects efficiently.

answers.content: Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the data. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition data that is more than 1 year old 10 S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: Amazon Redshift Spectrum involves managing Redshift clusters which adds cost and complexity versus serverless Athena.

answers.content: Use an AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Athena to query the data. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition data that is more than 1 year old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answers.explanation: Amazon Athena with AWS Glue Data Catalog is designed for querying unstructured data directly in S3 without the need for data loading or transformation. Athena supports cost-effective query execution since you pay per query and storage remains in S3. S3 Lifecycle policies transitioning data older than 1 year to S3 Glacier Deep Archive reduces storage costs while retaining compliance with indefinite retention requirements. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class suitable for long-term data retention that is infrequently accessed.

answers.content: Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the data. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition data that is more than 1 year old to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is more costly than Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage and does not match the cost-effectiveness for infrequently accessed data requiring indefinite retention.

questions.content: A company consists or two separate business units. Each business unit has its own AWS account within a single organization in AWS Organizations. The business units regularly share sensitive documents with each other. To facilitate sharing, the company created an Amazon S3 bucket in each account and configured low-way replication between the S3 buckets. The S3 buckets have millions of objects. Recently, a security audit identified that neither S3 bucket has encryption at rest enabled. Company policy requires that all documents must be stored with encryption at rest. The company wants to implement server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

answers.content: Turn on SSE-S3 on both S3 buckets. Use S3 Batch Operations to copy and encrypt the objects in the same location.
answers.explanation: SSE-S3 can be enabled by turning on default encryption on the S3 bucket, which applies to all new objects. Existing unencrypted objects must be copied or reprocessed to apply encryption because default encryption does not affect existing objects. S3 Batch Operations is a managed AWS service that can efficiently handle millions of objects for encryption applying server-side encryption using SSE-S3. This approach aligns with security best practices by ensuring all existing and new objects are encrypted at rest with SSE-S3, using managed services for operational efficiency.

answers.content: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in each account. Turn on server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) on each S3 bucket by using the corresponding KMS key in that AWS account. Encrypt the existing objects by using an S3 copy command in the AWS CLI.
answers.explanation: SSE-KMS is not required; the question specifically mandates SSE-S3 for encryption, and using KMS adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Turn on SSE-S3 on both S3 buckets. Encrypt the existing objects by using an S3 copy command in the AWS CLI.
answers.explanation: Using an S3 copy command in the AWS CLI for millions of objects is not operationally efficient compared to managed batch operations.

answers.content: Create an AWS Key Management Service, (AWS KMS) key in each account. Turn on server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) on each S3 bucket by using the corresponding KMS key in that AWS account. Use S3 Batch Operations to copy the objects into the same location.
answers.explanation: SSE-KMS is not required, and managing KMS keys adds complexity contrary to the requirement of SSE-S3; also, batch operations with KMS is more complex and less operationally efficient.

questions.content: A company has VPC flow logs enabled for Its NAT gateway. The company is seeing Action = ACCEPT for inbound traffic that comes from public IP address 198.51.100.2 destined for a private Amazon EC2 instancA solutions architect must determine whether the traffic represents unsolicited inbound connections from the internet. The first two octets of the VPC CIDR block are 203.0. Which set of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Open the AWS CloudTrail consolSelect the log group that contains the NAT gateway's elastic network interface and the private instance's elastic network interlacRun a query to filter with the destination address set as "like 203.0" and the source address set as "like 198.51.100.2". Run the stats command to filter the sum of bytes transferred by the source address and the destination address.
answers.explanation: AWS CloudTrail does not log VPC flow logs, which are in CloudWatch Logs.

answers.content: Open the Amazon CloudWatch consolSelect the log group that contains the NAT gateway's elastic network interface and the private instance's elastic network interfacRun a query to filter with the destination address set as "like 203.0" and the source address set as "like 198.51.100.2". Run the stats command to filter the sum of bytes transferred by the source address and the destination address.
answers.explanation: VPC flow logs are delivered to CloudWatch Logs, so analysis should be done in the Amazon CloudWatch console, not AWS CloudTrail. The destination address for traffic destined to a private instance should match the VPC CIDR's first two octets (203.0). The source address to check for unsolicited inbound traffic is the public IP address (198.51.100.2). Filtering with destination address like 203.0 and source address like 198.51.100.2 matches the scenario correctly to identify unsolicited inbound connections. Running a stats command to summarize bytes transferred helps in quantifying and analyzing the traffic.

answers.content: Open the AWS CloudTrail consolSelect the log group that contains the NAT gateway's elastic network interface and the private instance's elastic network interfacRun a query to filter with the destination address set as "like 198.51.100.2" and the source address set as "like 203.0". Run the stats command to filter the sum of bytes transferred by the source address and the destination address.
answers.explanation: Swaps source and destination IPs incorrectly for the filtering criteria.

answers.content: Open the Amazon CloudWatch consolSelect the log group that contains the NAT gateway's elastic network interface and the private instance's elastic network interfacRun a query to filter with the destination address set as "like 198.51.100.2" and the source address set as "like 203.0". Run the stats command to filter the sum of bytes transferred by the source address and the destination address.
answers.explanation: Swaps source and destination IPs incorrectly for the filtering criteria.

questions.content: A company is using AWS CloudFormation to deploy its infrastructurThe company is concerned that, if a production CloudFormation stack is deleted, important data stored in Amazon RDS databases or Amazon EBS volumes might also be deleted. How can the company prevent users from accidentally deleting data in this way?

answers.content: Modify the CloudFormation templates to add a DeletionPolicy attribute to RDS and EBS resources.
answers.explanation: Adding a DeletionPolicy attribute to RDS and EBS resources in the CloudFormation template explicitly prevents accidental deletion of these resources when the stack is deleted. DeletionPolicy is a native CloudFormation feature designed exactly for this purpose, making it a managed service solution aligned with AWS best practices. Stack policies and IAM policies focus on controlling who can perform actions but do not inherently prevent data loss upon stack deletion. AWS Config rules monitor compliance and can alert or remediate, but do not directly prevent resource deletion during stack deletion as effectively as DeletionPolicy.

answers.content: Configure a stack policy that disallows the deletion of RDS and EBS resources.
answers.explanation: Stack policies do not prevent resource deletion but restrict actions on stack resources conditionally, which is less direct and less effective than DeletionPolicy for protecting data.

answers.content: Modify IAM policies lo deny deleting RDS and EBS resources that are tagged with an "aws:cloudformation:stack-name" tag.
answers.explanation: IAM policies can restrict actions but managing policies for tags is complex and error-prone, and they do not cover deletion protection during stack deletion inherently.

answers.content: Use AWS Config rules to prevent deleting RDS and EBS resources.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules provide monitoring and compliance but do not prevent deletion automatically and are reactive rather than proactive in preventing data loss.

questions.content: A company wants to change its internal cloud billing strategy for each of its business units. Currently, the cloud governance team shares reports for overall cloud spending with the head of each business unit. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage the separate AWS accounts for each business unit. The existing tagging standard in Organizations includes the application, environment, and owner. The cloud governance team wants a centralized solution so each business unit receives monthly reports on its cloud spending. The solution should also send notifications for any cloud spending that exceeds a set threshold. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective way to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure AWS Budgets in each account and configure budget alerts that are grouped by application, environment, and owner. Add each business unit to an Amazon SNS topic for each alert. Use Cost Explorer in each account to create monthly reports for each business unit.
answers.explanation: Configuring budgets and reports in each individual account increases operational overhead and complexity rather than centralizing management.

answers.content: Configure AWS Budgets in the organization's management account and configure budget alerts that are grouped by application, environment, and owner. Add each business unit to an Amazon SNS topic for each alert. Use Cost Explorer in the organization's management account to create monthly reports for each business unit.
answers.explanation: AWS Budgets can be configured in the organization's management account to centrally manage and monitor budgets across member accounts, making it cost-effective and centralized. Budget alerts grouped by tags such as application, environment, and owner can effectively split costs among business units. Using Cost Explorer in the management account provides a centralized and consolidated view for monthly reporting, reducing the complexity of managing multiple accounts separately. This approach avoids the overhead and complexity of deploying and maintaining custom Lambda functions, and uses managed services for cost tracking and alerting.

answers.content: Configure AWS Budgets in each account and configure budget alerts that are grouped by application, environment, and owner. Add each business unit to an Amazon SNS topic for each alert. Use the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard in each account to create monthly reports for each business unit.
answers.explanation: Using the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard in each account is less efficient and increases manual work compared to centralized management in the organization's management account.

answers.content: Enable AWS Cost and Usage Reports in the organization's management account and configure reports grouped by application, environment. and owner. Create an AWS Lambda function that processes AWS Cost and Usage Reports, sends budget alerts, and sends monthly reports to each business unit's email list.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Lambda to process reports and send alerts introduces unnecessary custom complexity and maintenance overhead; managed services are preferred.

questions.content: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect is designing VPC infrastructure in an AWS Region where the application needs to access an Amazon Aurora DB Cluster. The EC2 instances are all associated with the same security group. The DB cluster is associated with its own security group. The solutions architect needs to add rules to the security groups to provide the application with least privilege access to the DB Cluster. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Add an inbound rule to the EC2 instances' security group. Specify the DB cluster's security group as the source over the default Aurora port.
answers.explanation: incorrect because EC2 instances do not need an inbound rule for database access; they initiate the connection.

answers.content: Add an outbound rule to the EC2 instances' security group. Specify the DB cluster's security group as the destination over the default Aurora port.
answers.explanation: required because the EC2 instances’ security group must allow outbound traffic to the DB cluster’s security group on the database port. Although security groups allow all outbound traffic by default, explicitly restricting outbound traffic to only the DB security group over the required port enforces least privilege.

answers.content: Add an inbound rule to the DB cluster's security group. Specify the EC2 instances' security group as the source over the default Aurora port.
answers.explanation: required because the Aurora DB cluster’s security group must allow inbound traffic from the EC2 instances’ security group on the default Aurora port (e.g., 3306 for MySQL or 5432 for PostgreSQL). This permits the application to connect to the database with least privilege.

answers.content: Add an outbound rule to the DB cluster's security group. Specify the EC2 instances' security group as the destination over the default Aurora port.
answers.explanation: incorrect because the DB cluster does not initiate connections to EC2 instances.

answers.content: Add an outbound rule to the DB cluster's security group. Specify the EC2 instances' security group as the destination over the ephemeral ports.
answers.explanation: incorrect because return traffic is automatically allowed by security groups due to their stateful nature; ephemeral port rules are unnecessary.

questions.content: A company plans to refactor a monolithic application into a modern application design deployed on AWS. The CI/CD pipeline needs to be upgraded to support the modern design for the application with the following requirements: • It should allow changes to be released several times every hour. • It should be able to roll back the changes as quickly as possiblWhich design will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Deploy a CI/CD pipeline that incorporates AMIs to contain the application and their configurations. Deploy the application by replacing Amazon EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Replacing EC2 instances with AMIs is slower and more error-prone, limiting the ability to release multiple times per hour with quick rollbacks.

answers.content: Specify AWS Elastic Beanstalk to stage in a secondary environment as the deployment target for the CI/CD pipeline of the application. To deploy, swap the staging and production environment URLs.
answers.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk supports blue/green deployments by staging a secondary environment and swapping environment URLs, which enables rapid releases and quick rollbacks. This approach aligns with CI/CD best practices by allowing environment isolation during deployment, reducing downtime, and providing fast rollback capabilities. Other options rely on managing EC2 instances and AMIs manually, which is less automated and slower to rollback compared to Elastic Beanstalk’s managed environment swap.

answers.content: Use AWS Systems Manager to re-provision the infrastructure for each deployment. Update the Amazon EC2 user data to pull the latest code artifact from Amazon S3 and use Amazon Route 53 weighted routing to point to the new environment.
answers.explanation: Reprovisioning infrastructure with Systems Manager and using Route 53 weighted routing adds complexity and slower rollback compared to Elastic Beanstalk environment swaps.

answers.content: Roll out the application updates as part of an Auto Scaling event using prebuilt AMIs. Use new versions of the AMIs to add instances. and phase out all instances that use the previous AMI version with the configured termination policy during a deployment event.
answers.explanation: Rolling out updates through autoscaling events with AMI versioning is less flexible and slower compared to Elastic Beanstalk’s direct environment swapping, making quick rollback harder.

questions.content: A company has its cloud infrastructure on AWS. A solutions architect needs to define the infrastructure as codThe infrastructure is currently deployed in one AWS Region. The company's business expansion plan includes deployments in multiple Regions across multiple AWS accounts. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation templates. Add IAM policies to control the various accounts, Deploy the templates across the multiple Regions.
answers.explanation: Does not address multi-account management or scalable deployment across multiple accounts securely.

answers.content: Use AWS Organizations. Deploy AWS CloudFormation templates from the management account Use AWS Control Tower to manage deployments across accounts.
answers.explanation: Mixes AWS Control Tower without clarifying deployment mechanisms; Control Tower manages landing zones, not direct template deployment.

answers.content: Use AWS Organizations and AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Deploy a Cloud Formation template from an account that has the necessary IAM permissions.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Organizations enables centralized governance across multiple AWS accounts, aligning with the requirement for multi-account deployments. AWS CloudFormation StackSets allow deployment of CloudFormation templates across multiple accounts and Regions from a single administrator account. This approach ensures proper IAM permissions are used to securely manage infrastructure deployment. StackSets is a managed service designed specifically for multi-account and multi-Region infrastructure as code deployments, adhering to best practices.

answers.content: Use nested stacks with AWS CloudFormation templates. Change the Region by using nested stacks.
answers.explanation: Nested stacks do not handle deployment across multiple Regions or accounts and do not provide centralized management.

questions.content: A company uses Amazon S3 to store files and images in a variety of storage classes. The company's S3 costs have increased substantially during the past year. A solutions architect needs to review data trends for the past 12 months and identity the appropriate storage class for the objects. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Download AWS Cost and Usage Reports for the last 12 months of S3 usagReview AWS Trusted Advisor recommendations for cost savings.
answers.explanation: Cost and Usage Reports track billing but do not provide specific storage class usage and access pattern analysis for S3 objects.

answers.content: Use S3 storage class analysis. Import data trends into an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to analyze storage trends.
answers.explanation: S3 Storage Class Analysis is a great tool, but it is typically used at the bucket or prefix level rather than providing a global 12-month trend review. It focuses on recommending transitions to S3 Standard-IA, but Storage Lens Advanced offers a more holistic dashboard approach for broad data trends.

answers.content: Use Amazon S3 Storage Lens. Upgrade the default dashboard to include advanced metrics for storage trends.
answers.explanation: most effective solution because S3 Storage Lens Advanced Metrics provides 15 months of historical data and organization-wide cost optimization recommendations, which are essential for analyzing long-term storage trends.

answers.content: Use Access Analyzer for S3. Download the Access Analyzer for S3 report for the last 12 months. Import the .csv file to an Amazon QuickSight dashboard.
answers.explanation: Access Analyzer for S3 focuses on resource permissions and access auditing, not on storage cost trends or storage class suitability.

questions.content: An adventure company has launched a new feature on its mobile app. Users can use the feature to upload their hiking and rafting photos and videos anytimThe photos and videos are stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage in an S3 bucket and are served through Amazon CloudFront. The company needs to optimize the cost of the storagA solutions architect discovers that most of the uploaded photos and videos are accessed infrequently after 30 days. However, some of the uploaded photos and videos are accessed frequently after 30 days. The solutions architect needs to implement a solution that maintains millisecond retrieval availability of the photos and videos at the lowest possible cost. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing cost while maintaining millisecond retrieval timS3 Glacier Deep Archive (Option B) does not provide millisecond retrieval, which is required. Replacing S3 with EFS (Option C) is not cost-effective and does not align with object storage best practices. Adding Cache-Control headers (Option D) does not reduce storage costs, only affects caching behavior.

answers.content: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition image objects and video objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
answers.explanation: S3 Glacier Deep Archive does not provide millisecond retrieval times.

answers.content: Replace Amazon S3 with an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on Amazon EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS is not suitable for cost-optimized object storage and retrieval at scale for this use case.

answers.content: Add a Cache-Control: max-age header to the S3 image objects and S3 video objects. Set the header to 30 days.
answers.explanation: Cache-Control headers do not reduce storage costs and do not address infrequent access optimization.

questions.content: A company is building an electronic document management system in which users upload their documents. The application stack is entirely serverless and runs on AWS in the eu-central-1 Region. The system includes a web application that uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution for delivery with Amazon S3 as the origin. The web application communicates with Amazon API Gateway Regional endpoints. The API Gateway APIs call AWS Lambda functions that store metadata in an Amazon Aurora Serverless database and put the documents into an S3 bucket. The company is growing steadily and has completed a proof of concept with its largest customer. The company must improve latency outside of EuropWhich combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket. Ensure that the web application uses the Transfer Acceleration signed URLs.
answers.explanation: Since your application stores documents in an S3 bucket, users located far from the eu-central-1 Region may experience significant latency during uploads. S3 Transfer Acceleration leverages Amazon CloudFront’s globally distributed edge locations. When enabled, your users upload their documents to the closest AWS edge location, which then routes the data to your destination S3 bucket over the optimized, high-speed AWS private network backbone. This significantly reduces the time and reliability issues associated with long-distance transfers over the public internet.

answers.content: Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Attach the accelerator to the CloudFront distribution.
answers.explanation: (AWS Global Accelerator): While Global Accelerator improves performance by routing traffic over the AWS network, it is generally used for TCP/UDP traffic to endpoints like Network Load Balancers or EC2 instances, not for accelerating a CloudFront distribution which already provides global content delivery.

answers.content: Change the API Gateway Regional endpoints to edge-optimized endpoints.
answers.explanation: Your web application communicates with API Gateway to handle metadata and trigger backend processes. By changing your API Gateway endpoints from Regional to Edge-Optimized, you utilize CloudFront's global network to terminate TLS connections closer to your users. This reduces the latency of the initial connection handshake and routes traffic over the AWS global network to your backend, providing a more responsive experience for geographically diverse users compared to routing traffic over the public internet directly to a single regional endpoint.

answers.content: Provision the entire stack in two other locations that are spread across the world. Use global databases on the Aurora Serverless cluster.
answers.explanation: (Provisioning the entire stack in other locations): While multi-region deployments can reduce latency, they introduce significant complexity in managing application state, data replication (e.g., Aurora Global Database management), and CI/CD pipelines. Options A and C provide immediate latency improvements with minimal architectural overhead.

answers.content: Add an Amazon RDS proxy between the Lambda functions and the Aurora Serverless database.
answers.explanation: (RDS Proxy): RDS Proxy is designed to improve database connection management, reduce memory usage, and handle spikes in database connections. It does not address network latency between the global user and the serverless backend.

questions.content: A company runs an IoT platform on AWS. IoT sensors in various locations send data to the company's Node.js API servers on Amazon EC2 instances running behind an Application Load Balancer. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance that uses a 4 TB General Purpose SSD volumThe number of sensors the company has deployed in the field has increased over time, and is expected to grow significantly. The API servers are consistently overloaded and RDS metrics show high write latency. Which of the following steps together will resolve the issues permanently and enable growth as new sensors are provisioned, while keeping this platform cost-efficient? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Resize the MySQL General Purpose SSD storage to 6 TB to improve the volume's IOPS.
answers.explanation: Simply increasing the size of an RDS volume can provide more IOPS, but it does not address the fundamental architectural bottleneck of a single-writer relational database under massive IoT load, and it remains a costly, non-scalable approach long-term.

answers.content: Re-architect the database tier to use Amazon Aurora instead of an RDS MySQL DB instance and add read replicas.
answers.explanation: While Amazon Aurora is an excellent, high-performance relational database, it is still a relational model. Adding read replicas improves read performance but does not inherently solve high write latency for massive IoT streaming, and it still requires managing relational data constraints.

answers.content: Leverage Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and AWS Lambda to ingest and process the raw data.
answers.explanation: Currently, your API servers are struggling because they are handling both the ingestion of data and the synchronous writes to your database. By introducing Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, you decouple the ingestion layer from your API servers. Sensors send data to the stream, which acts as a buffer, allowing you to ingest large volumes of data without overloading your compute resources. AWS Lambda can then consume this stream and process/write the data asynchronously, which drastically reduces the load on your API servers and improves overall system responsiveness.

answers.content: Use AWS X-Ray to analyze and debug application issues and add more API servers to match the load.
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray is a great tool for observability, but adding more API servers is a band-aid solution that increases cost without addressing the underlying database write saturation.

answers.content: Re-architect the database tier to use Amazon DynamoDB instead of an RDS MySQL DB instance.
answers.explanation: IoT sensor data is often high-velocity, semi-structured, and write-heavy. Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database purpose-built for such workloads. Unlike an RDS MySQL instance, which faces limitations in write throughput and horizontal scaling (especially as the volume reaches 4 TB and beyond), DynamoDB provides consistent, single-digit millisecond latency at any scale. It handles horizontal scaling automatically, allowing you to accommodate growth in sensor data without managing manual sharding or complex database scaling operations.

questions.content: A company recently acquired several other companies. Each company has a separate AWS account with a different billing and reporting method. The acquiring company has consolidated all the accounts into one organization in AWS Organizations. However, the acquiring company has found it difficult to generate a cost report that contains meaningful groups for all the teams. The acquiring company's finance team needs a solution to report on costs for all the companies through a self-managed application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report for the organization. Define tags and cost categories in the report. Create a table in Amazon Athena. Create an Amazon QuickSight dataset based on the Athena tablShare the dataset with the finance team.
answers.explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports support defining tags and cost categories to group costs effectively across multiple accounts within an AWS Organization. Creating a table in Amazon Athena allows querying detailed cost and usage data programmatically. Using Amazon QuickSight for the dataset enables the finance team to have self-service access to customizable reports. This approach leverages managed AWS services (Cost and Usage Report, Athena, QuickSight) to provide comprehensive, secure, and meaningful cost grouping across organizations.

answers.content: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report for the organization. Define tags and cost categories in the report. Create a specialized template in AWS Cost Explorer that the finance department will use to build reports.
answers.explanation: Cost Explorer templates are less flexible for self-managed applications and lack the detailed query capabilities Athena provides.

answers.content: Create an Amazon QuickSight dataset that receives spending information from the AWS Price List Query API. Share the dataset with the finance team.
answers.explanation: Using the AWS Price List Query API for spending information is inaccurate because it provides pricing data, not actual usage or cost data.

answers.content: Use the AWS Price List Query API to collect account spending information. Create a specialized template in AWS Cost Explorer that the finance department will use to build reports.
answers.explanation: Using the AWS Price List Query API and Cost Explorer templates does not deliver comprehensive billing data needed for detailed cost reporting across accounts.

questions.content: A company wants to migrate to AWS. The company wants to use a multi-account structure with centrally managed access to all accounts and applications. The company also wants to keep the traffic on a private network. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required at login, and specific roles are assigned to user groups. The company must create separate accounts for development. staging, production, and shared network. The production account and the shared network account must have connectivity to all accounts. The development account and the staging account must have access only to each other. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take 10 meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Deploy a landing zone environment by using AWS Control Tower. Enroll accounts and invite existing accounts into the resulting organization in AWS Organizations.
answers.explanation: Deploy a landing zone environment by using AWS Control Tower. This is the standard best practice for setting up a multi-account environment. It automatically configures AWS Organizations, sets up governance guardrails, and provides a baseline for security and compliance across all accounts.

answers.content: Enable AWS Security Hub in all accounts to manage cross-account access. Collect findings through AWS CloudTrail to force MFA login.
answers.explanation: Security Hub and CloudTrail are for security findings and auditing, not centralized identity management or MFA enforcement.

answers.content: Create transit gateways and transit gateway VPC attachments in each account. Configure appropriate route tables.
answers.explanation: Create transit gateways and transit gateway VPC attachments in each account. This enables private network connectivity across accounts. By configuring custom route tables within the Transit Gateway, you can implement the required network segmentation (e.g., allowing production and shared network connectivity while isolating development and staging environments).

answers.content: Set up and enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Create appropriate permission sets with required MFA for existing accounts.
answers.explanation: Set up and enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). This provides the required centrally managed access to all accounts and applications. It allows the company to integrate with an identity source, assign specific roles (permission sets) to user groups, and enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) at login.

answers.content: Enable AWS Control Tower in all accounts to manage routing between accounts. Collect findings through AWS CloudTrail to force MFA login.
answers.explanation: Control Tower does not manage routing between accounts; networking is handled via VPCs and Transit Gateway.

answers.content: Enable AWS Control Tower in all accounts to manage routing between accounts. Collect findings through AWS CloudTrail to force MFA login.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users in each account contradicts the requirement for centralized access. Cognito is for application user authentication, not AWS account access management.

questions.content: A company is running an application in the AWS Cloud. The company's security team must approve the creation of all new IAM users. When a new IAM user is created, all access for the user must be removed automatically. The security team must then receive a notification to approve the user. The company has a multi-Region AWS CloudTrail trail in the AWS account. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rulDefine a pattern with the detail-type value set to AWS API Call via CloudTrail and an eventName of CreateUser.
answers.explanation: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule. This rule monitors the CreateUser event, which is generated in CloudTrail whenever a new IAM user is created. By setting the detail-type to AWS API Call via CloudTrail and specifying eventName as CreateUser, you trigger the workflow immediately upon the event.

answers.content: Configure CloudTrail to send a notification for the CreateUser event to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
answers.explanation: While CloudTrail can log events, configuring it directly to send notifications for specific IAM events is less flexible and scalable than using an EventBridge rule to trigger a sophisticated remediation workflow.

answers.content: Invoke a container that runs in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate technology to remove access.
answers.explanation: Running a container on Fargate is overkill for simple IAM remediation tasks and introduces higher operational overhead compared to a lightweight serverless state machine or Lambda function.

answers.content: Invoke an AWS Step Functions state machine to remove access.
answers.explanation: Invoke an AWS Step Functions state machine to remove access. Step Functions provides a robust way to orchestrate the remediation process. Once triggered by EventBridge, the state machine can execute tasks—such as invoking an AWS Lambda function—to attach a policy that denies all access to the newly created user, effectively revoking their permissions.

answers.content: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the security team.
answers.explanation: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) to notify the security team. As part of the Step Functions workflow, an SNS notification can be sent to the security team containing the user details, providing them with the necessary information to review and approve or delete the user.

answers.content: Use Amazon Pinpoint to notify the security team.
answers.explanation: Amazon Pinpoint is primarily designed for large-scale customer engagement and marketing communications, whereas Amazon SNS is the standard, purpose-built service for internal operational alerts and notifications.

questions.content: A retail company has an on-premises data center in EuropThe company also has a multi-Region AWS presence that includes the eu-west-1 and us-east-1 Regions. The company wants to be able to route network traffic from its on-premises infrastructure into VPCs in either of those Regions. The company also needs to support traffic that is routed directly between VPCs in those Regions. No single points of failure can exist on the network. The company already has created two 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections from its on-premises data center. Each connection goes into a separate Direct Connect location in Europe for high availability. These two locations are named DX-A and DX-B, respectively. Each Region has a single AWS Transit Gateway that is configured to route all inter-VPC traffic within that Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a private VIF from the DX-A connection into a Direct Connect gateway. Create a private VIF from the DX-B connection into the same Direct Connect gateway for high availability. Associate both the eu-west-1 and us-east-1 transit gateways with the Direct Connect gateway. Peer the transit gateways with each other to support cross-Region routing.
answers.explanation: Private VIF cannot attach to a Transit Gateway (only to a Virtual Private Gateway).

answers.content: Create a transit VIF from the DX-A connection into a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the eu-west-1 transit gateway with this Direct Connect gateway. Create a transit VIF from the DX-8 connection into a separate Direct Connect gateway. Associate the us-east-1 transit gateway with this separate Direct Connect gateway. Peer the Direct Connect gateways with each other to support high availability and cross-Region routing.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect gateways cannot be peered with each other.

answers.content: Create a transit VIF from the DX-A connection into a Direct Connect gateway. Create a transit VIF from the DX-B connection into the same Direct Connect gateway for high availability. Associate both the eu-west-1 and us-east-1 transit gateways with this Direct Connect gateway. Configure the Direct Connect gateway to route traffic between the transit gateways.
answers.explanation: Direct Connect gateway does not route traffic between Transit Gateways; TGW peering is required.

answers.content: Create a transit VIF from the DX-A connection into a Direct Connect gateway. Create a transit VIF from the DX-B connection into the same Direct Connect gateway for high availability. Associate both the eu-west-1 and us-east-1 transit gateways with this Direct Connect gateway. Peer the transit gateways with each other to support cross-Region routing.
answers.explanation: correct because connecting Direct Connect to a Transit Gateway requires transit VIFs (not private VIFs), using two DX connections (DX-A and DX-B) with two transit VIFs attached to the same Direct Connect gateway provides high availability with no single point of failure, a Direct Connect gateway can associate with multiple Transit Gateways across Regions for multi-Region on-premises connectivity, and since a Direct Connect gateway does not route traffic between Transit Gateways, Transit Gateway peering is required to enable direct cross-Region VPC-to-VPC communication.

questions.content: A team collects and routes behavioral data for an entire company. The company runs a Multi-AZ VPC environment with public subnets, private subnets, and in internet gateway. Each public subnet also contains a NAT gateway. Most of the company's applications read from and write to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Most of the workloads run in private subnets. A solutions architect must review the infrastructurThe solution architect needs to reduce costs and maintain the function of the applications. The solutions architect uses Cost Explorer and notices that the cost in the EC2-Other category is consistently high. A further review shows that NatGateway-Bytes charges are increasing the cost in the EC2-Other category. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Enable VPC Flow Logs. Use Amazon Athena to analyze the logs for traffic that can be removed. Ensure that security groups are blocking traffic that is responsible for high costs.
answers.explanation: Analyzing VPC Flow Logs helps identify traffic but does not reduce NAT Gateway costs directly or prevent traffic routing through NAT Gateways.

answers.content: Add an interface VPC endpoint for Kinesis Data Streams to the VPC. Ensure that applications have the correct IAM permissions to use the interface VPC endpoint.
answers.explanation: This is incomplete. While it correctly identifies the need for an interface VPC endpoint, it lacks the necessary step of configuring the VPC endpoint policy, which is crucial for managing access and ensuring the security of the communication path.

answers.content: Enable VPC Flow Logs and Amazon DetectivReview Detective findings for traffic that is not related to Kinesis Data Streams. Configure security groups to block that traffic.
answers.explanation: Amazon Detective is primarily for security investigations and may add complexity/cost without directly addressing NAT Gateway data charges or reducing traffic through NAT Gateways.

answers.content: Add an interface VPC endpoint for Kinesis Data Streams to the VPC. Ensure that the VPC endpoint policy allows traffic from the applications.
answers.explanation: correct because the high EC2-Other cost is driven by NAT Gateway data processing charges, which occur when private subnet workloads access Kinesis Data Streams through the NAT gateway to reach the public service endpoint; creating an interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for Kinesis Data Streams allows traffic to stay within the AWS private network and bypass the NAT gateway, reducing NatGateway-Bytes charges, and configuring the VPC endpoint policy ensures only the intended application traffic is allowed through the endpoint.

questions.content: A company has an on-premises monitoring solution using a PostgreSQL database for persistence of events. The database is unable to scale due to heavy ingestion and it frequently runs out of storagThe company wants to create a hybrid solution and has already set up a VPN connection between its network and AWS. The solution should include the following attributes: • Managed AWS services to minimize operational complexity. • A buffer that automatically scales to match the throughput of data and requires no ongoing administration. • A visualization tool to create dashboards to observe events in near-real tim• Support for semi-structured JSON data and dynamic schemas. Which combination of components will enable the company to create a monitoring solution that will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to buffer events. Create an AWS Lambda function to process and transform events.
answers.explanation: correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed service that automatically scales to handle ingestion throughput with no ongoing administration, acting as the required buffer; it integrates with AWS Lambda for optional transformation of incoming JSON data before delivery.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to buffer events. Create an AWS Lambda function to process and transform events.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Kinesis Data Streams requires shard management and scaling administration, which increases operational complexity.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster to receive events. Use Amazon QuickSight to read from the database and create near-real-time visualizations and dashboards.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Aurora PostgreSQL does not scale well for heavy event ingestion workloads with dynamic schemas and is not optimized for near-real-time log analytics.

answers.content: Configure Amazon Elasticsearch Service (Amazon ES) to receive events. Use the Kibana endpoint deployed with Amazon ES to create near-real-time visualizations and dashboards.
answers.explanation: correct because Amazon Elasticsearch Service (now Amazon OpenSearch Service) supports semi-structured JSON data and dynamic schemas, and includes Kibana for near-real-time visualization and dashboards, making it well suited for monitoring and event analytics.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon Neptune DB instance to receive events. Use Amazon QuickSight to read from the database and create near-real-time visualizations and dashboards.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Amazon Neptune is a graph database and is not designed for log ingestion, event analytics, or dashboard-style monitoring.

questions.content: A company is developing and hosting several projects in the AWS Cloud. The projects are developed across multiple AWS accounts under the same organization in AWS Organizations. The company requires the cost for cloud infrastructure to be allocated to the owning project. The team responsible for all of the AWS accounts has discovered that several Amazon EC2 instances are lacking the Project tag used for cost allocation. Which actions should a solutions architect lake to resolve the problem and prevent it from happening in the future? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create an AWS Config rule in each account to find resources with missing tags.
answers.explanation: correct because an AWS Config rule in each account can detect EC2 instances that are missing the required Project tag, helping identify noncompliant existing resources.

answers.content: Create an SCP in the organization with a deny action for ec2:RunInstances if the Project tag is missing.
answers.explanation: correct because an SCP with a deny condition on ec2:RunInstances when the Project tag is missing prevents new EC2 instances from being launched without the required tag across all accounts in the organization.

answers.content: Use Amazon Inspector in the organization to find resources with missing tags.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Amazon Inspector assesses security vulnerabilities, not tagging compliance.

answers.content: Create an IAM policy in each account with a deny action for ec2:RunInstances if the Project tag is missing.
answers.explanation: incorrect because IAM policies apply only within individual accounts and can be bypassed by privileged users; SCPs enforce organization-wide guardrails.

answers.content: Create an AWS Config aggregator for the organization to collect a list of EC2 instances with the missing Project tag.
answers.explanation: correct because an AWS Config aggregator provides centralized visibility across all accounts in the organization, allowing the team to collect and review EC2 instances that are missing the Project tag.

answers.content: Use AWS Security Hub to aggregate a list of EC2 instances with the missing Project tag.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Security Hub aggregates security findings, not tagging compliance data.

questions.content: A large mobile gaming company has successfully migrated all of its on-premises infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect is reviewing the environment to ensure that it was built according to the design and that it is running in alignment with the Well-Architected Framework. While reviewing previous monthly costs in Cost Explorer, the solutions architect notices that the creation and subsequent termination of several large instance types account for a high proportion of the costs. The solutions architect finds out that the company's developers are launching new Amazon EC2 instances as part of their testing and that the developers are not using the appropriate instance types. The solutions architect must implement a control mechanism to limit the instance types that only the developers can launch. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create a desired-instance-type managed rule in AWS Config. Configure the rule with the instance types that are allowed. Attach the rule to an event to run each time a new EC2 instance is launched.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules are reactive and evaluate compliance after the instance is launched, not preventive, so they do not stop unauthorized launches.

answers.content: In the EC2 console, create a launch template that specifies the instance types that are allowed. Assign the launch template to the developers' IAM accounts.
answers.explanation: Launch templates cannot be assigned directly to IAM users or groups to enforce restrictions; users can still launch instances outside these templates.

answers.content: Create a new IAM policy. Specify the instance types that are allowed. Attach the policy to an IAM group that contains the IAM accounts for the developers
answers.explanation: IAM policies allow fine-grained control over the actions and resources that users can access, including specifying allowable EC2 instance types. Attaching a policy restricting instance types directly to the developers' IAM group ensures they can only launch approved instance types, enforcing security best practices. This method prevents unauthorized instance launches at the permission level, which is more secure than post-launch checks or relying on launch templates alone.

answers.content: Use EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline for the developers and assist them in the creation of a golden image.
answers.explanation: Creating golden AMIs with EC2 Image Builder does not prevent developers from specifying disallowed instance types when launching instances.

questions.content: A solutions architect is auditing the security setup or an AWS Lambda function for a company. The Lambda function retrieves, the latest changes from an Amazon Aurora databasThe Lambda function and the database run in the same VPC. Lambda environment variables are providing the database credentials to the Lambda function. The Lambda function aggregates data and makes the data available in an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). The data must not travel across the Internet. If any database credentials become compromised, the company needs a solution that minimizes the impact of the compromisWhat should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Enable IAM database authentication on the Aurora DB cluster. Change the IAM role for the Lambda function to allow the function to access the database by using IAM database authentication. Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
answers.explanation: IAM database authentication does not provide credential rotation and secrets management, and the option misses secret rotation best practice.

answers.content: Enable IAM database authentication on the Aurora DB cluster. Change the IAM role for the Lambda function to allow the function to access the database by using IAM database authentication. Enforce HTTPS on the connection to Amazon S3 during data transfers.
answers.explanation: Enforcing HTTPS alone on S3 does not address secure secret management or credential rotation.

answers.content: Save the database credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter StorSet up password rotation on the credentials in Parameter StorChange the IAM role for the Lambda function to allow the function to access Parameter StorModify the Lambda function to retrieve the credentials from Parameter StorDeploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
answers.explanation: Parameter Store is less preferred than Secrets Manager for managing and rotating database credentials securely.

answers.content: Save the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Set up password rotation on the credentials in Secrets Manager. Change the IAM role for the Lambda function to allow the function to access Secrets Manager. Modify the Lambda function to retrieve the credentials from Secrets Manager. Enforce HTTPS on the connection to Amazon S3 during data transfers.
answers.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is the preferred managed service for storing and rotating database credentials securely. Setting up password rotation in Secrets Manager minimizes the impact if credentials are compromised. Changing the Lambda IAM role to access Secrets Manager follows best practices for secure access to secrets. Enforcing HTTPS on the connection to Amazon S3 ensures data does not travel unencrypted over the internet while accessing the bucket. Using Secrets Manager is more secure than storing credentials in environment variables or Parameter Store without rotation.

questions.content: A company wants to deploy an AWS WAF solution to manage AWS WAF rules across multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are managed under different OUs in AWS Organizations. Administrators must be able to add or remove accounts or OUs from managed AWS WAF rule sets as needed. Administrators also must have the ability to automatically update and remediate noncompliant AWS WAF rules in all accounts. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answers.content: Use AWS Firewall Manager to manage AWS WAF rules across accounts in the organization. Use an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter to store account numbers and OUs to managUpdate the parameter as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to identify any changes to the parameter and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update the security policy in the Firewall Manager administrative account.
answers.explanation: AWS Firewall Manager is a managed service designed to centrally manage AWS WAF rules across multiple accounts in an AWS Organization, which minimizes operational overhead. Using a central parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for storing and updating account numbers and OUs enables dynamic management without manual intervention in each account. An EventBridge rule to detect parameter changes and invoke Lambda for updates automates remediation and compliance enforcement. This approach aligns with AWS best practices for multi-account management and centralized security policy enforcement without requiring manual updates or custom role assumptions.

answers.content: Deploy an organization-wide AWS Config rule that requires all resources in the selected OUs to associate the AWS WAF rules. Deploy automated remediation actions by using AWS Lambda to fix noncompliant resources. Deploy AWS WAF rules by using an AWS CloudFormation stack set to target the same OUs where the AWS Config rule is applied.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Config and Lambda with CloudFormation StackSets involves more manual setup and less integrated management compared to Firewall Manager.

answers.content: Create AWS WAF rules in the management account of the organization. Use AWS Lambda environment variables to store account numbers and OUs to managUpdate environment variables as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Create cross-account IAM roles in member accounts. Assume the roles by using AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) in the Lambda function to create and update AWS WAF rules in the member accounts.
answers.explanation: Managing environment variables in Lambda and cross-account role assumptions increases operational overhead and complexity over managed Firewall Manager.

answers.content: Use AWS Control Tower to manage AWS WAF rules across accounts in the organization. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to store account numbers and OUs to managUpdate AWS KMS as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Create IAM users in member accounts. Allow AWS Control Tower in the management account to use the access key and secret access key to create and update AWS WAF rules in the member accounts.
answers.explanation: Control Tower and KMS are not designed for storing account/OUs information or for managing WAF rules; creating IAM users with shared keys reduces security compared to managed role-based services.

questions.content: A large company is running a popular web application. The application runs on several Amazon EC2 Linux instances in an Auto Scaling group in a private subnet. An Application Load Balancer is targeting the instances in the Auto Scaling group in the private subnet. AWS Systems Manager Session Manager is configured, and AWS Systems Manager Agent is running on all the EC2 instances. The company recently released a new version of the application. Some EC2 instances are now being marked as unhealthy and are being terminated. As a result, the application is running at reduced capacity. A solutions architect tries to determine the root cause by analyzing Amazon CloudWatch logs that are collected from the application, but the logs are inconclusivHow should the solutions architect gain access to an EC2 instance to troubleshoot the issue?

answers.content: Suspend the Auto Scaling group's HealthCheck scaling process. Use Session Manager to log in to an instance that is marked as unhealthy.
answers.explanation: Suspending only the HealthCheck process does not prevent instance termination; unhealthy instances may still be terminated.

answers.content: Enable EC2 instance termination protection. Use Session Manager to log in to an instance that is marked as unhealthy.
answers.explanation: Enabling termination protection requires manual intervention and does not prevent the Auto Scaling group from replacing unhealthy instances.

answers.content: Set the termination policy to OldestInstance on the Auto Scaling group. Use Session Manager to log in to an instance that is marked an unhealthy.
answers.explanation: Changing termination policy to OldestInstance does not prevent termination of unhealthy instances and does not help in accessing the instances.

answers.content: Suspend the Auto Scaling group's Terminate process. Use Session Manager to log in to an instance that is marked as unhealthy.
answers.explanation: Suspending the Auto Scaling group's Terminate process prevents instances from being terminated automatically, allowing troubleshooting on the unhealthy instancUsing AWS Systems Manager Session Manager is the preferred secure method to access EC2 instances without SSH access in private subnets. This approach follows security best practices by avoiding disabling health checks or termination protection, which can interfere with Auto Scaling functionality. Options that suspend HealthCheck or change termination policies do not prevent termination by the termination process and are less secure or effective.

questions.content: A retail company has structured its AWS accounts to be part of an organization in AWS Organizations. The company has set up consolidated billing and has mapped its departments to the following OUs: Finance, Sales, Human Resources (HR), Marketing, and Operations. Each OU has multiple AWS accounts, one for each environment within a department. These environments are development, test, pre-production, and production. The HR department is releasing a new system that will launch in 3 months. In preparation, the HR department has purchased several Reserved Instances (RIs) in its production AWS account. The HR department will install the new application on this account. The HR department wants to make sure that other departments cannot share the RI discounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: In the AWS Billing and Cost Management console for the HR department's production account turn off RI sharing.
answers.explanation: incorrect because RI sharing settings cannot be modified independently from within a member account when consolidated billing is enabled.

answers.content: Remove the HR department's production AWS account from the organization. Add the account 10 the consolidating billing configuration only.
answers.explanation: incorrect because removing the account from the organization would break centralized governance and is unnecessary; RI sharing can be controlled without removing the account.

answers.content: In the AWS Billing and Cost Management consoluse the organization's management account 10 turn off RI Sharing for the HR departments production AWS account.
answers.explanation: correct because Reserved Instance (RI) sharing is controlled at the organization level from the management account in AWS Organizations. By disabling RI sharing for the HR production account in the Billing and Cost Management console (from the management account), the RI discounts will apply only to that specific account and will not be shared across other accounts in the organization.

answers.content: Create an SCP in the organization to restrict access to the RIs. Apply the SCP to the OUs of the other departments.
answers.explanation: incorrect because SCPs control permissions for API actions and cannot restrict or control the sharing of RI billing discounts.

questions.content: A company has an asynchronous HTTP application that is hosted as an AWS Lambda function. A public Amazon API Gateway endpoint invokes the Lambda function. The Lambda function and the API Gateway endpoint reside in the us-east-1 Region. A solutions architect needs to redesign the application to support failover to another AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an API Gateway endpoint in the us-west-2 Region to direct traffic to the Lambda function in us-east-1. Configure Amazon Route 53 to use a failover routing policy to route traffic for the two API Gateway endpoints.
answers.explanation: Creates an endpoint in a second region but routes traffic only to Lambda in the first region, so no true failover if the first region is down.
