answers.content: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuConfigure API Gateway to direct traffic to the SQS queue instead of to the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to pull messages from the queue for processing.
answers.explanation: Introduces SQS but does not address multi-region deployment or failover of Lambda and API Gateway endpoints.

answers.content: Deploy the Lambda function to the us-west-2 Region. Create an API Gateway endpoint in us-west-2 10 direct traffic to the Lambda function in us-west-2. Configure AWS Global Accelerator and an Application Load Balancer to manage traffic across the two API Gateway endpoints.
answers.explanation: Using Global Accelerator and an ALB for API Gateway is not a standard or recommended architecture and adds unnecessary complexity.

answers.content: Deploy the Lambda function and an API Gateway endpoint to the us-west-2 Region. Configure Amazon Route 53 to use a failover routing policy to route traffic for the two API Gateway endpoints.
answers.explanation: Deploying the Lambda function and API Gateway endpoint in the secondary region provides full failover capability by having active resources in both regions. Configuring Amazon Route 53 with a failover routing policy allows automatic routing to the backup region if the primary region becomes unavailablThis approach aligns with using AWS managed services for fault tolerance and disaster recovery across regions, leveraging the multi-region AWS infrastructurOption D directly supports failover with separate endpoints in both regions, which is a best practice for multi-Region high availability.

questions.content: A company runs a Java application that has complex dependencies on VMs that are in the company's data center. The application is stablbut the company wants to modernize the technology stack. The company wants to migrate the application to AWS and minimize the administrative overhead to maintain the servers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST code changes?

answers.content: Migrate the application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate by using AWS App2Container. Store container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Grant the ECS task execution role permission 10 access the ECR image repository. Configure Amazon ECS to use an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Use the ALB to interact with the application.
answers.explanation: AWS App2Container (A2C) can transform existing Java applications running on VMs into containers without code changes. A2C supports seamless deployment to Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate, minimizing server maintenance overhead. Using Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate avoids managing servers, meeting the requirement to minimize administrative overhead. Storing container images in Amazon ECR follows AWS best practices for managed container registries. Granting the ECS task execution role permission to access ECR images aligns with secure access practices. Using an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to interact with the application is a common, secure, and managed solution.

answers.content: Migrate the application code to a container that runs in AWS Lambda. Build an Amazon API Gateway REST API with Lambda integration. Use API Gateway to interact with the application.
answers.explanation: Migrating the application code to Lambda requires code changes due to the different runtime and event model.

answers.content: Migrate the application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) on EKS managed node groups by using AWS App2Container. Store container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Give the EKS nodes permission to access the ECR image repository. Use Amazon API Gateway to interact with the application.
answers.explanation: Amazon EKS requires managing Kubernetes nodes, increasing administrative overhead compared to Fargate.

answers.content: Migrate the application code to a container that runs in AWS Lambda. Configure Lambda to use an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Use the ALB to interact with the application.
answers.explanation: Running containers in Lambda with an ALB is not a standard architecture and would likely require code changes.

questions.content: A finance company is running its business-critical application on current-generation Linux EC2 instances. The application includes a self-managed MySQL database performing heavy I/O operations. The application is working fine to handle a moderate amount of traffic during the month. However, it slows down during the final three days of each month due to month-end reporting, even though the company is using Elastic Load Balancers and Auto Scaling within its infrastructure to meet the increased demand. Which of the following actions would allow the database to handle the month-end load with the LEAST impact on performance?

answers.content: Pre-warming Elastic Load Balancers, using a bigger instance type, changing all Amazon EBS volumes to GP2 volumes.
answers.explanation: Pre-warming ELB and changing EBS to GP2 does not directly address database performance under heavy I/O load and GP2 volumes may not offer sufficient performance compared to PIOPS.

answers.content: Performing a one-time migration of the database cluster to Amazon RDS, and creating several additional read replicas to handle the load during end of month.
answers.explanation: (RDS Migration): While migrating to Amazon RDS is a best practice for managed services, it is a significant architectural migration that involves code changes, data migration, and a complete change to your database management strategy. It is not the LEAST impact solution compared to dynamically tuning the existing storage.

answers.content: Using Amazon CloudWatch with AWS Lambda to change the type, size, or IOPS of Amazon EBS volumes in the cluster based on a specific CloudWatch metric.
answers.explanation: correct because the bottleneck is heavy I/O during month-end processing, and modifying the EBS volume type, size, or provisioned IOPS (for example, switching to higher IOPS or io1/io2 volumes) dynamically using CloudWatch-triggered Lambda automation directly addresses the I/O constraint with minimal architectural change and minimal performance impact. EBS Elastic Volumes allows modification without detaching volumes, reducing downtime.

answers.content: Replacing all existing Amazon EBS volumes with new PIOPS volumes that have the maximum available storage size and I/O per second by taking snapshots before the end of the month and reverting back afterwards.
answers.explanation: Temporarily replacing EBS volumes with high-performance PIOPS adds operational complexity and risk, and manual snapshot reverting is not a best practice compared to managed scaling.

questions.content: A company developed a pilot application by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk and Java. To save costs during development, the company's development team deployed the application into a single-instance environment. Recent tests indicate that the application consumes more CPU than expected. CPU utilization is regularly greater than 85%, which causes some performance bottlenecks. A solutions architect must mitigate the performance issues before the company launches the application to production. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create a new Elastic Beanstalk application. Select a load-balanced environment typSelect all Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the maximum CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.
answers.explanation: Creates a new application unnecessarily instead of modifying the existing environment, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create a second Elastic Beanstalk environment. Apply the traffic-splitting deployment policy. Specify a percentage of incoming traffic to direct to the new environment in the average CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.
answers.explanation: Creating a second environment and splitting traffic is more complex and requires managing multiple environments, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Modify the existing environment's capacity configuration to use a load-balanced environment typSelect all Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the average CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.
answers.explanation: Modifying the existing environment to use a load-balanced environment type aligns with AWS best practices to mitigate high CPU utilization with minimal operational overhead. Adding a scale-out rule based on CPU utilization allows automatic scaling and improves performance without needing to manage multiple environments. Using all Availability Zones increases availability and fault tolerancThis approach uses managed Elastic Beanstalk features rather than creating multiple environments or manual rebuilds.

answers.content: Select the Rebuild environment action with the load balancing option. Select an Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the sum CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.
answers.explanation: Rebuilding the environment manually is less efficient and does not guarantee optimal scaling or multi-AZ usage; also, 'sum CPU utilization' is not a typical metric for scaling.

questions.content: A publishing company's design team updates the icons and other static assets that an ecommerce web application uses. The company serves the icons and assets from an Amazon S3 bucket that is hosted in the company's production account. The company also uses a development account that members of the design team can access. After the design team tests the static assets in the development account, the design team needs to load the assets into the S3 bucket in the production account. A solutions architect must provide the design team with access to the production account without exposing other parts of the web application to the risk of unwanted changes. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: In the production account, create a new IAM policy that allows read and write access to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: correct because the production account must have an IAM policy that grants the required read/write permissions to the specific S3 bucket containing the static assets.

answers.content: In the development account, create a new IAM policy that allows read and write access to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: incorrect because permissions to the production S3 bucket must be granted in the production account, not the development account.

answers.content: In the production account, create a role Attach the new policy to the rolDefine the development account as a trusted entity.
answers.explanation: correct because a role must be created in the production account with the S3 access policy attached, and the development account must be defined as the trusted entity so users there can assume the role.

answers.content: In the development account, create a rolAttach the new policy to the role Define the production account as a trusted entity.
answers.explanation: incorrect because the role that grants access to production resources must reside in the production account.

answers.content: In the development account, create a group that contains all the IAM users of the design team Attach a different IAM policy to the group to allow the sts:AssumeRole action on the role In the production account.
answers.explanation: correct because in the development account, the design team users should be placed in a group with a policy that allows sts:AssumeRole on the production account role, enabling controlled cross-account access without exposing other resources.

answers.content: In the development account, create a group that contains all the IAM users of the design team Attach a different IAM policy to the group to allow the sts:AssumeRole action on the role in the development account.
answers.explanation: incorrect because assuming a role within the development account does not grant access to production resources.

questions.content: A company is planning to migrate its business-critical applications from an on-premises data center to AWS. The company has an on-premises installation of a Microsoft SQL Server Always On cluster. The company wants to migrate to an AWS managed database servicA solutions architect must design a heterogeneous database migration on AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Migrate the SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for MySQL by using backup and restore utilities.
answers.explanation: Backup and restore utilities do not support heterogeneous migration from SQL Server to MySQL, making it invalid.

answers.content: Use an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device to transfer data to Amazon S3. Set up Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use S3 integration with SQL Server features, such as BULK INSERT.
answers.explanation: Using Snowball Edge and S3 integration relies on manual data import and does not leverage AWS managed migration tools; also it does not perform schema conversion.

answers.content: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool to translate the database schema to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data from on-premises databases to Amazon RDS.
answers.explanation: AWS Schema Conversion Tool is designed to translate database schemas for heterogeneous database migration, enabling migration from SQL Server to MySQL. AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) supports migrating data and ongoing replication from on-premises SQL Server to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Using AWS DMS and Schema Conversion Tool aligns with AWS best practices for managed, secure, and supported heterogeneous database migration. Options involving Snowball Edge or DataSync to move data to S3 and then using SQL Server features for import do not directly address heterogeneous migration and do not leverage managed migration services.

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync to migrate data over the network between on-premises storage and Amazon S3. Set up Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use S3 integration with SQL Server features, such as BULK INSERT.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync copies files to S3 but does not perform database schema conversion or migration; S3 integration with SQL Server features is not a complete heterogeneous migration solution.

questions.content: A company is running applications on AWS in a multi-account environment. The company's sales team and marketing team use separate AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The sales team stores petabytes of data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The marketing team uses Amazon QuickSight for data visualizations. The marketing team needs access to data that the sates team stores in the S3 bucket. The company has encrypted the S3 bucket with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. The marketing team has already created the IAM service role for QuickSight to provide QuickSight access in the marketing AWS account. The company needs a solution that will provide secure access to the data in the S3 bucket across AWS accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create a new S3 bucket in the marketing account. Create an S3 replication rule in the sales account to copy the objects to the new S3 bucket in the marketing account. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the new S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Replicating petabytes of data adds significant operational overhead and cost, violating the requirement for least operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an SCP to grant access to the S3 bucket to the marketing account. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the KMS key from the sates account with the marketing account. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) do not grant direct resource permissions and AWS RAM cannot share KMS keys; thus, this approach is invalid.

answers.content: Update the S3 bucket policy in the marketing account to grant access to the QuickSight rolCreate a KMS grant for the encryption key that is used in the S3 bucket. Grant decrypt access to the QuickSight rolUpdate the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Updating the bucket policy in the marketing account is incorrect because the bucket is in the sales account; also, KMS grants must be given from the key owner's account, which is the sales account.

answers.content: Create an IAM role in the sales account and grant access to the S3 bucket. From the marketing account, assume the IAM role in the sales account to access the S3 bucket. Update the QuickSight rote, to create a trust relationship with the new IAM role in the sales account.
answers.explanation: Creating an IAM role in the sales account with proper S3 bucket access and allowing the marketing account to assume this role follows AWS best practices for cross-account access. This approach leverages IAM roles and trust relationships to securely grant least-privilege access without duplicating data or managing complex replication setups. Granting decrypt access via KMS to an IAM role in the sales account is simpler and more secure than sharing keys broadly or replicating data. This method minimizes operational overhead by avoiding data replication and uses AWS-managed IAM capabilities for secure access.

questions.content: A company is running an application in the AWS Cloud. Recent application metrics show inconsistent response times and a significant increase in error rates. Calls to third-party services are causing the delays. Currently, the application calls third-party services synchronously by directly invoking an AWS Lambda function. A solutions architect needs to decouple the third-party service calls and ensure that all the calls are eventually completed. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to store events and invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon SQS decouples the application from the third-party service calls by queuing events asynchronously. SQS ensures all messages (calls) are eventually processed, meeting the requirement for eventual completion. Invoking Lambda functions asynchronously from SQS improves fault tolerance and handles retries automatically. This approach aligns with AWS best practices for decoupling and handling unreliable or slow third-party integrations.

answers.content: Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to pass events to the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Step Functions are primarily for orchestrating workflows, not for decoupling asynchronous calls with guaranteed at-least-once processing like SQS.

answers.content: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to pass events to the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: EventBridge is event routing, but it does not provide queuing and retry semantics necessary for guaranteed eventual call completion.

answers.content: Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to store events and Invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: SNS is a pub/sub service that pushes messages to subscribers, but does not store messages for retries or guarantee eventual processing in cases of consumer failure.

questions.content: A company has introduced a new policy that allows employees to work remotely from their homes if they connect by using a VPN. The company is hosting internal applications with VPCs in multiple AWS accounts. Currently, the applications are accessible from the company's on-premises office network through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The VPC in the company's main AWS account has peering connections established with VPCs in other AWS accounts. A solutions architect must design a scalable AWS Client VPN solution for employees to use while they work from homWhat is the MOST cost-effective solution that meets these requirements?

answers.content: Create a Client VPN endpoint in each AWS account. Configure required routing that allows access to internal applications.
answers.explanation: Creating separate Client VPN endpoints in each AWS account increases cost and operational overhead unnecessarily.

answers.content: Create a Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account. Configure required routing that allows access to internal applications.
answers.explanation: Creating a single Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account is more cost-effective than deploying multiple endpoints in each account, as AWS Client VPN pricing is per endpoint. The main AWS account already has VPC peering connections to other AWS accounts, so routing can be configured to allow access to internal applications across accounts without additional infrastructurClient VPN is a managed service that provides secure, scalable, elastic access without the need for provisioning and managing additional resources like transit gateways. This approach adheres to AWS best practices by using a managed service and leveraging existing VPC peering rather than more complex or costly alternatives.

answers.content: Create a Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account. Provision a transit gateway that is connected to each AWS account. Configure required routing that allows access to internal applications.
answers.explanation: Introducing a transit gateway adds complexity and cost that is not justified since peering connections are already in place.

answers.content: Create a Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account. Establish connectivity between the Client VPN endpoint and the AWS Site-to-Site VPN.
answers.explanation: Connecting the Client VPN endpoint to the Site-to-Site VPN is not a supported or necessary architecture for providing scalable remote access to internal applications.

questions.content: A digital marketing company has multiple AWS accounts that belong to various teams. The creative team uses an Amazon S3 bucket in its AWS account to securely store images and media files that are used as content for the company's marketing campaigns. The creative team wants to share the S3 bucket with the strategy team so that the strategy team can view the objects. A solutions architect has created an IAM role that is named strategy_reviewer in the Strategy account. The solutions architect also has set up a custom AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in the Creative account and has associated the key with the S3 bucket. However, when users from the Strategy account assume the IAM role and try to access objects in the S3 bucket, they receive an Access Denied error. The solutions architect must ensure that users in the Strategy account can access the S3 bucket. The solution must provide these users with only the minimum permissions that they need. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a bucket policy that includes read permissions for the S3 bucket. Set the principal of the bucket policy to the account ID of the Strategy account.
answers.explanation: correct because the S3 bucket policy in the Creative account must explicitly allow cross-account read access (e.g., s3:GetObject) to the Strategy account (or specifically to the strategy_reviewer role).

answers.content: Update the strategy_reviewer IAM role to grant full permissions for the S3 bucket and to grant decrypt permissions for the custom KMS key.
answers.explanation: Incorrect: Granting full permissions is too permissive and violates least privilege.

answers.content: Update the custom KMS key policy in the Creative account to grant decrypt permissions to the strategy_reviewer IAM role.
answers.explanation: Correct: The KMS key policy must grant decrypt permissions to the Strategy account role for access.

answers.content: Create a bucket policy that includes read permissions for the S3 bucket. Set the principal of the bucket policy to an anonymous user.
answers.explanation: Incorrect: Setting principal to anonymous user exposes bucket to the public and is insecure.

answers.content: Update the custom KMS key policy in the Creative account to grant encrypt permissions to the strategy_reviewer IAM role.
answers.explanation: Incorrect: Encrypt permission is not required; decrypt permission is needed for access.

answers.content: Update the strategy_reviewer IAM role to grant read permissions for the S3 bucket and to grant decrypt permissions for the custom KMS key.
answers.explanation: correct because the strategy_reviewer IAM role must include identity-based permissions allowing s3:GetObject on the bucket and kms:Decrypt on the KMS key, ensuring least privilege access.

questions.content: A company has an on-premises website application that provides real estate information for potential renters and buyers. The website uses a Java backend and a NoSQL MongoDB database to store subscriber data. The company needs to migrate the entire application to AWS with a similar structurThe application must be deployed for high availability, and the company cannot make changes to the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use an Amazon Aurora DB cluster as the database for the subscriber data. Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones for the Java backend application.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora is not compatible with MongoDB, requiring application changes which are not allowed.

answers.content: Use MongoDB on Amazon EC2 instances as the database for the subscriber data. Deploy EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone for the Java backend application.
answers.explanation: Deploying EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone does not meet high availability requirements.

answers.content: Configure Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) with appropriately sized instances in multiple Availability Zones as the database for the subscriber data. Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones for the Java backend application.
answers.explanation: Amazon DocumentDB provides a managed MongoDB-compatible database service, preserving the application’s database structure without requiring changes. Deploying Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones ensures high availability for the Java backend without application changes. Option A suggests Amazon Aurora which is not compatible with MongoDB, thus requiring application changes. Option B uses a single Availability Zone, which does not meet high availability requirements. Option D mentions on-demand capacity mode for DocumentDB, which is not a documented configuration, making it invalid.

answers.content: Configure Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) in on-demand capacity mode in multiple Availability Zones as the database for the subscriber data. Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones for the Java backend application.
answers.explanation: On-demand capacity mode is not a valid configuration for Amazon DocumentDB, so this option is incorrect.

questions.content: A company is creating a sequel for a popular online game.A large number of users from all over the world will play the game within the first week after launch. Currently, the game consists of the following components deployed in a single AWS Region: • Amazon S3 bucket that stores game assets • Amazon DynamoDB table that stores player scores A solutions architect needs to design a multi-Region solution that will reduce latency, improve reliability, and require the least effort to implement. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve assets from the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication. Create a new DynamoDB table in a new Region. Use the new table as a replica target for DynamoDB global tables.
answers.explanation: incomplete because although it uses CloudFront and global tables, it does not configure multi-origin failover for S3 and relies only on CRR without improving asset availability at the application layer.

answers.content: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve assets from the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Same-Region Replication. Create a new DynamoDB table in a new Region. Configure asynchronous replication between the DynamoDB tables by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with change data capture (CDC).
answers.explanation: incorrect because Same-Region Replication does not provide multi-Region redundancy, and using AWS DMS for DynamoDB replication is unnecessarily complex compared to global tables.

answers.content: Create another S3 bucket in a new Region, and configure S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and configure origin failover with two origins accessing the S3 buckets in each Region. Configure DynamoDB global tables by enabling Amazon DynamoDB Streams, and add a replica table in a new Region.
answers.explanation: correct because it provides a true multi-Region architecture with minimal operational effort: S3 Cross-Region Replication ensures game assets are replicated to another Region, CloudFront with origin failover improves global latency and availability by serving from the nearest healthy origin, and DynamoDB global tables (enabled via DynamoDB Streams) provide fully managed, multi-Region active-active replication for player scores with low latency and high reliability.

answers.content: Create another S3 bucket in the sine Region, and configure S3 Same-Region Replication between the buckets. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and configure origin failover with two origins accessing the S3 buckets. Create a new DynamoDB table in a new Region. Use the new table as a replica target for DynamoDB global tables.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Same-Region Replication does not improve cross-Region latency or resilience, which is required for a global launch.

questions.content: A company runs a proprietary stateless ETL application on an Amazon EC2 Linux instances. The application is a Linux binary, and the source code cannot be modified. The application is single-threaded, uses 2 GB of RAM, and is highly CPU intensivThe application is scheduled to run every 4 hours and runs for up to 20 minutes. A solutions architect wants to revise the architecture for the solution. Which strategy should the solutions architect use?

answers.content: Use AWS Lambda to run the application. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to invoke the Lambda function every 4 hours.
answers.explanation: incorrect because Lambda has a maximum 15-minute execution limit and is not suitable for CPU-intensive long-running binaries.

answers.content: Use AWS Batch to run the application. Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to invoke the AWS Batch job every 4 hours.
answers.explanation: incorrect because AWS Batch is more appropriate for large-scale batch processing workloads and introduces unnecessary orchestration complexity for a single scheduled job.

answers.content: Use AWS Fargate to run the application. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to invoke the Fargate task every 4 hours.
answers.explanation: correct because the workload is stateless, runs on a schedule, is CPU intensive, requires 2 GB RAM, and runs for up to 20 minutes; AWS Fargate can run the Linux binary in a container without managing servers, supports the required compute resources, and EventBridge can trigger the task every 4 hours, resulting in a fully managed, low-operations solution.

answers.content: Use Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to run the application. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy and run the application every 4 hours.
answers.explanation: incorrect because managing EC2 Spot Instances and CodeDeploy increases operational overhead and does not align with minimizing infrastructure management.

questions.content: A company runs a serverless application in a single AWS Region. The application accesses external URLs and extracts metadata from those sites. The company uses an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to publish URLs to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuAn AWS Lambda function uses the queue as an event source and processes the URLs from the queuResults are saved to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to process each URL in other Regions to compare possible differences in site localization. URLs must be published from the existing Region. Results must be written to the existing S3 bucket in the current Region. Which combination of changes will produce multi-Region deployment that meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Deploy the SQS queue with the Lambda function to other Regions.
answers.explanation: correct because to process URLs in multiple Regions, the company must deploy an SQS queue and Lambda function in each additional Region so processing occurs locally in those Regions.

answers.content: Subscribe the SNS topic in each Region to the SQS queue.
answers.explanation: incorrect because SNS topics do not subscribe to SQS queues; SQS queues subscribe to SNS topics.

answers.content: Subscribe the SQS queue in each Region to the SNS topic.
answers.explanation: correct because the SNS topic in the original Region can have cross-Region subscriptions to SQS queues in other Regions; by subscribing each Regional SQS queue to the original SNS topic, URLs published in the existing Region will be delivered to all Regions for processing.

answers.content: Configure the SQS queue to publish URLs to SNS topics in each Region.
answers.explanation: Incorrect; SQS queues do not publish to SNS topics, SNS topics publish to SQS queues.

answers.content: Deploy the SNS topic and the Lambda function to other Regions.
answers.explanation: Incorrect; replicating the SNS topic is unnecessary since publishing must remain in the existing region.

questions.content: A company manages multiple AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations. Under the root OU, the company has two OUs: Research and DataOps. Because of regulatory requirements, all resources that the company deploys in the organization must reside in the ap-northeast-1 Region. Additionally, EC2 instances that the company deploys in the DataOps OU must use a predefined list of instance types. A solutions architect must implement a solution that applies these restrictions. The solution must maximize operational efficiency and must minimize ongoing maintenancWhich combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Create an IAM role in one account under the DataOps OU. Use the ec2:InstanceType condition key in an inline policy on the role to restrict access to specific instance type.
answers.explanation: IAM role inline policies do not centrally enforce restrictions across all accounts and require individual account management, which is less operationally efficient.

answers.content: Create an IAM user in all accounts under the root OU. Use the aws:RequestedRegion condition key in an inline policy on each user to restrict access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-1.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users with inline policies in all accounts is operationally inefficient and does not centrally enforce restrictions; also, it does not apply to all identities.

answers.content: Create an SCP. Use the aws:RequestedRegion condition key to restrict access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-1. Apply the SCP to the root OU.
answers.explanation: correct because an SCP applied at the root OU using the aws:RequestedRegion condition key can restrict all accounts in the organization to operate only in ap-northeast-1, centrally enforcing the Region requirement with minimal ongoing maintenance.

answers.content: Create an SCP. Use the ec2:Region condition key to restrict access to all AWS Regions except ap-northeast-1. Apply the SCP to the root OU, the DataOps OU, and the Research OU.
answers.explanation: The ec2:Region condition key is invalid for SCPs; the correct key to restrict regions is aws:RequestedRegion, so this approach will not work as intended.

answers.content: Create an SCP. Use the ec2:InstanceType condition key to restrict access to specific instance types. Apply the SCP to the DataOps OU.
answers.explanation: correct because an SCP applied specifically to the DataOps OU using the ec2:InstanceType condition key can restrict EC2 launches to a predefined list of instance types, ensuring the policy applies only to DataOps accounts.

questions.content: A company uses AWS Organizations for a multi-account setup in the AWS Cloud. The company uses AWS Control Tower for governance and uses AWS Transit Gateway for VPC connectivity across accounts. In an AWS application account, the company's application team has deployed a web application that uses AWS Lambda and Amazon RDS. The company's database administrators have a separate DBA account and use the account to centrally manage all the databases across the organization. The database administrators use an Amazon EC2 instance that is deployed in the DBA account to access an RDS database that is deployed m the application account. The application team has stored the database credentials as secrets in AWS Secrets Manager in the application account. The application team is manually sharing the secrets with the database administrators. The secrets are encrypted by the default AWS managed key for Secrets Manager in the application account. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that gives the database administrators access to the database and eliminates the need to manually share the secrets. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the secrets from the application account with the DBA account. In the DBA account, create an IAM role that is named DBA-Admin. Grant the role the required permissions to access the shared secrets. Attach the DBA-Admin role to the EC2 instance for access to the cross-account secrets.
answers.explanation: AWS RAM does not support sharing secrets from Secrets Manager across accounts; this is not a supported method.

answers.content: In the application account, create an IAM role that is named DBA-Secret. Grant the role the required permissions to access the secrets. In the DBA account, create an IAM role that is named DBA-Admin. Grant the DBA-Admin role the required permissions to assume the DBA-Secret role in the application account. Attach the DBA-Admin role to the EC2 instance for access to the cross-account secrets
answers.explanation: The best practice for cross-account access to AWS Secrets Manager secrets is to use IAM roles with trust policies allowing role assumption across accounts. Option B provides a solution where an IAM role in the DBA account assumes a role in the application account that has permissions to access the secrets, enabling secure and managed access without manual secret sharing. This approach avoids storing credentials in less secure locations and uses managed AWS IAM capabilities to control access securely. Options involving AWS RAM or SCPs for secrets access are not the recommended mechanism for cross-account Secrets Manager secret sharing. Proper resource-based permissions and role assumption respect AWS security best practices and avoid manual sharing.

answers.content: In the DBA account create an IAM role that is named DBA-Admin. Grant the role the required permissions to access the secrets and the default AWS managed key in the application account. In the application account, attach resource-based policies to the key to allow access from the DBA account. Attach the DBA-Admin role to the EC2 instance for access to the cross-account secrets.
answers.explanation: Granting direct permissions on the AWS managed key and accessing secrets via a role in the DBA account is complex and error-prone, and Secrets Manager does not support sharing via encryption key policies alone.

answers.content: In the DBA account, create an IAM role that is named DBA-Admin. Grant the role the required permissions to access the secrets in the application account. Attach an SCP to the application account to allow access to the secrets from the DBA account. Attach the DBA-Admin role to the EC2 instance for access to the cross-account secrets.
answers.explanation: Service control policies (SCPs) cannot grant cross-account Secrets Manager access; SCPs restrict permissions but don't enable cross-account resource access.

questions.content: A solutions architect must analyze a company's Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to determine whether the company is using resources efficiently. The company is running several large, high-memory EC2 instances to host database clusters that are deployed in active/passive configurations. The utilization of these EC2 instances varies by the applications that use the databases, and the company has not identified a pattern. The solutions architect must analyze the environment and take action based on the findings. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Create a dashboard by using AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Configure visualizations for Amazon CloudWatch metrics that are associated with the EC2 instances and their EBS volumes. Review the dashboard periodically, and identify usage patterns. Rightsize the EC2 instances based on the peaks in the metrics.
answers.explanation: Systems Manager OpsCenter is not designed specifically for cost optimization or detailed usage pattern analysis of EC2 instances and EBS volumes.

answers.content: Turn on Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances and their EBS volumes. Create and review a dashboard that is based on the metrics. Identify usage patterns. Rightsize the EC2 instances based on the peaks in the metrics.
answers.explanation: Enabling detailed CloudWatch monitoring increases costs and requires manual analysis; it lacks automated rightsizing recommendations.

answers.content: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on each of the EC2 instances. Turn on AWS Compute Optimizer, and let it run for at least 12 hours. Review the recommendations from Compute Optimizer, and rightsize the EC2 instances as directed.
answers.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer is a managed service that provides recommendations based on actual utilization to optimize EC2 instances cost-effectively. Installing the CloudWatch agent provides detailed metrics to feed into Compute Optimizer for accurate analysis. Reviewing Compute Optimizer recommendations after it runs allows tailored rightsizing based on real usage patterns, balancing performance and cost. This approach aligns with AWS best practices to use managed services for optimization and avoids manual monitoring or less detailed metrics.

answers.content: Sign up for the AWS Enterprise Support plan. Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor. Wait 12 hours. Review the recommendations from Trusted Advisor, and rightsize the EC2 instances as directed.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor requires Enterprise Support plan and provides general recommendations, not detailed or continuous workload-based rightsizing suggestions like Compute Optimizer.

questions.content: An external audit of a company's serverless application reveals IAM policies that grant too many permissions. These policies are attached to the company's AWS Lambda execution roles. Hundreds of the company's Lambda functions have broad access permissions such as full access to Amazon S3 buckets and Amazon DynamoDB tables. The company wants each function to have only the minimum permissions that the function needs to complete its task. A solutions architect must determine which permissions each Lambda function needs. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of effort?

answers.content: Set up Amazon CodeGuru to profile the Lambda functions and search for AWS API calls. Create an inventory of the required API calls and resources for each Lambda function. Create new IAM access policies for each Lambda function. Review the new policies to ensure that they meet the company's business requirements.
answers.explanation: Amazon CodeGuru is intended for code profiling and automated code review but is not designed to analyze or generate IAM policies from AWS API usage.

answers.content: Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging for the AWS account. Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to generate IAM access policies based on the activity recorded in the CloudTrail log. Review the generated policies to ensure that they meet the company's business requirements.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to generate IAM policies from CloudTrail logs automates the permission analysis and policy creation process with minimal effort. This method leverages managed AWS services designed for permission analysis and fine-tuning, which aligns with best practices of least privilege and managed service preferencThe generated policies reflect actual usage data captured by CloudTrail, ensuring that permissions are scoped to only what is needed.

answers.content: Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging for the AWS account. Create a script to parse the CloudTrail log, search for AWS API calls by Lambda execution role, and create a summary report. Review the report. Create IAM access policies that provide more restrictive permissions for each Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Creating a custom script to parse CloudTrail logs is more manual and requires significant effort compared to using the managed Access Analyzer service.

answers.content: Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging for the AWS account. Export the CloudTrail logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon EMR to process the CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3 and produce a report of API calls and resources used by each execution rolCreate a new IAM access policy for each rolExport the generated roles to an S3 bucket. Review the generated policies to ensure that they meet the company's business requirements.
answers.explanation: Using EMR to process CloudTrail logs for permission analysis is overly complex and manual compared to the managed Access Analyzer, thus more effort intensive.

questions.content: A software company hosts an application on AWS with resources in multiple AWS accounts and Regions. The application runs on a group of Amazon EC2 instances in an application VPC located in the us-east-1 Region with an IPv4 CIDR block of 10.10.0.0/16. In a different AWS account, a shared services VPC is located in the us-east-2 Region with an IPv4 CIDR block of 10.10.10.0/24. When a cloud engineer uses AWS CloudFormation to attempt to peer the application VPC with the shared services VPC, an error message indicates a peering failurWhich factors could cause this error? (Choose two.)

answers.content: The IPv4 CIDR ranges of the two VPCs overlap
answers.explanation: The IPv4 CIDR ranges of the two VPCs overlap: VPC peering requires that the CIDR blocks of the peered VPCs are unique and do not overlap. If you attempt to peer two VPCs where one CIDR range is contained within or overlaps with the other, AWS will reject the request. In your case, the application VPC has a CIDR of 10.10.0.0/16 and the shared services VPC has a CIDR of 10.10.10.0/24. Because 10.10.10.0/24 is a subset of 10.10.0.0/16, these ranges overlap, which prevents the peering connection from being created.

answers.content: The VPCs are not in the same Region
answers.explanation: incorrect because VPC peering is supported across Regions.

answers.content: One or both accounts do not have access to an Internet gateway
answers.explanation: Incorrect: Internet gateway access is not required or relevant for VPC peering.

answers.content: One of the VPCs was not shared through AWS Resource Access Manager
answers.explanation: Incorrect: VPC peering does not require resource sharing via AWS RAM.

answers.content: The IAM role in the peer accepter account does not have the correct permissions
answers.explanation: correct because cross-account VPC peering requires the accepter account to have the proper IAM permissions to accept the peering request. If the IAM role lacks ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection, the peering will fail.

questions.content: A delivery company needs to migrate its third-party route planning application to AWS. The third party supplies a supported Docker image from a public registry. The image can run in as many containers as required to generate the route map. The company has divided the delivery area into sections with supply hubs so that delivery drivers travel the shortest distance possible from the hubs to the customers. To reduce the time necessary to generate route maps, each section uses its own set of Docker containers with a custom configuration that processes orders only in the section's area. The company needs the ability to allocate resources cost-effectively based on the number of running containers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application in pods by using the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the pod.
answers.explanation: Amazon EKS on EC2 requires managing EC2 instances and Kubernetes control plane, increasing operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on AWS FargatUse the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application. Use the AWS CLI tag-resource API call to assign a custom tag to the pod.
answers.explanation: EKS on Fargate with manual tagging via CLI is more complex and less integrated than ECS managed tagging for cost allocation.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the AWS CLI with run-tasks set to true to launch the planning application by using the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.
answers.explanation: ECS on EC2 involves managing and patching EC2 instances, which increases operational overhead compared to Fargate.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on AWS FargatUse the AWS CLI run-task command and set enableECSManagedTags to true to launch the planning application. Use the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate removes the need to manage the underlying infrastructure, thus minimizing operational overhead. Enabling ECS managed tags and custom tags on tasks allows cost allocation based on the number of running containers effectively. AWS Fargate is a managed service that aligns with best practices by preferring managed AWS services over self-managed EC2 clusters. This approach supports scaling as required while maintaining cost-effectiveness without manual patching or cluster management.

questions.content: An AWS partner company is building a service in AWS Organizations using its organization named org1. This service requires the partner company to have access to AWS resources in a customer account, which is in a separate organization named org2. The company must establish least privilege security access using an API or command line tool to the customer account. What is the MOST secure way to allow org1 to access resources in org2?

answers.content: The customer should provide the partner company with their AWS account access keys to log in and perform the required tasks.
answers.explanation: Providing account access keys is insecure and does not follow least privilege principles.

answers.content: The customer should create an IAM user and assign the required permissions to the IAM user. The customer should then provide the credentials to the partner company to log in and perform the required tasks.
answers.explanation: Sharing IAM user credentials violates best practices by exposing long-term credentials and lacking scoped control via role assumption.

answers.content: The customer should create an IAM role and assign the required permissions to the IAM rolThe partner company should then use the IAM role's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) when requesting access to perform the required tasks.
answers.explanation: Using an IAM role without an external ID is less secure as it is vulnerable to the confused deputy problem.

answers.content: The customer should create an IAM role and assign the required permissions to the IAM rolThe partner company should then use the IAM role's Amazon Resource Name (ARN), including the external ID in the IAM role's trust policy, when requesting access to perform the required tasks.
answers.explanation: Creating an IAM role with the necessary permissions and allowing the partner company to assume that role is a best practice for cross-account access. Including an external ID in the IAM role's trust policy adds an important layer of security to prevent the confused deputy problem. Providing role ARN and requiring role assumption via API or CLI aligns with least privilege and secure access policies. Options involving direct access keys or IAM user credentials are less secure and do not follow best practices for least privilege and secure cross-account access.

questions.content: A company is running a critical application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database to store data. The RDS DB instance is deployed in Multi-AZ modA recent RDS database failover test caused a 40-second outage to the application. A solutions architect needs to design a solution to reduce the outage time to less than 20 seconds. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached in front of the database
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Memcached does not reduce database failover time; it only caches data.

answers.content: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in front of the database
answers.explanation: ElastiCache for Redis also only serves as a caching layer and does not reduce database failover time.

answers.content: Use RDS Proxy in front of the database.
answers.explanation: RDS Proxy is a highly effective tool for mitigating the DNS propagation bottleneck that often occurs during failovers. Instead of applications needing to detect connection failures, wait for DNS TTL to expire, and re-establish connections (which can take significantly longer than 20 seconds), RDS Proxy maintains a pool of connections and transparently routes traffic to the new primary instance. This can reduce client recovery time by up to 79% for Aurora MySQL.

answers.content: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL.
answers.explanation: Amazon Aurora is purpose-built for high availability. Unlike standard RDS for MySQL, which relies on traditional binlog replication (often leading to longer failover times as the standby must replay logs), Aurora utilizes a distributed, quorum-based storage layer. Failovers in Aurora are typically much faster—often under 30 seconds—because there is no need to replay transaction logs upon promotion.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Aurora Replica.
answers.explanation: By deploying Aurora Replicas in different Availability Zones, you provide Aurora with a pool of healthy targets. During a failover, Aurora automatically promotes the most appropriate reader to the writer role. This architecture is a prerequisite for the fast failover performance that Aurora provides.

answers.content: Create an RDS for MySQL read replica
answers.explanation: Read replicas are for scaling reads.Not used for Multi-AZ automatic failover.Failover time remains similar

questions.content: A company has hundreds of AWS accounts. The company recently implemented a centralized internal process for purchasing new Reserved Instances and modifying existing Reserved Instances. This process requires all business units that want to purchase or modify Reserved Instances to submit requests to a dedicated team for procurement. Previously, business units directly purchased or modified Reserved Instances in their own respective AWS accounts autonomously. A solutions architect needs to enforce the new process in the most secure way possiblWhich combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Ensure that all AWS accounts are part of an organization in AWS Organizations with all features enabled.
answers.explanation: SCPs are a feature of AWS Organizations that require All Features to be enabled. Without this, you cannot use SCPs to centrally restrict permissions across member accounts. This provides the necessary foundation for the management account to impose governance over the entire organization.

answers.content: Use AWS Config to report on the attachment of an IAM policy that denies access to the ec2:PurchaseReservedInstancesOffering action and the ec2:ModifyReservedInstances action.
answers.explanation: AWS Config is a detective control. While it can alert you when a policy is attached or a change occurs, it does not prevent the action from happening in the first place. You need an inline preventive control to enforce the new process.

answers.content: In each AWS account, create an IAM policy that denies the ec2:PurchaseReservedInstancesOffering action and the ec2:ModifyReservedInstances action.
answers.explanation: While you could apply IAM policies to individual users or roles, this is highly inefficient and insecure in an environment with hundreds of accounts. It requires manual, repetitive work for every identity and does not prevent account administrators from simply removing or bypassing the policy.

answers.content: Create an SCP that denies the ec2:PurchaseReservedInstancesOffering action and the ec2:ModifyReservedInstances action. Attach the SCP to each OU of the organization.
answers.explanation: SCPs are the most effective tool for this requirement because they define the maximum permissions allowed for member accounts, regardless of what local IAM policies permit (even if a user has administrative privileges). By denying the purchase and modification actions, you proactively prevent business units from acting autonomously. Attaching this to the Organizational Units (OUs) ensures that all current and future accounts within those business segments are automatically restricted.

answers.content: Ensure that all AWS accounts are part of an organization in AWS Organizations that uses the consolidated billing feature.
answers.explanation: While consolidated billing is required for centralized cost management and sharing RI benefits, it is not a mechanism for restricting permissions or enforcing security guardrails.

questions.content: A company is migrating some of its applications to AWS. The company wants to migrate and modernize the applications quickly after it finalizes networking and security strategies. The company has set up an AWS Direct Connect connection in a central network account. The company expects to have hundreds of AWS accounts and VPCs in the near futurThe corporate network must be able to access the resources on AWS seamlessly and also must be able to communicate with all the VPCs. The company also wants to route its cloud resources to the internet through its on-premises data center. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Create a Direct Connect gateway in the central account. In each of the accounts, create an association proposal by using the Direct Connect gateway and the account ID for every virtual private gateway.
answers.explanation: Uses virtual private gateways (VGW) per VPC.Not scalable for hundreds of VPCs.TGW is the modern scalable design.

answers.content: Create a Direct Connect gateway and a transit gateway in the central network account. Attach the transit gateway to the Direct Connect gateway by using a transit VIF.
answers.explanation: Using a Transit Gateway is the only way to scale connectivity to hundreds of VPCs efficiently. The Transit Gateway acts as a central hub for your VPCs, and the Direct Connect gateway (connected via a transit VIF) acts as the bridge between this hub and your on-premises network. This setup centralizes your hybrid connectivity and routing management.

answers.content: Provision an internet gateway. Attach the internet gateway to subnets. Allow internet traffic through the gateway.
answers.explanation: Internet Gateway contradicts requirement (egress must go through on-prem).

answers.content: Share the transit gateway with other accounts. Attach VPCs to the transit gateway.
answers.explanation: By using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share the Transit Gateway across all your AWS accounts, you can attach VPCs from any account to this central hub. This is essential for achieving the requirement of seamless communication between all VPCs and the corporate network.

answers.content: Provision VPC peering as necessary.
answers.explanation: VPC peering does not scale well.No transitive routing.Operationally complex for hundreds of VPCs.

answers.content: Provision only private subnets. Open the necessary route on the transit gateway and customer gateway to allow outbound internet traffic from AWS to flow through NAT services that run in the data center.
answers.explanation: To force internet traffic through your on-premises data center rather than using local AWS Internet Gateways, you must configure your routing policy. By advertising a default route (0.0.0.0/0) from your on-premises data center to AWS over the Direct Connect/Transit Gateway link, and updating your Transit Gateway and VPC route tables to point internet-bound traffic towards the Transit Gateway (which then routes it on-premises), you ensure all internet egress is controlled by your corporate data center.

questions.content: A company has purchased appliances from different vendors. The appliances all have IoT sensors. The sensors send status information in the vendors' proprietary formats to a legacy application that parses the information into JSON. The parsing is simple, but each vendor has a unique format. Once daily, the application parses all the JSON records and stores the records in a relational database for analysis. The company needs to design a new data analysis solution that can deliver faster and optimize costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Connect the IoT sensors to AWS IoT CorSet a rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to parse the information and save a .csv file to Amazon. S3 Use AWS Glue to catalog the files. Use Amazon Athena and Amazon QuickSight for analysis.
answers.explanation: Using AWS IoT Core to securely connect IoT sensors aligns with managed AWS services best practicSetting a rule to invoke AWS Lambda for parsing leverages serverless compute for scalable, event-driven data transformation. Storing parsed data in Amazon S3 as .csv files provides cost-effective, durable storage suitable for analytics. AWS Glue catalogs the data for structured query access, enabling Amazon Athena and QuickSight for fast, serverless analysis and visualization. This design improves speed and optimizes cost by offloading parsing to Lambda and leveraging serverless analytics without managing servers.

answers.content: Migrate the application server to AWS Fargate, which will receive the information from IoT sensors and parse the information into a relational format. Save the parsed information to Amazon Redshlft for analysis.
answers.explanation: Migrating the legacy application to Fargate still requires managing and maintaining the parsing logic and infrastructure, increasing operational overhead and costs.

answers.content: Create an AWS Transfer for SFTP server. Update the IoT sensor code to send the information as a .csv file through SFTP to the server. Use AWS Glue to catalog the files. Use Amazon Athena for analysis.
answers.explanation: Updating IoT sensor code to send .csv via SFTP is complex and not aligned with best practice to use managed services tailored for IoT ingestion; also SFTP transfer adds overhead and latency.

answers.content: Use AWS Snowball Edge to collect data from the IoT sensors directly to perform local analysis. Periodically collect the data into Amazon Redshift to perform global analysis.
answers.explanation: Using Snowball Edge for local collection and periodic global analysis is less optimal for faster analysis and adds complexity with physical devices, not aligning with cost optimization.

questions.content: A financial company is planning to migrate its web application from on premises to AWS. The company uses a third-party security tool to monitor the inbound traffic to the application. The company has used the security tool for the last 15 years, and the tool has no cloud solutions available from its vendor. The company's security team is concerned about how to integrate the security tool with AWS technology. The company plans to deploy the application migration to AWS on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances will run in an Auto Scaling group in a dedicated VPC. The company needs to use the security tool to inspect all packets that come in and out of the VPC. This inspection must occur in real time and must not affect the application's performancA solutions architect must design a target architecture on AWS that is highly available within an AWS Region. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Deploy the security tool on EC2 instances m a new Auto Scaling group in the existing VPC
answers.explanation: To perform the actual packet inspection, you need to deploy your third-party security software on EC2 instances. Using an Auto Scaling group ensures that the appliance fleet is highly available and can scale horizontally to handle varying traffic loads, maintaining performance during peak periods.

answers.content: Deploy the web application behind a Network Load Balancer
answers.explanation: Deploying the web application behind a Network Load Balancer does not address how to integrate the third-party security tool for inbound/outbound traffic inspection.

answers.content: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in front of the security tool instances
answers.explanation: An Application Load Balancer is not appropriate for redirecting all traffic for packet inspection; it works at the application layer, not network layer needed for this use case.

answers.content: Provision a Gateway Load Balancer for each Availability Zone to redirect the traffic to the security tool
answers.explanation: GWLB is specifically designed for this 'bump-in-the-wire' use case. It allows you to transparently route traffic from your application to a fleet of virtual appliances. It uses the GENEVE protocol to encapsulate packets, ensuring the security appliance receives the original traffic for deep packet inspection and then routes it back to the intended destination without requiring complex network changes or affecting the latency of the application itself.

answers.content: Provision a transit gateway to facilitate communication between VPCs.
answers.explanation: Provisioning a transit gateway is unnecessary since the requirement is for traffic inspection within a single VPC, not facilitating communication between multiple VPCs.

questions.content: A company is developing a new serverless API by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company integrated the Lambda functions with API Gateway to use several shared libraries and custom classes. A solutions architect needs to simplify the deployment of the solution and optimize for code reusWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Deploy the shared libraries and custom classes into a Docker imagStore the image in an S3 bucket. Create a Lambda layer that uses the Docker image as the sourcDeploy the API's Lambda functions as Zip packages. Configure the packages to use the Lambda layer.
answers.explanation: Lambda layers cannot be created from Docker images stored in S3; layers require zip packages, so this solution is invalid.

answers.content: Deploy the shared libraries and custom classes to a Docker imagUpload the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Create a Lambda layer that uses the Docker image as the sourcDeploy the API's Lambda functions as Zip packages. Configure the packages to use the Lambda layer.
answers.explanation: Lambda layers cannot be created from Docker images in Amazon ECR; layers require zip packages, so this solution is invalid.

answers.content: Deploy the shared libraries and custom classes to a Docker container in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) by using the AWS Fargate launch typDeploy the API's Lambda functions as Zip packages. Configure the packages to use the deployed container as a Lambda layer.
answers.explanation: ECS containers and Lambda layers are unrelated; deploying shared code to an ECS Fargate container does not simplify Lambda function packaging or reuse.

answers.content: Deploy the shared libraries, custom classes, and code for the API's Lambda functions to a Docker imagUpload the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Configure the API's Lambda functions to use the Docker image as the deployment package.
answers.explanation: Deploying the shared libraries, custom classes, and Lambda function code together in a Docker image and uploading it to Amazon ECR aligns with AWS best practices for simplifying deployment and optimizing code reusUsing the Docker image as the Lambda deployment package is a managed AWS solution supported for Lambda and avoids complex or unsupported mechanisms like trying to create Lambda layers from Docker images. This approach leverages the managed container image support for Lambda to package dependencies and code together, which simplifies deployment and code reuse without manual layer management. Options involving creating Lambda layers from Docker images are not valid since Lambda layers must be zip archives, not container images. Option C involving ECS with Fargate is not appropriate because ECS containers and Lambda layers are unrelated and do not simplify Lambda deployments.

questions.content: A company is building a software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution on AWS. The company has deployed an Amazon API Gateway REST API with AWS Lambda integration in multiple AWS Regions and in the same production account. The company offers tiered pricing that gives customers the ability to pay for the capacity to make a certain number of API calls per second. The premium tier offers up to 3,000 calls per second, and customers are identified by a unique API key. Several premium tier customers in various Regions report that they receive error responses of 429 Too Many Requests from multiple API methods during peak usage hours. Logs indicate that the Lambda function is never invoked. What could be the cause of the error messages for these customers?

answers.content: The Lambda function reached its concurrency limit.
answers.explanation: The Lambda function is not invoked, so concurrency limit cannot be reached.

answers.content: The Lambda function its Region limit for concurrency.
answers.explanation: Similar to A, Lambda is never called so regional concurrency limit is irrelevant.

answers.content: The company reached its API Gateway account limit for calls per second.
answers.explanation: This is a default limit applied across all APIs within an AWS account and per Region. If the combined traffic from all premium-tier customers (and any other API users) in that Region exceeds this limit, API Gateway will throttle requests account-wide. This explains why errors are seen across multiple API methods and Regions, and why the Lambda function is not invoked.

answers.content: The company reached its API Gateway default per-method limit for calls per second.
answers.explanation: No strict default per-method limit causing this scenario.Usage plans + API keys control per-customer throttling.Problem affects multiple customers → suggests account-level throttle

questions.content: A company runs its application in the eu-west-1 Region and has one account for each of its environments: development, testing, and production. All the environments are running 24 hours a day, 7 days a week by using stateful Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS for MySQL databases. The databases are between 500 GB and 800 GB in sizThe development team and testing team work on business days during business hours, but the production environment operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The company wants to reduce costs. All resources are tagged with an environment tag with either development, testing, or production as the key. What should a solutions architect do to reduce costs with the LEAST operational effort?

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs once every day. Configure the rule to invoke one AWS Lambda function that starts or slops instances based on me tag, day, and time.
answers.explanation: Single daily rule is insufficient to handle different start and stop times during business days, leading to less optimized cost savings.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the evening. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that stops instances based on the tag. Create a second EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the morning. Configure the second rule lo invoke another Lambda function that starts instances based on the tag.
answers.explanation: Stopping EC2 instances when not in use reduces costs without deleting data, preserving operational state, which aligns with security and operational best practices. EventBridge rules scheduled during business days align with development and testing team hours, minimizing running time and costs while production runs continuously. Using Lambda functions triggered by EventBridge for start/stop operations is a managed, automated solution with low operational overhead. Terminating and restoring instances (as in C and D) leads to potential data loss and longer downtime, increasing operational effort and risk. Option A's single rule running once a day lacks granularity needed to start and stop instances appropriately at business hours' start and end.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the evening, Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that terminates, instances based on the lag. Create a second EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the morning. Configure the second rule lo invoke another Lambda function that restores the instances from their last backup based on the tag.
answers.explanation: Terminating and restoring instances daily causes potential data loss and high operational overhead, violating best practices for stateful workloads.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs every hour. Configure the rule to invoke one AWS Lambda function that terminates or restores instances from their last backup based on the tag. day, and time.
answers.explanation: Hourly termination and restoration increases operational complexity and risk of data loss, not minimizing effort or cost effectively.

questions.content: A company is running a web application in a VPC. The web application runs on a group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is using AWS WAF. An external customer needs to connect to the web application. The company must provide IP addresses to all external customers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Assign an Elastic IP address to the NLB.
answers.explanation: NLB supports Elastic IPs but replacing ALB with NLB loses ALB features such as integration with AWS WAF, increasing changes and overhead.

answers.content: Allocate an Elastic IP address. Assign the Elastic IP address to the ALProvide the Elastic IP address to the customer.
answers.explanation: Elastic IPs cannot be directly assigned to ALBs; this option is not possible.

answers.content: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator. Specify the ALB as the accelerator's endpoint. Provide the accelerator's IP addresses to the customer.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that can be used by external customers to connect reliably. Global Accelerator integrates with ALBs and offers the least operational overhead with managed IP addresses. Replacing the ALB or assigning Elastic IPs directly to ALBs is not supported or requires more manual management. CloudFront IP addresses are dynamic and not guaranteed fixed, making it unsuitable for providing stable IP addresses to external customers.

answers.content: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the ALB as the origin. Ping the distribution's DNS name to determine the distribution's public IP address. Provide the IP address to the customer.
answers.explanation: CloudFront IP addresses are not static and can change, so they cannot reliably be provided to customers.

questions.content: A company is running a critical stateful web application on two Linux Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with an Amazon RDS for MySQL databasThe company hosts the DNS records for the application in Amazon Route 53. A solutions architect must recommend a solution to improve the resiliency of the application. The solution must meet the following objectives: • Application tier: RPO of 2 minutes. RTO of 30 minutes • Database tier: RPO of 5 minutes. RTO of 30 minutes The company does not want to make significant changes to the existing application architecturThe company must ensure optimal latency after a failover. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure the EC2 instances to use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery. Create a cross-Region read replica for the RDS DB instancCreate an ALB in a second AWS Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint, and associate the endpoint with the ALBs. Update DNS records to point to the Global Accelerator endpoint.
answers.explanation: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery is a managed service designed for fast and reliable recovery of EC2 instances, aligning with the RPO of 2 minutes and RTO of 30 minutes for the application tier. Cross-Region RDS read replica ensures database recovery point objective (RPO) of 5 minutes and RTO of 30 minutes by enabling quick failover with minimal data loss. Using AWS Global Accelerator optimizes latency post-failover by routing traffic to the nearest healthy endpoint, fulfilling the requirement for optimal latency. Creating an ALB in a second Region supports seamless failover for the application workload with minimal architectural changes. Overall, this solution leverages managed AWS services that meet defined RPO and RTO targets without significant architectural changes.
