answers.content: Configure the EC2 instances to use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to take snapshots of the EBS volumes. Configure RDS automated backups. Configure backup replication to a second AWS Region. Create an ALB in the second Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint, and associate the endpoint with the ALBs. Update DNS records to point to the Global Accelerator endpoint.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon DLM for snapshots is not a managed disaster recovery solution and generally cannot meet the strict RPO and RTO requirements.

answers.content: Create a backup plan in AWS Backup for the EC2 instances and RDS DB instancConfigure backup replication to a second AWS Region. Create an ALB in the second Region. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB. Update DNS records to point to CloudFront.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup with backup replication and CloudFront does not provide rapid recovery or failover capabilities to meet RTO and RPO targets; CloudFront is not designed for failover routing.

answers.content: Configure the EC2 instances to use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to take snapshots of the EBS volumes. Create a cross-Region read replica for the RDS DB instancCreate an ALB in a second AWS Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint, and associate the endpoint with the ALBs.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon DLM snapshots for EC2 instances does not meet the strict RPO and RTO requirements, making this solution less resilient despite other components.

questions.content: A global media company is planning a multi-Region deployment of an application. Amazon DynamoDB global tables will back the deployment to keep the user experience consistent across the two continents where users are concentrated. Each deployment will have a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company manages public DNS internally. The company wants to make the application available through an apex domain. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

answers.content: Migrate public DNS to Amazon Route 53. Create CNAME records for the apex domain to point to the ALB. Use a geolocation routing policy to route traffic based on user location.
answers.explanation: CNAME records are not valid for apex domains, so this will not work even if DNS is migrated to Route 53.

answers.content: Place a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the ALMigrate public DNS to Amazon Route 53. Create a CNAME record for the apex domain to point to the NLB's static IP address. Use a geolocation routing policy to route traffic based on user location.
answers.explanation: NLB does not natively provide static IP address for apex domain use and migrating DNS to Route 53 is unnecessary given Global Accelerator's static IP support.

answers.content: Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator with multiple endpoint groups that target endpoints in appropriate AWS Regions. Use the accelerator's static IP address to create a record in public DNS for the apex domain.
answers.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that can be used with apex domains, enabling direct routing without needing CNAME records, which are not supported at the apex domain level. Global Accelerator supports multi-Region deployments with endpoint groups, allowing traffic routing to the closest or healthiest application endpoint, aligning well with the multi-continent deployment requirement. Using Global Accelerator eliminates the need to migrate DNS to Route 53, as the company manages public DNS internally and can create records pointing to static IPs provided by Global Accelerator. This solution requires the least operational effort while leveraging a managed AWS service designed for global traffic management and high availability.

answers.content: Create an Amazon API Gateway API that is backed by AWS Lambda in one of the AWS Regions. Configure a Lambda function to route traffic to application deployments by using the round robin method. Create CNAME records for the apex domain to point to the API's URL.
answers.explanation: Using API Gateway and Lambda as a routing mechanism is unnecessarily complex and does not align with best practices for global multi-Region deployments and application load balancing.

questions.content: A company has a latency-sensitive trading platform that uses Amazon DynamoDB as a storage backend. The company configured the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity modA solutions architect needs to design a solution to improve the performance of the trading platform. The new solution must ensure high availability for the trading platform. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST latency?

answers.content: Create a two-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read and write data by using DAX.
answers.explanation: A two-node DAX cluster provides less high availability than a three-node cluster.

answers.content: Create a three-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read data by using DAX and to write data directly to the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: DAX is used to improve read latency for DynamoDB by providing in-memory caching. A three-node DAX cluster provides high availability and fault tolerancUsing DAX to read data reduces latency for reads, while writing directly to DynamoDB ensures data consistency and durability. Option B aligns with best practices for minimizing latency with DynamoDB and DAX while maintaining high availability.

answers.content: Create a three-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read data directly from the DynamoDB table and to write data by using DAX.
answers.explanation: Writing through DAX is not supported; DAX caches reads, not writes—writing should be done directly to DynamoDB.

answers.content: Create a single-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read data by using DAX and to write data directly to the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: A single-node DAX cluster does not provide high availability due to lack of redundancy.

questions.content: A company gives users the ability to upload images from a custom application. The upload process invokes an AWS Lambda function that processes and stores the image in an Amazon S3 bucket. The application invokes the Lambda function by using a specific function version ARN. The Lambda function accepts image processing parameters by using environment variables. The company often adjusts the environment variables of the Lambda function to achieve optimal image processing output. The company tests different parameters and publishes a new function version with the updated environment variables after validating results. This update process also requires frequent changes to the custom application to invoke the new function version ARN. These changes cause interruptions for users. A solutions architect needs to simplify this process to minimize disruption to users. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Directly modify the environment variables of the published Lambda function version. Use the SLATEST version to test image processing parameters.
answers.explanation: Environment variables of published versions are immutable, so directly modifying them is not possible.

answers.content: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the image processing parameters. Modify the Lambda function to retrieve the image processing parameters from the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: Introducing DynamoDB adds unnecessary complexity and operational overhead for managing parameters.

answers.content: Directly code the image processing parameters within the Lambda function and remove the environment variables. Publish a new function version when the company updates the parameters.
answers.explanation: Hardcoding parameters requires publishing new function versions and updating clients, causing the same disruption as before.

answers.content: Create a Lambda function alias. Modify the client application to use the function alias ARN. Reconfigure the Lambda alias to point to new versions of the function when the company finishes testing.
answers.explanation: Using a Lambda function alias allows the client application to use a stable ARN while the alias can be repointed to new function versions without changing the client codThis approach minimizes disruption to users by decoupling the function version from the invocation ARN. It also has low operational overhead since updating the alias is simpler and faster than changing the client or modifying published versions' environment variables directly. Managed Lambda features like aliases are preferred over more complex custom solutions.

questions.content: A company has deployed an application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The application uses Amazon Aurora for the database layer. An Amazon CloudFront distribution serves web requests and includes the Elastic Beanstalk domain name as the origin server. The distribution is configured with an alternate domain name that visitors use when they access the application. Each week, the company takes the application out of service for routine maintenancDuring the time that the application is unavailable, the company wants visitors to receive an informational message instead of a CloudFront error messagA solutions architect creates an Amazon S3 bucket as the first step in the process. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take next to meet the requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Upload static informational content to the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: This is necessary to provide the informational content, so it is a correct step.

answers.content: Create a new CloudFront distribution. Set the S3 bucket as the origin.
answers.explanation: Creating a new CloudFront distribution is unnecessarily complex; modifying the existing distribution is preferred.

answers.content: Set the S3 bucket as a second origin in the original CloudFront distribution. Configure the distribution and the S3 bucket to use an origin access identity (OAI).
answers.explanation: This correctly secures and configures access between CloudFront and the S3 bucket, aligning with best practices.

answers.content: During the weekly maintenance, edit the default cache behavior to use the S3 origin. Revert the change when the maintenance is complete.
answers.explanation: Temporarily switching the cache behavior to the S3 origin is the simplest way to serve the maintenance page securely.

answers.content: During the weekly maintenance, create a cache behavior for the S3 origin on the new distribution. Set the path pattern to  Set the precedence to 0. Delete the cache behavior when the maintenance is complete.
answers.explanation: Modifying a new distribution with cache behavior changes is more complex and less secure than modifying the existing distribution; also path pattern and precedence setting described is unclear.

answers.content: During the weekly maintenance, configure Elastic Beanstalk to serve traffic from the S3 bucket.
answers.explanation: Modifying a new distribution with cache behavior changes is more complex and less secure than modifying the existing distribution; also path pattern and precedence setting described is unclear.

questions.content: A company is running an event ticketing platform on AWS and wants to optimize the platform's cost-effectiveness. The platform is deployed on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 and is backed by an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instancThe company is developing new application features to run on Amazon EKS with AWS FargatThe platform experiences infrequent high peaks in demand. The surges in demand depend on event dates. Which solution will provide the MOST cost-effective setup for the platform?

answers.content: Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that the EKS cluster uses in its baseline load. Scale the cluster with Spot Instances to handle peaks. Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the database to meet predicted peak load for the year.
answers.explanation: Purchasing Reserved Instances at peak load for the database is cost-inefficient and risks overprovisioning.

answers.content: Purchase Compute Savings Plans for the predicted medium load of the EKS cluster. Scale the cluster with On-Demand Capacity Reservations based on event dates for peaks. Purchase 1-year No Upfront Reserved Instances for the database to meet the predicted base load. Temporarily scale out database read replicas during peaks.
answers.explanation: On-Demand Capacity Reservations for peaks incur unnecessary costs; read replicas for infrequent peaks add complexity and may not be cost-effective.

answers.content: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the predicted base load of the EKS cluster. Scale the cluster with Spot Instances to handle peaks. Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the database to meet the predicted base load. Temporarily scale up the DB instance manually during peaks.
answers.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans lack the flexibility of Compute Savings Plans for EKS, and manually scaling DB instance is correct but overall less flexible.

answers.content: Purchase Compute Savings Plans for the predicted base load of the EKS cluster. Scale the cluster with Spot Instances to handle peaks. Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the database to meet the predicted base load. Temporarily scale up the DB instance manually during peaks.
answers.explanation: Using Compute Savings Plans for the predicted base load provides flexibility and cost savings for EKS workloads without tying to specific instance types, aligning with best practices to run workloads independent of specific infrastructurScaling the cluster with Spot Instances to handle peaks maximizes cost-effectiveness by leveraging the lowest-cost compute available when demand surges. Purchasing 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the database to meet predicted base load ensures cost savings on steady-state capacity while maintaining reliability. Temporarily scaling up the RDS instance manually during peaks addresses the infrequent high demand cost-effectively without overprovisioning or incurring unnecessary long-term costs. Option D balances cost optimization and operational flexibility while following best practices of using managed services and purchasing options that avoid wasted resources.

questions.content: A company has migrated an application from on premises to AWS. The application frontend is a static website that runs on two Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application backend is a Python application that runs on three EC2 instances behind another ALB. The EC2 instances are large, general purpose On-Demand Instances that were sized to meet the on-premises specifications for peak usage of the application. The application averages hundreds of thousands of requests each month. However, the application is used mainly during lunchtime and receives minimal traffic during the rest of the day. A solutions architect needs to optimize the infrastructure cost of the application without negatively affecting the application availability. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Change all the EC2 instances to compute optimized instances that have the same number of cores as the existing EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: Simply changing the instance family does not address the core issue of paying for idle capacity. If the workload is not compute-bound, this might not provide savings and could potentially impact performance.

answers.content: Move the application frontend to a static website that is hosted on Amazon S3.
answers.explanation: Move the application frontend to a static website that is hosted on Amazon S3. The application frontend is a static website currently running on two EC2 instances behind an ALB. Hosting a static website on Amazon S3 is significantly more cost-effective and scalable than running EC2 instances for this purpose. This is a common and recommended architectural pattern for cost optimization of static content. E. Deploy the backend Python application to general purpose burstable EC2 instances that have the same number of cores as the existing EC2 instances. The backend application is currently running on large, general purpose On-Demand EC2 instances sized for peak usage, but traffic is minimal outside of lunchtime. Burstable performance instances (like T-series) are designed for workloads that experience periodic spikes in usage and are minimal most of the time. Using T-series instances offers a lower baseline cost while still providing the required peak performance during lunchtime, optimizing infrastructure cost without negatively affecting availability. Explanations for Incorrect Answers: A. Change all the EC2 instances to compute optimized instances that have the same number of cores as the existing EC2 instances. While compute-optimized instances (like C-series) might offer better performance for compute-intensive workloads, they are generally more expensive than general-purpose instances (like M-series or burstable T-series). Since the main goal is cost optimization for an application with minimal traffic outside of peak hours, changing to a higher-cost instance type is counterproductive to the cost optimization goal. C. Deploy the application frontend by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Use the same instance type for the nodes. Elastic Beanstalk automates deployment but still relies on underlying EC2 instances for the frontend, which is static content. This solution does not address the cost of running EC2 instances unnecessarily for a static website. Hosting on S3 (Option B) is the most cost-effective solution for a static website. D. Change all the backend EC2 instances to Spot Instances. Spot Instances offer the lowest cost but are interruptible, meaning AWS can terminate them with a two-minute warning when the capacity is needed. While Spot Instances are great for fault-tolerant or flexible workloads, using them for the main application backend that must maintain availability during peak usage (lunchtime) carries a significant risk of interruption, which would negatively affect application availability.

answers.content: Deploy the application frontend by using AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Use the same instance type for the nodes.
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk is a management layer that still deploys EC2 instances. If you continue using the same large, general-purpose On-Demand instances without scaling them to match the traffic, you will still be paying for significant idle time outside of lunchtime peaks.

answers.content: Change all the backend EC2 instances to Spot Instances.
answers.explanation: For the backend Python application, while Auto Scaling is the primary way to match capacity to demand, using Spot Instances provides steep discounts (up to 90%) compared to On-Demand pricing. Since the application handles hundreds of thousands of requests and runs behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB), it is likely fault-tolerant enough to handle the potential reclamation of Spot instances. Combined with an Auto Scaling group that can maintain a minimum fleet of instances or bridge capacity with On-Demand instances if needed, this strategy drastically reduces the compute bill for your backend fleet.

answers.content: Deploy the backend Python application to general purpose burstable EC2 instances that have the same number of cores as the existing EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: While burstable instances (like the T-series) are cheaper for workloads with low baseline utilization, they are generally not recommended for critical production applications that receive sustained traffic. If your application consumes all its CPU credits during the lunchtime peak, the instance performance will be throttled, potentially causing application latency or downtime.

questions.content: A company is subject to regulatory audits of its financial information. External auditors who use a single AWS account need access to the company's AWS account. A solutions architect must provide the auditors with secure, read-only access to the company's AWS account. The solution must comply with AWS security best practices. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: In the company's AWS account, create resource policies for all resources in the account to grant access to the auditors' AWS account. Assign a unique external ID to the resource policy.
answers.explanation: Granting access via resource policies to all resources is complex, less manageable, and does not follow the IAM best practice for cross-account access.

answers.content: In the company's AWS account, create an IAM role that trusts the auditors' AWS account. Create an IAM policy that has the required permissions. Attach the policy to the rolAssign a unique external ID to the role's trust policy.
answers.explanation: Creating an IAM role in the company's AWS account that trusts the auditors' AWS account allows secure, temporary, and auditable access without sharing long-term credentials. Assigning a unique external ID to the role's trust policy prevents the confused deputy problem, enhancing security in cross-account access. Attaching a read-only IAM policy follows the principle of least privilege and AWS best practices for granting external access. This method leverages AWS managed IAM capabilities, avoiding manual key sharing or resource policy complexity.

answers.content: In the company's AWS account, create an IAM user. Attach the required IAM policies to the IAM user. Create API access keys for the IAM user. Share the access keys with the auditors.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users with static access keys and sharing them is insecure, violates best practices, and increases risk of credential leakage.

answers.content: In the company's AWS account, create an IAM group that has the required permissions. Create an IAM user in the company's account for each auditor. Add the IAM users to the IAM group.
answers.explanation: Creating IAM users for each auditor within the company's account means managing long-term credentials and violates principle of least privilege and AWS best practices.

questions.content: A company wants to use AWS to create a business continuity solution in case the company's main on-premises application fails. The application runs on physical servers that also run other applications. The on-premises application that the company is planning to migrate uses a MySQL database as a data storAll the company's on-premises applications use operating systems that are compatible with Amazon EC2. Which solution will achieve the company's goal with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Install the AWS Replication Agent on the source servers, including the MySQL servers. Set up replication for all servers. Launch test instances for regular drills. Cut over to the test instances to fail over the workload in the case of a failure event.
answers.explanation: Manually setting up replication and managing test instances increases operational overhead compared to AWS Elastic DR.

answers.content: Install the AWS Replication Agent on the source servers, including the MySQL servers. Initialize AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery in the target AWS Region. Define the launch settings. Frequently perform failover and fallback from the most recent point in time.
answers.explanation: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS Elastic DR) is designed specifically for business continuity and disaster recovery with minimal operational overhead by automating replication and failover. Installing the AWS Replication Agent on source servers and using AWS Elastic DR aligns with the goal of minimizing operational overhead. Option B supports frequent failover and fallback from recent points in time, which is ideal for continuity solutions. Managed AWS services such as AWS Elastic DR are preferred over complex custom or manual solutions or partial migration approaches.

answers.content: Create AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication servers and a target Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster to host the databasCreate a DMS replication task to copy the existing data to the target DB cluster. Create a local AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) change data capture (CDC) task to keep the data synchronized. Install the rest of the software on EC2 instances by starting with a compatible base AMI.
answers.explanation: Using AWS DMS with a local change data capture solution and manual EC2 instance setup involves more operational complexity.

answers.content: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway on premises. Mount volumes on all on-premises servers. Install the application and the MySQL database on the new volumes. Take regular snapshots. Install all the software on EC2 Instances by starting with a compatible base AMI. Launch a Volume Gateway on an EC2 instancRestore the volumes from the latest snapshot. Mount the new volumes on the EC2 instances in the case of a failure event.
answers.explanation: Deploying Storage Gateway and managing snapshots and restores manually incurs higher operational overhead and complexity.

questions.content: A financial services company receives a regular data feed from its credit card servicing partner. Approximately 5,000 records are sent every 15 minutes in plaintext, delivered over HTTPS directly into an Amazon S3 bucket with server-side encryption. This feed contains sensitive credit card primary account number (PAN) data. The company needs to automatically mask the PAN before sending the data to another S3 bucket for additional internal processing. The company also needs to remove and merge specific fields, and then transform the record into JSON format. Additionally, extra feeds are likely to be added in the future, so any design needs to be easily expandablWhich solutions will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Invoke an AWS Lambda function on file delivery that extracts each record and writes it to an Amazon SQS queuInvoke another Lambda function when new messages arrive in the SQS queue to process the records, writing the results to a temporary location in Amazon S3. Invoke a final Lambda function once the SQS queue is empty to transform the records into JSON format and send the results to another S3 bucket for internal processing.
answers.explanation: This approach involves multiple Lambda functions and SQS queues which adds unnecessary complexity and operational overhead compared to a managed ETL service; also less scalable and harder to maintain.

answers.content: Invoke an AWS Lambda function on file delivery that extracts each record and writes it to an Amazon SQS queuConfigure an AWS Fargate container application to automatically scale to a single instance when the SQS queue contains messages. Have the application process each record, and transform the record into JSON format. When the queue is empty, send the results to another S3 bucket for internal processing and scale down the AWS Fargate instance.
answers.explanation: While scalable, using AWS Fargate with SQS involves managing container infrastructure and is more complex than serverless Glue ETL, reducing manageability and increasing operational effort.

answers.content: Create an AWS Glue crawler and custom classifier based on the data feed formats and build a table definition to match. Invoke an AWS Lambda function on file delivery to start an AWS Glue ETL job to transform the entire record according to the processing and transformation requirements. Define the output format as JSON. Once complete, have the ETL job send the results to another S3 bucket for internal processing.
answers.explanation: AWS Glue ETL jobs are a managed service designed for scalable, serverless data extraction, transformation, and loading, suitable for transforming and masking sensitive data automatically. Creating a Glue crawler and custom classifier allows for automatic schema inference, supporting easy expansion when new feeds are added. Glue ETL jobs can output in JSON format and send results directly to S3, fulfilling the transformation and output requirements securely and efficiently.

answers.content: Create an AWS Glue crawler and custom classifier based upon the data feed formats and build a table definition to match. Perform an Amazon Athena query on file delivery to start an Amazon EMR ETL job to transform the entire record according to the processing and transformation requirements. Define the output format as JSON. Once complete, send the results to another S3 bucket for internal processing and scale down the EMR cluster.
answers.explanation: Using Athena to start an EMR cluster is more complex and requires manual cluster management, which is less secure and less preferable compared to managed serverless Glue ETL jobs.

questions.content: A company is running an application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on containers m an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The ECS tasks use the Fargate launch typThe application's data is relational and is stored in Amazon Aurora MySQL. To meet regulatory requirements, the application must be able to recover to a separate AWS Region in the event of an application failurIn case of a failure, no data can be lost. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

answers.content: Provision an Aurora Replica in a different Region.
answers.explanation: Provisioning an Aurora Replica in a different Region provides continuous, managed replication with no data loss, meeting the requirement for recovery in another AWS Region. Aurora Replicas are managed by AWS, reducing operational overhead compared to setting up custom replication solutions. Using Aurora’s cross-region replication natively supports failover scenarios, ensuring minimal recovery time and point objectives. AWS DataSync and AWS DMS involve more setup and maintenance for continuous replication and do not provide native managed database replication like Aurora Replicas. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager snapshots every 5 minutes cannot guarantee no data loss, as snapshots are not continuous replication.

answers.content: Set up AWS DataSync for continuous replication of the data to a different Region.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync is not designed for continuous replication of relational database data with no data loss and requires more operational overhead.

answers.content: Set up AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to perform a continuous replication of the data to a different Region.
answers.explanation: AWS DMS requires configuring migration tasks and monitoring, which adds complexity and is not a native Aurora replication solution.

answers.content: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to schedule a snapshot every 5 minutes.
answers.explanation: Snapshots every 5 minutes may result in data loss since they are periodic and not continuous replication, violating the no data loss requirement.

questions.content: An international delivery company hosts a delivery management system on AWS. Drivers use the system to upload confirmation of delivery. Confirmation includes the recipient's signature or a photo of the package with the recipient. The driver's handheld device uploads signatures and photos through FTP to a single Amazon EC2 instancEach handheld device saves a file in a directory based on the signed-in user, and the file name matches the delivery number. The EC2 instance then adds metadata to the file after querying a central database to pull delivery information. The file is then placed in Amazon S3 for archiving. As the company expands, drivers report that the system is rejecting connections. The FTP server is having problems because of dropped connections and memory issues in response to these problems, a system engineer schedules a cron task to reboot the EC2 instance every 30 minutes. The billing team reports that files are not always in the archive and that the central system is not always updated. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that maximizes scalability to ensure that the archive always receives the files and that systems are always updated. The handheld devices cannot be modified, so the company cannot deploy a new application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an AMI of the existing EC2 instancCreate an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Configure the Auto Scaling group to have a minimum of three instances.
answers.explanation: Scaling multiple EC2 instances behind a load balancer does not address stateful FTP connection issues and memory problems, plus rebooting every 30 minutes is not a scalable or reliable solution.

answers.content: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server that places the files in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume to the existing EC2 instancPoint the EC2 instance to the new path for file processing.
answers.explanation: While AWS Transfer Family with EFS can store files, mounting EFS to the EC2 instance still relies on the problematic EC2 instance for metadata processing, not fully solving scalability and reliability.

answers.content: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server that places the files in Amazon S3. Use an S3 event notification through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to add the metadata and update the delivery system.
answers.explanation: AWS Transfer Family supports FTP and can directly place files into Amazon S3, which improves scalability and reliability compared to managing files manually on an EC2 instancUsing an S3 event notification with SNS to invoke a Lambda function ensures metadata processing and delivery system updates occur asynchronously and reliably. This approach removes the single point of failure caused by the EC2 instance and avoids issues with dropped connections and memory problems. The handheld devices cannot be changed, so the solution must accommodate FTP without modifying clients. Using managed AWS services like Transfer Family, S3, SNS, and Lambda adheres to best practices for scalability, durability, and operational reliability.

answers.content: Update the handheld devices to place the files directly in Amazon S3. Use an S3 event notification through Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to add the metadata and update the delivery system.
answers.explanation: Requires updating handheld devices to upload directly to S3, but the problem states devices cannot be modified.

questions.content: A solutions architect is investigating an issue in which a company cannot establish new sessions in Amazon Workspaces. An initial analysis indicates that the issue involves user profiles. The Amazon Workspaces environment is configured to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server as the profile share storagThe FSx for Windows File Server file system is configured with 10 TB of storagThe solutions architect discovers that the file system has reached Its maximum capacity. The solutions architect must ensure that users can regain access. The solution also must prevent the problem from occurring again. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Remove old user profiles to create spacMigrate the user profiles to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
answers.explanation: Migrating to FSx for Lustre is unsuitable as it is not compatible with Windows user profiles in Amazon WorkSpaces.

answers.content: Increase capacity by using the update-file-system command. Implement an Amazon CloudWatch metric that monitors free spacUse Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function to increase capacity as required.
answers.explanation: Use the update-file-system API to immediately increase FSx for Windows File Server storage (supports online scaling so users quickly regain access), and prevent recurrence by monitoring the FreeStorageCapacity CloudWatch metric with an EventBridge rule that triggers a Lambda function to automatically expand storage, providing automated remediation with minimal operational overhead and no architectural redesign using the native supported scaling model.

answers.content: Monitor the file system by using the FreeStorageCapacity metric in Amazon CloudWatch. Use AWS Step Functions to increase the capacity as required.
answers.explanation: Using AWS Step Functions to increase FSx capacity is not a supported or documented method to manage FSx file system size.

answers.content: Remove old user profiles to create spacCreate an additional FSx for Windows File Server file system. Update the user profile redirection for 50% of the users to use the new file system.
answers.explanation: Removing profiles is a temporary, reactive fix that does not prevent future issues. Managing multiple file systems and manually splitting users introduces unnecessary operational complexity, increases administrative burden, and does not provide a scalable long-term solution.

questions.content: A weather service provides high-resolution weather maps from a web application hosted on AWS in the eu-west-1 Region. The weather maps are updated frequently and stored in Amazon S3 along with static HTML content. The web application is fronted by Amazon CloudFront. The company recently expanded to serve users in the us-east-1 Region, and these new users report that viewing their respective weather maps is slow from time to timWhich combination of steps will resolve the us-east-1 performance issues? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Configure the AWS Global Accelerator endpoint for the S3 bucket in eu-west-1. Configure endpoint groups for TCP ports 80 and 443 in us-east-1.
answers.explanation: Global Accelerator endpoints are not recommended for S3 bucket origins; it is designed for improving TCP/UDP performance for IP-based applications, not S3 access.

answers.content: Create a new S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 cross-Region replication to synchronize from the S3 bucket in eu-west-1.
answers.explanation: Create a new S3 bucket in us-east-1 and enable S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from eu-west-1 so weather maps are stored closer to US users, reducing origin fetch latency.

answers.content: Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint in us-east-1.
answers.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoints are regional and modifying requests with Lambda@Edge to use these is unnecessary when replication to a regional bucket is available.

answers.content: Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the S3 bucket in us-east-1.
answers.explanation: Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America so CloudFront routes them to the us-east-1 S3 bucket origin, ensuring users are served from the nearest Region.

answers.content: Configure the AWS Global Accelerator endpoint for us-east-1 as an origin on the CloudFront distribution. Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the new origin.
answers.explanation: Configuring Global Accelerator as an origin on CloudFront is not supported for S3 buckets, making this approach invalid.

questions.content: A company has developed APIs that use Amazon API Gateway with Regional endpoints. The APIs call AWS Lambda functions that use API Gateway authentication mechanisms. After a design review, a solutions architect identifies a set of APIs that do not require public access. The solutions architect must design a solution to make the set of APIs accessible only from a VPC. All APIs need to be called with an authenticated user Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

answers.content: Create an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Create a target group. Select the Lambda function to call. Use the ALB DNS name to call the API from the VPC.
answers.explanation: Using an ALB with Lambda is unnecessary complexity and not aligned with private API Gateway access best practices.

answers.content: Remove the DNS entry that is associated with the API in API Gateway. Create a hosted zone in Amazon Route 53. Create a CNAME record in the hosted zonUpdate the API in API Gateway with the CNAME record. Use the CNAME record to call the API from the VPC.
answers.explanation: Removing DNS entries and creating CNAME records does not restrict API access to VPC only and is not a secure method for private API access.

answers.content: Update the API endpoint from Regional to private in API Gateway. Create an interface VPC endpoint in the VPCreate a resource policy, and attach it to the API. Use the VPC endpoint to call the API from the VPC.
answers.explanation: Updating the API endpoint to private and creating an interface VPC endpoint allows the API to be accessible only from within the VPC, aligning with the requirement to restrict public access. Using a resource policy attached to the API ensures controlled authenticated access. Interface VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink are designed for private access to AWS services, which is recommended for private APIs. This solution requires the least effort as it leverages managed AWS services specifically intended for private API access, without additional infrastructure or complex network configuration.

answers.content: Deploy the Lambda functions inside the VPC Provision an EC2 instance, and install an Apache server. From the Apache server, call the Lambda functions. Use the internal CNAME record of the EC2 instance to call the API from the VPC.
answers.explanation: Deploying Lambda inside VPC and using an EC2 instance with Apache is complex, increases operational overhead, and is not a recommended best practice for private API access.

questions.content: A company is processing videos in the AWS Cloud by Using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. It takes 30 minutes to process a video Several EC2 instances scale in and out depending on the number of videos in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuThe company has configured the SQS queue with a redrive policy that specifies a target dead-letter queue and a maxReceiveCount of 1. The company has set the visibility timeout for the SQS queue to 1 hour. The company has set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to notify the development team when there are messages in the dead-letter queuSeveral times during the day. the development team receives notification that messages are in the dead-letter queue and that videos have not been processed property. An investigation finds no errors m the application logs. How can the company solve this problem?

answers.content: Turn on termination protection tor the EC2 Instances
answers.explanation: Turn on termination protection for the EC2 instances: This is a broad setting for the instance itself (preventing manual or API-based termination) and is generally not used for managing dynamic Auto Scaling behavior. It would prevent the instance from ever being terminated by the Auto Scaling group, leading to unnecessary costs.

answers.content: Update the visibility timeout for the SQS queue to 3 hours
answers.explanation: Update the visibility timeout for the SQS queue to 3 hours: While this would give the instances more time before the message reappears, it does not stop the Auto Scaling group from terminating the instance mid-process. You would still lose the work and suffer from the same issue; you would just be waiting longer for the message to return to the queue.

answers.content: Configure scale-in protection for the instances during processing
answers.explanation: Configuring scale-in protection during processing prevents Auto Scaling from terminating EC2 instances that are actively handling SQS messages, ensures each video is fully processed and deleted from the queue before scale-in occurs, and represents the correct solution for the ASG + SQS worker pattern.

answers.content: Update the redrive policy and set maxReceiveCount to 0.
answers.explanation: Update the redrive policy and set maxReceiveCount to 0: Setting maxReceiveCount to 0 is invalid for a redrive policy configuration, as the policy requires a count of at least 1 to function.

questions.content: A software as a service (SaaS) based company provides a case management solution to customers A3 part of the solution. The company uses a standalone Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server to send email messages from an application. The application also stores an email template for acknowledgement email messages that populate customer data before the application sends the email message to the customer. The company plans to migrate this messaging functionality to the AWS Cloud and needs to minimize operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answers.content: Set up an SMTP server on Amazon EC2 instances by using an AMI from the AWS MarketplacStore the email template in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the template from the S3 bucket and to merge the customer data from the application with the templatUse an SDK in the Lambda function to send the email message.
answers.explanation: Managing SMTP servers on EC2 increases operational overhead and complexity, not minimizing it.

answers.content: Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send email messages. Store the email template in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the template from the S3 bucket and to merge the customer data from the application with the templatUse an SDK in the Lambda function to send the email message.
answers.explanation: Storing templates in S3 and merging them in Lambda is more complex and less cost-effective than using SES built-in templating.

answers.content: Set up an SMTP server on Amazon EC2 instances by using an AMI from the AWS MarketplacStore the email template in Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) with parameters for the customer data. Create an AWS Lambda function to call the SES template and to pass customer data to replace the parameters. Use the AWS Marketplace SMTP server to send the email message.
answers.explanation: Combines managing SMTP servers on EC2 with SES templating, increasing operational overhead unnecessarily.

answers.content: Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send email messages. Store the email template on Amazon SES with parameters for the customer data. Create an AWS Lambda function to call the SendTemplatedEmail API operation and to pass customer data to replace the parameters and the email destination.
answers.explanation: Amazon SES is a managed service designed to send email, which reduces operational overhead compared to managing SMTP servers on EC2. Amazon SES supports storing email templates with parameters and can send templated emails using the SendTemplatedEmail API, which integrates customer data securely and efficiently. Using SES templates and API removes the need for custom Lambda-based template merging and external email template storage, minimizing complexity and cost. Managing SMTP credentials and infrastructure challenges is avoided by using SES directly for templated emails, following best practices for email sending in AWS.

questions.content: A company runs a content management application on a single Windows Amazon EC2 instance in a development environment. The application reads and writes static content to a 2 TB Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is attached to the instance as the root devicThe company plans to deploy this application in production as a highly available and fault-tolerant solution that runs on at least three EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. A solutions architect must design a solution that joins all the instances that run the application to an Active Directory domain. The solution also must implement Windows ACLs to control access to file contents. The application always must maintain exactly the same content on all running instances at any given point in timWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST management overhead?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file sharCreate an Auto Scaling group that extends across three Availability Zones and maintains a minimum size of three instances. Implement a user data script to install the application, join the instance to the AD domain, and mount the EFS file share.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS does not support Windows ACLs and native Windows permissions, which are required for the application.

answers.content: Create a new AMI from the current EC2 Instance that is running. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Create an Auto Scaling group that extends across three Availability Zones and maintains a minimum size of three instances. Implement a user data script to join the instance to the AD domain and mount the FSx for Lustre file system.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for high-performance computing and does not support Windows ACLs or Active Directory domain join.

answers.content: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Create an Auto Scaling group that extends across three Availability Zones and maintains a minimum size of three instances. Implement a user data script to install the application and mount the FSx for Windows File Server file system. Perform a seamless domain join to join the instance to the AD domain.
answers.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server supports Windows ACLs, enabling native Windows permission management, which is required for the application. FSx for Windows File Server is a managed service that provides a fully managed file system compatible with Windows workloads, reducing management overhead. The solution supports seamless domain joining for EC2 instances, meeting the Active Directory requirement with minimal operational complexity. FSx ensures consistency of file content across instances, meeting the requirement for always having the same content on all running instances.

answers.content: Create a new AMI from the current EC2 instance that is running. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Create an Auto Scaling group that extends across three Availability Zones and maintains a minimum size of three Instances. Perform a seamless domain join to join the instance to the AD domain.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EFS lacks support for Windows ACLs and Windows-native permission management; also, creating a new AMI adds unnecessary management overhead compared to FSx.

questions.content: A life sciences company is using a combination of open source tools to manage data analysis workflows and Docker containers running on servers in its on-premises data center to process genomics data. Sequencing data is generated and stored on a local storage area network (SAN), and then the data is processed. The research and development teams are running into capacity issues and have decided to re-architect their genomics analysis platform on AWS to scale based on workload demands and reduce the turnaround time from weeks to days. The company has a high-speed AWS Direct Connect connection. Sequencers will generate around 200 GB of data for each genome, and individual jobs can take several hours to process the data with ideal compute capacity. The end result will be stored in Amazon S3. The company is expecting 10-15 job requests each day. Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Use regularly scheduled AWS Snowball Edge devices to transfer the sequencing data into AWS. When AWS receives the Snowball Edge device and the data is loaded into Amazon S3, use S3 events to trigger an AWS Lambda function to process the data.
answers.explanation: AWS Snowball Edge is a physical data transfer appliance; scheduled use conflicts with continuous data generation and high-speed Direct Connect available, making it less efficient.

answers.content: Use AWS Data Pipeline to transfer the sequencing data to Amazon S3. Use S3 events to trigger an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to launch custom-AMI EC2 instances running the Docker containers to process the data.
answers.explanation: AWS Data Pipeline is less suitable compared to DataSync for large-scale data transfer, and using EC2 Auto Scaling with custom AMIs requires more manual management than AWS Batch.

answers.content: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the sequencing data to Amazon S3. Use S3 events to trigger an AWS Lambda function that starts an AWS Step Functions workflow. Store the Docker images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and trigger AWS Batch to run the container and process the sequencing data.
answers.explanation: AWS DataSync efficiently transfers large amounts of data to Amazon S3, leveraging the high-speed AWS Direct Connect connection for scalable and fast data movement. Using S3 events to trigger AWS Lambda functions that start AWS Step Functions workflows aligns with managed services best practices, automating processing without manual intervention. Storing Docker images in Amazon ECR is a managed service designed for container storage and management. AWS Batch is a managed service that can run containerized jobs on optimized compute resources, ideal for workloads that require several hours of processing time and can scale based on demand. This solution maximizes scalability, operational efficiency, and security best practices using managed AWS services rather than manual or custom solutions.

answers.content: Use an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to transfer the sequencing data to Amazon S3. Use S3 events to trigger an AWS Batch job that executes on Amazon EC2 instances running the Docker containers to process the data.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway adds unnecessary complexity compared to DataSync, and while AWS Batch usage is correct, DataSync is preferred for data transfer in this scenario.

questions.content: A company is building a call center by using Amazon Connect. The company's operations team is defining a disaster recovery (DR) strategy across AWS Regions. The contact center has dozens of contact flows, hundreds of users, and dozens of claimed phone numbers. Which solution will provide DR with the LOWEST RTO?

answers.content: Create an AWS Lambda function to check the availability of the Amazon Connect instance and to send a notification to the operations team in case of unavailability. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes. After notification, instruct the operations team to use the AWS Management Console to provision a new Amazon Connect instance in a second Region. Deploy the contact flows, users, and claimed phone numbers by using an AWS CloudFormation template.
answers.explanation: Requires manual provisioning of the Connect instance after failure, increasing RTO.

answers.content: Provision a new Amazon Connect instance with all existing users in a second Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to check the availability of the Amazon Connect instancCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes. In the event of an issue, configure the Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions contact flows and claimed numbers in the second Region.
answers.explanation: These rely on deploying AWS CloudFormation templates after a disaster is detected. This approach results in a significantly higher RTO because you must wait for the infrastructure to provision and the resources (users, flows, numbers) to be created from scratch.

answers.content: Provision a new Amazon Connect instance with all existing contact flows and claimed phone numbers in a second Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for the URL of the Amazon Connect instancCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for failed health checks. Create an AWS Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions all users. Configure the alarm to invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Provisioning users via Lambda after failure delays availability of the instance with users, increasing RTO.

answers.content: Provision a new Amazon Connect instance with all existing users and contact flows in a second Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for the URL of the Amazon Connect instancCreate an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for failed health checks. Create an AWS Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions claimed phone numbers. Configure the alarm to invoke the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: provides the lowest RTO because the secondary Amazon Connect instance is pre-provisioned with users and contact flows, and only claimed phone numbers are created automatically upon Route 53 health check failure, minimizing failover actions and recovery time.

questions.content: A company runs a customer service center that accepts calls and automatically sends all customers a managed, interactive, two-way experience survey by text messagThe applications that support the customer service center run on machines that the company hosts in an on-premises data center. The hardware that the company uses is old, and the company is experiencing downtime with the system. The company wants to migrate the system to AWS to improve reliability. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST ongoing operational overhead?

answers.content: Use Amazon Connect to replace the old call center hardwarUse Amazon Pinpoint to send text message surveys to customers.
answers.explanation: Amazon Connect is a fully managed service for contact centers that removes the need to maintain call center hardware, directly addressing the reliability issues caused by old on-premises hardwarAmazon Pinpoint is a managed service designed for sending targeted, interactive SMS messages which suits the requirement for two-way survey text messaging with low operational overhead. Using these managed services reduces operational overhead compared to migrating and managing traditional software on EC2 instances or relying solely on one service, aligning with AWS best practices.

answers.content: Use Amazon Connect to replace the old call center hardwarUse Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send text message surveys to customers.
answers.explanation: Amazon SNS is a simple notification service not optimized for interactive two-way SMS surveys, thus not fully meeting the requirements.

answers.content: Migrate the call center software to Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. Use the EC2 instances to send text message surveys to customers.
answers.explanation: Managing EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group requires significant operational effort and does not eliminate hardware or software management overhead.

answers.content: Use Amazon Pinpoint to replace the old call center hardware and to send text message surveys to customers.
answers.explanation: Amazon Pinpoint cannot replace the call center hardware functionality; it only handles messaging, so this does not solve the call center system's reliability issue.

questions.content: A company has an application that runs as a ReplicaSet of multiple pods in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster has nodes in multiple Availability Zones. The application generates many small files that must be accessible across all running instances of the application. The company needs to back up the files and retain the backups for 1 year. Which solution will meet these requirements while providing the FASTEST storage performance?

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and a mount target for each subnet that contains nodes in the EKS cluster. Configure the ReplicaSet to mount the file system. Direct the application to store files in the file system. Configure AWS Backup to back up and retain copies of the data for 1 year.
answers.explanation: Amazon EFS provides a shared file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple pods across Availability Zones, meeting the requirement for accessible files across all running instances. EFS is a managed AWS service that supports fast storage performance suitable for many small files and allows straightforward backup using AWS Backup with retention policies. Using AWS Backup with EFS reduces operational overhead and leverages a native managed backup solution for long-term retention. EBS Multi-Attach is limited in the number of concurrent mounts and Availability Zone boundaries, thus not ideal for multi-AZ EKS clusters. S3 is object storage rather than a mounted file system, and mounting S3 as a file system is non-native and could degrade performancLocal pod storage is ephemeral and not shared, making it unsuitable for sharing files across ReplicaSet pods and for reliable backups.

answers.content: Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumEnable the EBS Multi-Attach featurConfigure the ReplicaSet to mount the EBS volumDirect the application to store files in the EBS volumConfigure AWS Backup to back up and retain copies of the data for 1 year.
answers.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach cannot span multiple Availability Zones, so it cannot provide access to all pods running across multiple AZs.

answers.content: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the ReplicaSet to mount the S3 bucket. Direct the application to store files in the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Versioning to retain copies of the data. Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete objects after 1 year.
answers.explanation: Amazon S3 is object storage and not suitable as a shared file system mounted by pods; also, mounting S3 as a file system is non-native and may degrade performance.

answers.content: Configure the ReplicaSet to use the storage available on each of the running application pods to store the files locally. Use a third-party tool to back up the EKS cluster for 1 year.
answers.explanation: Local pod storage is not shared between pods and is ephemeral, making it unsuitable for sharing files and reliable backups across ReplicaSet pods.

questions.content: A solutions architect needs to assess a newly acquired company's portfolio of applications and databases. The solutions architect must create a business case to migrate the portfolio to AWS. The newly acquired company runs applications in an on-premises data center. The data center is not well documented. The solutions architect cannot immediately determine how many applications and databases exist. Traffic for the applications is variablSome applications are batch processes that run at the end of each month. The solutions architect must gain a better understanding of the portfolio before a migration to AWS can begin. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to evaluate migration. Use AWS Service Catalog to understand application and database dependencies.
answers.explanation: AWS SMS and DMS focus on migration, not discovery; Service Catalog does not assess dependencies effectively.

answers.content: Use AWS Application Migration ServicRun agents on the on-premises infrastructurManage the agents by using AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Storage Gateway to assess local storage needs and database dependencies.
answers.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway is for storage integration, not for application and database dependency assessment.

answers.content: Use Migration Evaluator to generate a list of servers. Build a report for a business casUse AWS Migration Hub to view the portfolio. Use AWS Application Discovery Service to gain an understanding of application dependencies.
answers.explanation: Migration Evaluator generates a list of servers and helps build a business case based on the portfolio. AWS Migration Hub provides a centralized view of the migration portfolio. AWS Application Discovery Service gathers information about application dependencies, essential for understanding the portfolio. This approach aligns with AWS best practices for assessing undocumented on-premises environments before migration.

answers.content: Use AWS Control Tower in the destination account to generate an application portfolio. Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) to generate deeper reports and a business casUse a landing zone for core accounts and resources.
answers.explanation: AWS Control Tower and SMS do not generate portfolio reports; Control Tower is for landing zone governance, not discovery.

questions.content: A company needs to audit the security posture of a newly acquired AWS account. The company's data security team requires a notification only when an Amazon S3 bucket becomes publicly exposed. The company has already established an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that has the data security team's email address subscribed. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Create an S3 event notification on all S3 buckets for the isPublic event. Select the SNS topic as the target for the event notifications.
answers.explanation: S3 event notifications do not generate events for bucket policy changes or public exposure status.

answers.content: Create an analyzer in AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for the event type "Access Analyzer Finding" with a filter for "isPublic: true." Select the SNS topic as the EventBridge rule target.
answers.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer can analyze S3 bucket policies and detect public exposure (isPublic findings). Creating an EventBridge rule for the 'Access Analyzer Finding' event filtered by 'isPublic: true' targets exactly the required notification condition. Selecting the existing SNS topic as the EventBridge rule target aligns with the requirement to notify the data security team via email. This approach uses managed AWS services designed for continuous analysis and notification of public bucket exposure, meeting security best practices.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for the event type "Bucket-Level API Call via CloudTrail" with a filter for "PutBucketPolicy." Select the SNS topic as the EventBridge rule target.
answers.explanation: Filtering CloudTrail events for PutBucketPolicy does not guarantee the bucket is publicly exposed; also, complexity and potential for false positives are high.

answers.content: Activate AWS Config and add the cloudtrail-s3-dataevents-enabled rulCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule for the event type "Config Rules Re-evaluation Status" with a filter for "NON_COMPLIANT." Select the SNS topic as the EventBridge rule target.
answers.explanation: AWS Config rule triggering on NON_COMPLIANT states is less direct and may not specifically identify public exposure events for notification.

questions.content: A company has multiple business units that each have separate accounts on AWS. Each business unit manages its own network with several VPCs that have CIDR ranges that overlap. The company's marketing team has created a new internal application and wants to make the application accessible to all the other business units. The solution must use private IP addresses only. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answers.content: Instruct each business unit to add a unique secondary CIDR range to the business unit's VPC. Peer the VPCs and use a private NAT gateway in the secondary range to route traffic to the marketing team.
answers.explanation: VPC peering cannot be used with overlapping CIDR blocks, so adding secondary CIDR is complex and high operational overhead.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as a virtual appliance in the marketing account's VPC. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the marketing team and each business unit's VPC. Perform NAT where necessary.
answers.explanation: Using EC2 as a virtual appliance with multiple VPN connections and NAT introduces high operational overhead and complexity.

answers.content: Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service to share the marketing application. Grant permission to specific AWS accounts to connect to the servicCreate interface VPC endpoints in other accounts to access the application by using private IP addresses.
answers.explanation: AWS PrivateLink allows sharing services across accounts using private IP addresses without requiring unique or non-overlapping CIDR ranges. PrivateLink uses interface VPC endpoints which provide private connectivity to the application with low operational overhead and no need for managing VPNs or NAT. VPC peering requires non-overlapping CIDR blocks, which is not possible here due to overlapping ranges. Managed AWS services like PrivateLink reduce complexity and align with security best practices.

answers.content: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the marketing application in a private subnet. Create an API Gateway API. Use the Amazon API Gateway private integration to connect the API to the NLB. Activate IAM authorization for the API. Grant access to the accounts of the other business units.
answers.explanation: Using API Gateway with NLB is more complex and involves managing IAM authorization and API Gateway setup, increasing operational overhead compared to PrivateLink.

questions.content: A company uses an AWS CodeCommit repository. The company must store a backup copy of the data that is in the repository in a second AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Configure AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the CodeCommit repository data to the second Region.
answers.explanation: Elastic Disaster Recovery does not support replicating CodeCommit repository data.

answers.content: Use AWS Backup to back up the CodeCommit repository on an hourly schedulCreate a cross-Region copy in the second Region.
answers.explanation: AWS Backup cannot back up or replicate CodeCommit repositories.

answers.content: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke AWS CodeBuild when the company pushes code to the repository. Use CodeBuild to clone the repository. Create a .zip file of the content. Copy the file to an S3 bucket in the second Region.
answers.explanation: AWS CodeCommit does not have a native cross-Region replication feature or snapshot capability. Using an EventBridge rule to trigger CodeBuild on repository changes is a managed and automated approach. CodeBuild can clone the repository, package it, and copy to an S3 bucket in another Region, ensuring automated backups. Elastic Disaster Recovery and AWS Backup do not support CodeCommit repository backup or replication. Step Functions does not provide a native capability to snapshot CodeCommit repositories.

answers.content: Create an AWS Step Functions workflow on an hourly schedule to take a snapshot of the CodeCommit repository. Configure the workflow to copy the snapshot to an S3 bucket in the second Region
answers.explanation: Step Functions cannot natively create snapshots of CodeCommit repositories.

questions.content: A solutions architect wants to cost-optimize and appropriately size Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS account. The solutions architect wants to ensure that the instances are optimized based on CPU, memory, and network metrics. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Purchase AWS Business Support or AWS Enterprise Support for the account.
answers.explanation: While purchasing Business or Enterprise support grants access to the full suite of AWS Trusted Advisor checks, it is a service-level agreement and support structure, not a technical tool for resource optimization.

answers.content: Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor and review any "Low Utilization Amazon EC2 Instances" recommendations.
answers.explanation: Trusted Advisor is excellent for identifying 'Low Utilization' EC2 instances (based primarily on CPU and network). However, it is a high-level advisory tool. It lacks the advanced machine learning and granular rightsizing analysis provided by Compute Optimizer, especially when memory constraints are involved.

answers.content: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent and configure memory metric collection on the EC2 instances.
answers.explanation: By default, Amazon EC2 only provides metrics for CPU, disk I/O, and network activity. Memory utilization is not captured automatically because the operating system needs to be queried to retrieve this data. Installing the CloudWatch agent is a prerequisite for capturing accurate memory usage, which is essential for rightsizing instances that are memory-constrained.

answers.content: Configure AWS Compute Optimizer in the AWS account to receive findings and optimization recommendations.
answers.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze the historical utilization metrics (CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O) of your EC2 instances. It provides actionable rightsizing recommendations (e.g., downsizing, upsizing, or changing instance families) to help you balance performance and cost. It is specifically designed to use the memory metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent to provide more precise and 'risk-aware' recommendations than general-purpose tools.

answers.content: Create an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the AWS Regions, instance families, and operating systems of interest.
answers.explanation: While this is a powerful cost-reduction strategy, it is a rate optimization tactic (discounting the price of usage) rather than a resource optimization tactic (sizing the resource correctly). The best practice is to right-size your environment first using Compute Optimizer, and then apply Savings Plans to the optimized, efficient footprint.

questions.content: A delivery company is running a serverless solution in the AWS Cloud. The solution manages user data, delivery information, and past purchase details. The solution consists of several microservices. The central user service stores sensitive data in an Amazon DynamoDB tablSeveral of the other microservices store a copy of parts of the sensitive data in different storage services. The company needs the ability to delete user information upon request. As soon as the central user service deletes a user, every other microservice must also delete its copy of the data immediately. Which solution will meet these requirements?

answers.content: Activate DynamoDB Streams on the DynamoDB tablCreate an AWS Lambda trigger for the DynamoDB stream that will post events about user deletion in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queuConfigure each microservice to poll the queue and delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: Using DynamoDB Streams with Lambda to post to SQS adds unnecessary complexity and SQS polling delays; also, SQS does not have native event filtering for multiple subscribers, making it less efficient.

answers.content: Set up DynamoDB event notifications on the DynamoDB tablCreate an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target for the DynamoDB event notification. Configure each microservice to subscribe to the SNS topic and to delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: SNS subscriptions do not support advanced filtering required for granular user deletion events, leading to all subscribers receiving all messages, which can cause excess processing or delays.

answers.content: Configure the central user service to post an event on a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus when the company deletes a user. Create an EventBridge rule for each microservice to match the user deletion event pattern and invoke logic in the microservice to delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: Using Amazon EventBridge allows the central user service to post an event indicating user deletion, which can trigger multiple microservices to immediately and independently process that event to delete their copies of the data. EventBridge is a managed event bus service designed for scalable, event-driven architectures, fitting the serverless microservices model. This approach supports immediate propagation of user-deletion events across microservices without polling or custom event filters on a queuIt avoids polling inefficiencies or SQS queue filtering, and SNS does not natively support event filtering based on detailed conditions making it less precise for this use casEventBridge rules allow precise event pattern matching and decoupling microservices, which is aligned with best practices for microservices and secure data handling.

answers.content: Configure the central user service to post a message on an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when the company deletes a user. Configure each microservice to create an event filter on the SQS queue and to delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
answers.explanation: SQS does not support event filters natively, so configuring microservices to create event filters on an SQS queue is not a supported design pattern and results in all services polling all messages.

questions.content: A company has a few AWS accounts for development and wants to move its production application to AWS. The company needs to enforce Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption at rest current production accounts and future production accounts only. The company needs a solution that includes built-in blueprints and guardrails. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

answers.content: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy AWS Config rules on production accounts.
answers.explanation: (StackSets + Config) is unnecessary since Control Tower provides managed guardrails.

answers.content: Create a new AWS Control Tower landing zone in an existing developer account. Create OUs for accounts. Add production and development accounts to production and development OUs, respectively.
answers.explanation: incorrect (landing zone cannot be created in a developer account).

answers.content: Create a new AWS Control Tower landing zone in the company's management account. Add production and development accounts to production and development OUs. respectively.
answers.explanation: Setting up a Control Tower landing zone in the management account establishes the foundation for a well-architected multi-account environment. By creating dedicated Organizational Units (OUs) for Production and Development, you create the necessary isolation to apply different policies (guardrails) to each environment.

answers.content: Invite existing accounts to join the organization in AWS Organizations. Create SCPs to ensure compliance.
answers.explanation: While Control Tower provides the governance framework, you must first bring your existing accounts into the AWS Organization structure. Creating Service Control Policies (SCPs) serves as a preventive layer of security. While the Control Tower guardrail (Step F) is excellent for detective compliance and reporting, an SCP can be used to explicitly deny the ability to create unencrypted volumes, thereby enforcing the encryption requirement proactively.
